-/// not usages. This keeps the index focused and compact.
-fn extract_symbols(path: &Path, content: &str) -> Vec<(Arc<str>, u32, bool)> {
-    let FileType::Code(lang) = detect_file_type(path) else {
-        return Vec::new();
-    };
-
-    let Some(ts_lang) = outline_language(lang) else {
-        return Vec::new();
-    };
-
-    let mut parser = tree_sitter::Parser::new();
-    if parser.set_language(&ts_lang).is_err() {
-        return Vec::new();
-    }
-
-    let Some(tree) = parser.parse(content, None) else {
-        return Vec::new();
-    };
-
-    let lines: Vec<&str> = content.lines().collect();
-    let mut symbols = Vec::new();
-
-    walk_definitions(tree.root_node(), &lines, &mut symbols, lang, 0);
-
-    symbols
-}
-
-/// Recursively walk tree-sitter AST nodes to find all definitions.
-///
-/// Unlike `search::symbol::walk_for_definitions` which searches for a specific name,
-/// this extracts ALL definition names for index building.
-/// Depth-limited to 3 levels (matching search behavior) to avoid descending
-/// into deeply nested anonymous blocks.
-fn walk_definitions(
-    node: tree_sitter::Node,
-    lines: &[&str],
-    symbols: &mut Vec<(Arc<str>, u32, bool)>,
-    lang: crate::types::Lang,
-    depth: usize,
-) {
-    if depth > 3 {
-        return;
-    }
-
-    let kind = node.kind();
-
-    if DEFINITION_KINDS.contains(&kind) {
-        if let Some(name) = extract_definition_name(node, lines) {
-            let line = node.start_position().row as u32 + 1;
-            symbols.push((Arc::from(name.as_str()), line, true));
-        }
-
-        // For impl blocks in Rust, also index the trait name and type name
-        // so lookups for "MyTrait" find `impl MyTrait for Foo`.
-        if kind == "impl_item" {
-            if let Some(trait_name) = crate::lang::treesitter::extract_impl_trait(node, lines) {
-                let line = node.start_position().row as u32 + 1;
-                symbols.push((Arc::from(trait_name.as_str()), line, true));
-            }
-            if let Some(type_name) = crate::lang::treesitter::extract_impl_type(node, lines) {
-                let line = node.start_position().row as u32 + 1;
-                symbols.push((Arc::from(type_name.as_str()), line, true));
-            }
-        }
-
-        // For classes implementing interfaces, index the interface names too
-        if kind == "class_declaration" || kind == "class_definition" {
-            let interfaces = crate::lang::treesitter::extract_implemented_interfaces(node, lines);
-            for iface in interfaces {
-                let line = node.start_position().row as u32 + 1;
-                symbols.push((Arc::from(iface.as_str()), line, true));
-            }
-        }
-    } else if lang == crate::types::Lang::Elixir
-        && crate::lang::treesitter::is_elixir_definition(node, lines)
-    {
-        // Elixir: all definitions are `call` nodes — handle separately
-        if let Some(name) = crate::lang::treesitter::extract_elixir_definition_name(node, lines) {
-            let line = node.start_position().row as u32 + 1;
-            symbols.push((Arc::from(name.as_str()), line, true));
-        }
-    }
-
-    // Recurse into children for nested definitions (impl blocks, class bodies, modules)
-    let mut cursor = node.walk();
-    for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
-        walk_definitions(child, lines, symbols, lang, depth + 1);
-    }
-}

-/// A probabilistic set membership data structure.
-///
-/// Supports `insert` and `contains`. `contains` may return false positives
-/// but never false negatives: if it returns `false`, the item is definitely
-/// absent.

-    bits: Vec<u64>,
-    num_hashes: u8,
-    num_bits: usize,

-impl BloomFilter {
-    /// Create a new Bloom filter sized for `expected_items` with the given
-    /// target false-positive rate.
-    ///
-    /// # Panics
-    ///
-    /// Panics if `expected_items` is 0 or `target_fpr` is not in (0, 1).
-    ///
-    /// # Examples
-    ///
-    /// ```
-    /// use tilth::index::bloom::BloomFilter;
-    ///
-    /// let bf = BloomFilter::new(100, 0.01);
-    /// assert!(!bf.contains("hello"));
-    /// ```

-    #[allow(clippy::cast_precision_loss)] // expected_items fits in f64 mantissa for practical sizes
-    pub fn new(expected_items: usize, target_fpr: f64) -> Self {
-        assert!(expected_items > 0, "expected_items must be > 0");
-        assert!(
-            target_fpr > 0.0 && target_fpr < 1.0,
-            "target_fpr must be in (0, 1)"

-        let n = expected_items as f64;
-        let ln2 = std::f64::consts::LN_2;

-        // Optimal number of bits: m = -(n * ln(p)) / (ln(2)^2)

+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Action extraction (pure, defensive)
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+//
+// CONFIDENCE LEVEL: medium. We know the `gemini` / `user` / `message_update`
+// envelope (used by parseTranscript + verified by fake-gemini.sh). Tool-call
+// records are *inferred* by analogy — handled if present, gracefully ignored
+// if not. Final-message and turn-count remain reliable.
+//
+// TODO(b3-gemini): verify function_call / function_response record shape
+// against a real Gemini CLI transcript and refine field extraction.
+
+function pushUnique(arr: string[], val: string): void {
+  if (!arr.includes(val)) arr.push(val);
+}
+
+function extractToolCallFromBlock(
+  block: JsonObj,
+  toolsUsed: Record<string, number>,
+  filesRead: string[],
+  filesEdited: string[],
+  filesWritten: string[],
+  bashCommands: string[],
+): void {
+  // Accept either { name, args } or { function_call: { name, args } }.
+  let toolName: string | undefined;
+  let argsField: JsonObj | null = null;
+
+  if (typeof block.name === 'string') {
+    toolName = block.name;
+    if (block.args !== undefined && typeof block.args === 'object')
+      argsField = block.args as JsonObj;
+    else if (block.input !== undefined && typeof block.input === 'object')
+      argsField = block.input as JsonObj;
+  } else if (block.function_call !== undefined && typeof block.function_call === 'object') {
+    const fc = block.function_call as JsonObj;
+    if (typeof fc.name === 'string') {
+      toolName = fc.name;
+      if (fc.args !== undefined && typeof fc.args === 'object') argsField = fc.args as JsonObj;
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (toolName === undefined) return;
+  toolsUsed[toolName] = (toolsUsed[toolName] ?? 0) + 1;
+
+  if (argsField === null) return;
+  const filePath = typeof argsField.file_path === 'string' ? argsField.file_path : undefined;
+  const command = typeof argsField.command === 'string' ? argsField.command : undefined;
+  if (toolName === 'Read' && filePath !== undefined) pushUnique(filesRead, filePath);
+  else if ((toolName === 'Edit' || toolName === 'MultiEdit') && filePath !== undefined)
+    pushUnique(filesEdited, filePath);
+  else if (toolName === 'Write' && filePath !== undefined) pushUnique(filesWritten, filePath);
+  else if (toolName === 'Bash' && command !== undefined) bashCommands.push(command);
+}
+
+export function extractGeminiActionsFromContent(content: string): ActionManifest {
+  const lines = content.split('\n').filter((l) => l.trim().length > 0);
+
+  const toolsUsed: Record<string, number> = {};
+  const filesRead: string[] = [];
+  const filesEdited: string[] = [];
+  const filesWritten: string[] = [];
+  const bashCommands: string[] = [];
+  const errors: string[] = [];
+  let turnCount = 0;
+
+  for (const line of lines) {
+    const parsed = parseLine(line);
+    if (parsed === null || typeof parsed !== 'object') continue;
+    const obj = parsed as JsonObj;
+
+    if (obj.type === 'gemini') {
+      turnCount++;
+      // gemini.content[] may contain function_call blocks alongside text blocks.
+      const contentArr = obj.content;
+      if (Array.isArray(contentArr)) {
+        for (const item of contentArr) {
+          if (item !== null && typeof item === 'object') {
+            extractToolCallFromBlock(
+              item as JsonObj,
+              toolsUsed,
+              filesRead,
+              filesEdited,
+              filesWritten,
+              bashCommands,
+            );
+          }
+        }
+      }
+      continue;
+    }
+
+    // Top-level function_call records (alternative shape).
+    if (obj.type === 'function_call') {
+      extractToolCallFromBlock(obj, toolsUsed, filesRead, filesEdited, filesWritten, bashCommands);
+    }
+
+    // Top-level function_response with error.
+    if (obj.type === 'function_response' && obj.is_error === true) {
+      const errMsg =
+        typeof obj.response === 'string'
+          ? obj.response
+          : typeof obj.error === 'string'
+            ? obj.error
+            : typeof obj.message === 'string'
+              ? obj.message
+              : '';
+      if (errMsg.length > 0) errors.push(errMsg);
+    }
+  }
+
+  return {
+    toolsUsed,
+    filesRead,
+    filesEdited,
+    filesWritten,
+    bashCommands,
+    errors,
+    finalMessage: parseGeminiTranscript(content),
+    turnCount,
+  };
+}
+
+// Pure: split Gemini transcript into completed turns. Each `gemini` record is
+// one turn (Gemini, unlike Claude/Codex, doesn't have a separate
+// "task_complete" event — the gemini record itself IS the boundary). The
+// turn's text is the concatenation of text blocks in that record's content
+// array. Pure — never throws; returns [] for empty/malformed input.
+export function extractGeminiTurnsFromContent(content: string): Turn[] {
+  const lines = content.split('\n').filter((l) => l.trim().length > 0);
+  const turns: Turn[] = [];
+  let idx = 0;
+  for (const line of lines) {
+    const parsed = parseLine(line);
+    if (parsed === null || typeof parsed !== 'object') continue;
+    const obj = parsed as JsonObj;
+    if (obj.type !== 'gemini') continue;
+
+    const contentArr = obj.content;
+    let text = '';
+    if (Array.isArray(contentArr)) {
+      const parts: string[] = [];
+      for (const item of contentArr) {
+        if (item !== null && typeof item === 'object') {
+          const block = item as JsonObj;
+          if (typeof block.text === 'string') parts.push(block.text);
+        }
+      }
+      text = parts.join('');
+    }
+    turns.push({ index: idx, text });
+    idx++;
+  }
+  return turns;
+}
+
 // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 // GeminiProvider
 // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+

+  },
 } as const;
 
 export const GeminiProvider: AgentProvider = geminiProvider;

-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { generate as generateOutput } from './generator.js';
-import type { Feature, Catalog, Step } from '../../core/types.js';
-
-/**
- * Test shim: unwrap the `AdapterOutput` envelope. The claude-tasks adapter
- * is single-file, so this returns `output.content`.
- */
-function generate(feature: Feature, catalog: Catalog): string {
-  const out = generateOutput(feature, catalog);
-  if (out.kind !== 'single-file') throw new Error('claude-tasks adapter must return single-file');
-  return out.content;
-}
-
-// ─── Fixtures ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-function makeCatalog(): Catalog {
-  return {
-    schema_version: '1',
-    project_id: 'test-project',
-    status: 'planned',
-    features: [],
-  };
-}
-
-function makeFeature(overrides: Partial<Feature> = {}): Feature {
-  return {
-    id: 'auth-login',
-    title: 'Auth Login',
-    status: 'planned',
-    ...overrides,
-  };
-}
-
-function makeStep(
-  id: string,
-  overrides: Partial<Step> = {},
-): Step {
-  return { id, title: `Step ${id}`, ...overrides };
-}
-
-// ─── Empty steps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('generate — empty steps', () => {
-  it('returns "no steps" message when no steps defined', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature();

-
-    expect(output).toContain('No implementation steps defined.');
-  });
-
-  it('includes feature title in no-steps output', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({ title: 'User Registration' });
-    const output = generate(feature, makeCatalog());
-
-    expect(output).toContain('# User Registration');
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── Header ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-describe('generate — header', () => {

-      title: 'Auth Login',
-      steps: [makeStep('i001')],
-    });
-
-    const output = generate(feature, makeCatalog());
-
-    expect(output).toContain('# Auth Login');
-  });
-
-  it('includes feature_id', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      steps: [makeStep('i001')],

-
-    const output = generate(feature, makeCatalog());
-
-    expect(output).toContain('feature: auth-login');

-  it('includes status', () => {

-      what: 'Allow users to log in',
-      steps: [makeStep('i001')],

-
-    const output = generate(feature, makeCatalog());
-
-    expect(output).toContain('goal: Allow users to log in');
-  });
-});

-
-describe('generate — step blocks', () => {

-    const output = generate(feature, makeCatalog());

-describe('generate — CHECKPOINT block', () => {

-// ─── listen() ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-/** Build an ExecutionHandle from a simple taskId → stepId map. */
-function makeHandle(pairs: Array<[taskId: string, stepId: string]>): ExecutionHandle {
-  const taskIds = pairs.map(([t]) => t);
-  const stepMap = new Map(pairs);
-  return { taskIds, stepMap };
-}
-
-/** Collect callback invocations into an array. */
-function collectUpdates(): { updates: Array<{ step_id: string; status: string }>; cb: StatusCallback } {
-  const updates: Array<{ step_id: string; status: string }> = [];
-  const cb: StatusCallback = (u) => updates.push(u);
-  return { updates, cb };
-}
-
-describe('listen() — single task completes immediately', () => {
-  it('resolves with step_id and final_status=done', async () => {
-    const handle = makeHandle([['task-1', 'step-1']]);
-    const { cb } = collectUpdates();
-
-    const results = await listen(handle, cb, {
-      pollIntervalMs: 0,
-      fetchStatus: async () => 'completed',
-    });
-
-    expect(results).toHaveLength(1);
-    expect(results[0]!.step_id).toBe('step-1');
-    expect(results[0]!.final_status).toBe('done');
-  });
-
-  it('fires the callback with in-progress then done when status transitions', async () => {
-    const handle = makeHandle([['task-1', 'step-1']]);
-    const { updates, cb } = collectUpdates();
-
-    let call = 0;
-    const fetchStatus = async () => {
-      call++;
-      return call === 1 ? 'in_progress' : 'completed';
-    };
-
-    await listen(handle, cb, { pollIntervalMs: 0, fetchStatus });
-
-    expect(updates).toHaveLength(2);
-    expect(updates[0]).toEqual({ step_id: 'step-1', status: 'in-progress' });
-    expect(updates[1]).toEqual({ step_id: 'step-1', status: 'done' });
-  });
-});
-
-describe('listen() — idempotent on no status change', () => {
-  it('does not fire callback when status stays the same across ticks', async () => {
-    const handle = makeHandle([['task-1', 'step-1']]);
-    const { updates, cb } = collectUpdates();
-
-    let call = 0;
-    const fetchStatus = async () => {
-      call++;
-      // First two ticks return pending, third tick resolves with completed
-      return call < 3 ? 'pending' : 'completed';
-    };
-
-    await listen(handle, cb, { pollIntervalMs: 0, fetchStatus });
-
-    // Only two callback fires: pending→pending (no-op) then pending→completed
-    // The transition from initial 'pending' (set before first tick) to first fetch 'pending' is no-op
-    // Then pending → completed fires once
-    const statuses = updates.map((u) => u.status);
-    expect(statuses).not.toContain('pending'); // pending→pending never fires
-    expect(statuses).toContain('done');
-    expect(statuses.filter((s) => s === 'done')).toHaveLength(1);
-  });
-});
-
-describe('listen() — task fails', () => {

-
-    const results = await listen(handle, cb, {

-    expect(results[0]!.final_status).toBe('failed');

-
-  it('resolves with final_status=skipped when task is cancelled', async () => {
-    const handle = makeHandle([['task-1', 'step-1']]);
-    const { cb } = collectUpdates();
-
-    const results = await listen(handle, cb, {
-      pollIntervalMs: 0,

-    });
-
-    expect(results[0]!.final_status).toBe('skipped');
-  });
-});
-
-describe('listen() — multi-step task (multiple tasks in one handle)', () => {
-  it('resolves once all tasks have reached a terminal state', async () => {
-    const handle = makeHandle([
-      ['task-A', 'step-A'],
-      ['task-B', 'step-B'],
-      ['task-C', 'step-C'],
-    ]);
-    const { updates, cb } = collectUpdates();
-
-    // task-A: completes on first tick
-    // task-B: fails on first tick
-    // task-C: cancelled on first tick
-    const statuses: Record<string, string> = {
-      'task-A': 'completed',
-      'task-B': 'failed',
-      'task-C': 'cancelled',
-    };
-
-    const results = await listen(handle, cb, {
-      pollIntervalMs: 0,
-      fetchStatus: async (id) => statuses[id]!,
-    });
-
-    expect(results).toHaveLength(3);
-    const byStepId = Object.fromEntries(results.map((r) => [r.step_id, r.final_status]));
-    expect(byStepId['step-A']).toBe('done');
-    expect(byStepId['step-B']).toBe('failed');
-    expect(byStepId['step-C']).toBe('skipped');
-    // Each task fired exactly one callback (pending → terminal)
-    expect(updates).toHaveLength(3);
-  });
-
-  it('waits for the slower task before resolving', async () => {
-    const handle = makeHandle([
-      ['task-fast', 'step-fast'],
-      ['task-slow', 'step-slow'],
-    ]);
-    const { cb } = collectUpdates();
-
-    const fastCalls: Record<string, number> = { 'task-fast': 0, 'task-slow': 0 };
-
-    const fetchStatus = async (id: string) => {
-      fastCalls[id] = (fastCalls[id] ?? 0) + 1;
-      if (id === 'task-fast') return 'completed'; // terminal on tick 1
-      return fastCalls[id]! < 3 ? 'in_progress' : 'completed'; // terminal on tick 3
-    };
-
-    const results = await listen(handle, cb, { pollIntervalMs: 0, fetchStatus });
-
-    expect(results).toHaveLength(2);
-    const stepSlow = results.find((r) => r.step_id === 'step-slow');
-    expect(stepSlow?.final_status).toBe('done');
-    // task-slow must have been polled at least 3 times
-    expect(fastCalls['task-slow']!).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
-  });
-});
-
-describe('listen() — partial completion (some done, some not yet)', () => {
-  it('callbacks reflect which tasks have transitioned so far', async () => {
-    const handle = makeHandle([
-      ['task-1', 'step-1'],
-      ['task-2', 'step-2'],

-    const { updates, cb } = collectUpdates();
-
-    const tick1Calls: Record<string, number> = { 'task-1': 0, 'task-2': 0 };
-    const fetchStatus = async (id: string) => {
-      tick1Calls[id] = (tick1Calls[id] ?? 0) + 1;
-      // task-1 completes on tick 1; task-2 completes on tick 2
-      if (id === 'task-1') return 'completed';
-      return tick1Calls[id]! < 2 ? 'in_progress' : 'completed';
-    };
-
-    await listen(handle, cb, { pollIntervalMs: 0, fetchStatus });
-
-    const step1Updates = updates.filter((u) => u.step_id === 'step-1');
-    const step2Updates = updates.filter((u) => u.step_id === 'step-2');
-
-    expect(step1Updates.map((u) => u.status)).toContain('done');
-    expect(step2Updates.map((u) => u.status)).toContain('done');
-  });
-});

-describe('listen() — fetch errors / maxRetries', () => {
-  it('treats a task as failed after maxRetries consecutive errors', async () => {
-    const handle = makeHandle([['task-err', 'step-err']]);
-    const { updates, cb } = collectUpdates();
-
-    let errCount = 0;
-    const fetchStatus = async () => {
-      errCount++;
-      throw new Error(`simulated network error ${errCount}`);

-
-    const results = await listen(handle, cb, {
-      pollIntervalMs: 0,
-      maxRetries: 3,
-      fetchStatus,
-    });
-
-    expect(errCount).toBe(3); // hit exactly maxRetries before giving up
-    expect(results[0]!.final_status).toBe('failed');
-  });
-
-  it('recovers from transient errors (error count resets on success)', async () => {
-    const handle = makeHandle([['task-1', 'step-1']]);
-    const { cb } = collectUpdates();
-
-    let callCount = 0;
-    const fetchStatus = async () => {
-      callCount++;
-      if (callCount === 1) throw new Error('transient');
-      // second call succeeds and resolves terminal
-      return 'completed';
-    };
-
-    const results = await listen(handle, cb, {
-      pollIntervalMs: 0,
-      maxRetries: 5,
-      fetchStatus,
-    });
-
-    expect(results[0]!.final_status).toBe('done');
-  });
-
-  it('does not fire callback for tasks with no stepMap entry', async () => {

-      taskIds: ['unmapped-task'],
-      stepMap: new Map(),
-    };
-    const { cb } = collectUpdates();

-    const results = await listen(handle, cb, {

-      fetchStatus: async () => 'completed',
-    });
-
-    expect(results[0]!.step_id).toBe('unmapped-task');
-    expect(results[0]!.final_status).toBe('done');
-  });
-});
-
-describe('listen() — default fetchStatus (always pending)', () => {
-  it('uses the default fetchStatus that always returns pending when none provided', async () => {

-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { generate as generateOutput } from './generator.js';
-import type { Feature, Step, Catalog } from '../../core/types.js';
-
-/**
- * Test shim: the github-issues adapter is `multi-file` — one issue per step.
- * Every emitted issue carries the full feature-level header (goal, context
- * table, solves, dependencies, checks) plus its own step. These feature-context
- * assertions therefore hold against any issue, so the shim returns the FIRST
- * issue's JSON payload string.
- *
- * Fixtures that declare no steps would emit zero issues; to keep the
- * feature-context assertions meaningful, the shim injects a single placeholder
- * step when the fixture omits one. Stepless behaviour itself is asserted
- * directly against `generateOutput` in the "one issue per step" suite.
- */
-function generate(feature: Feature, catalog?: Catalog): string {
-  const withStep: Feature =
-    (feature.steps?.length ?? 0) > 0
-      ? feature
-      : { ...feature, steps: [{ id: '__probe', title: 'probe step' }] };
-  const out = generateOutput(withStep, catalog);
-  if (out.kind !== 'multi-file') throw new Error('github-issues adapter must return multi-file');
-  if (out.files.length === 0) throw new Error('expected at least one issue file');
-  return out.files[0]!.content;
-}
-
-// ─── Fixtures ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-function makeFeature(overrides: Partial<Feature> = {}): Feature {
-  return {
-    id: 'auth-login',
-    title: 'Auth Login',
-    status: 'planned',
-    ...overrides,
-  };
-}
-
-function makeStep(
-  id: string,
-  overrides: Partial<Step> = {},
-): Step {
-  return { id, title: `Step ${id}`, ...overrides };
-}
-
-function makeCatalog(overrides: Partial<Catalog> = {}): Catalog {
-  return {
-    project_id: 'test',
-    status: 'planned',
-    features: [],
-    ...overrides,
-  };
-}
-
-function parsePayload(output: string) {
-  return JSON.parse(output) as {
-    title: string;
-    body: string;
-    labels: string[];
-    assignees: string[];
-  };
-}
-

-// ─── Integration: real `make -n` invocation (c001, c002, c005) ────────────────
-// Writes a generated Makefile to a temp directory and runs make -n to confirm:
-//   c001: make -n exits 0 (parseable Makefile)
-//   c002: make -n output lists steps in dependency order
-//   c005: make -j2 -n exits 0; targets are .done sentinels (not PHONY)
-
-/**
- * Write a full MakefileOutput (Makefile + all prompt stubs) to a temp dir.
- * GNU Make 3.81 (macOS bundled) requires prerequisite files to exist even for
- * -n dry-runs when they are not themselves targets. We write empty stubs for
- * every prompt file so `make -n` resolves prerequisites without executing recipes.
- * Caller must rm dir in finally.
- */
-function writeMakefileToTmpDir(feature: Feature): string {
-  const out = buildOutput(feature);
-  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'tend-makefile-test-'));
-  mkdirSync(join(dir, 'prompts'), { recursive: true });
-  writeFileSync(join(dir, 'Makefile'), out.makefile, 'utf8');
-  // Write empty stubs for all prompt files — make -n needs them to exist
-  for (const path of Object.keys(out.prompts)) {
-    writeFileSync(join(dir, path), '', 'utf8');
-  }
-  return dir;
-}
-
-/** Run `make` with given args in a dir. Returns { status, stdout, stderr }. */
-function runMake(dir: string, args: string[]): { status: number; stdout: string; stderr: string } {
-  try {
-    const stdout = execFileSync('make', args, {
-      cwd: dir,
-      encoding: 'utf8',
-      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
-    });
-    return { status: 0, stdout, stderr: '' };
-  } catch (err: unknown) {
-    const e = err as { status?: number; stdout?: string; stderr?: string };
-    return {
-      status: e.status ?? 1,
-      stdout: e.stdout ?? '',
-      stderr: e.stderr ?? '',
-    };
-  }
-}
-
-describe('integration — make -n dry-run (c001, c002, c005)', () => {
-  it('c001: make -n exits 0 against a generated Makefile (parseable)', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'test-feat',
-      steps: [makeStep('i001'), makeStep('i002'), makeStep('i003')],
-    });
-    const dir = writeMakefileToTmpDir(feature);
-    try {
-      const result = runMake(dir, ['-n', 'all']);
-      expect(result.status).toBe(0);
-    } finally {
-      rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('c002: make -n output shows steps in dependency order (i001 before i002 before i003)', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'dep-feat',
-      steps: [
-        makeStep('i001'),
-        makeStep('i002', { dependencies: ['i001'] }),
-        makeStep('i003', { dependencies: ['i002'] }),
-      ],
-    });
-    const dir = writeMakefileToTmpDir(feature);
-    try {
-      const result = runMake(dir, ['-n', 'all']);
-      expect(result.status).toBe(0);
-      // make -n lists recipe lines in execution order; prompts/<id> appear in order
-      const stdout = result.stdout;
-      const i001Pos = stdout.indexOf('i001');
-      const i002Pos = stdout.indexOf('i002');
-      const i003Pos = stdout.indexOf('i003');
-      expect(i001Pos).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
-      expect(i002Pos).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
-      expect(i003Pos).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
-      expect(i001Pos).toBeLessThan(i002Pos);
-      expect(i002Pos).toBeLessThan(i003Pos);
-    } finally {
-      rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('c005: make -j2 -n exits 0; each step has a .done sentinel target (not purely phony)', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'par-feat',
-      steps: [makeStep('i001'), makeStep('i002'), makeStep('i003')],
-    });
-    const dir = writeMakefileToTmpDir(feature);
-    const { makefile } = buildOutput(feature);
-    try {
-      const result = runMake(dir, ['-j2', '-n', 'all']);
-      expect(result.status).toBe(0);
-      // Confirm sentinel files are named *.done, not .PHONY entries for the steps
-      expect(makefile).toMatch(/^i001\.done\s*:/m);
-      expect(makefile).toMatch(/^i002\.done\s*:/m);
-      expect(makefile).toMatch(/^i003\.done\s*:/m);
-      // .PHONY should NOT contain the step targets (they are real files, not phony)
-      const phonyLine = makefile.split('\n').find((l) => l.startsWith('.PHONY'));
-      if (phonyLine) {
-        expect(phonyLine).not.toContain('i001.done');
-        expect(phonyLine).not.toContain('i002.done');
-        expect(phonyLine).not.toContain('i003.done');
-      }
-    } finally {
-      rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('c002 + c005: make -j2 -n with test-first steps exits 0; RED before IMPL in output', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'tf-feat',
-      checks: [makeCheck('c001', { verification_recipe: 'echo verify-c001' })],
-      steps: [
-        makeStep('i001'),
-        makeStep('i002', { traces_to: ['c001'], dependencies: ['i001'] }),
-      ],
-    });
-    const dir = writeMakefileToTmpDir(feature);
-    try {
-      const result = runMake(dir, ['-j2', '-n', 'all']);
-      expect(result.status).toBe(0);
-      const stdout = result.stdout;
-      // RED target (i002-test) must precede IMPL target (i002-impl) in dry-run output
-      const redPos = stdout.indexOf('i002-test');
-      const implPos = stdout.indexOf('i002-impl');
-      expect(redPos).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
-      expect(implPos).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
-      expect(redPos).toBeLessThan(implPos);
-    } finally {
-      rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
-    }
-  });
-});

-/**
- * Cross-repo guard: two distinct, separately-labeled guarantees about the Plan
- * tend's umbel adapter generates. They are NOT the same thing, and conflating
- * them is the drift the pleach maintainer flagged in jahala/pleach#9:
- *
- *  (A) pleach's LOAD invariants — `assertConductorValid`. The five checks
- *      pleach's validatePlan enforces; a plan failing any is rejected at load
- *      (validate throws → exit 2). Mirrored from pleach/src/core/validate.ts —
- *      re-verify on every @agent-contract/plan contract bump. The five:
- *        1. ≥1 node                              (validate.ts:9-11)
- *        2. unique node ids                      (validate.ts:14-24)
- *        3. every `needs` resolves to a node id  (validate.ts:29-35)
- *        4. audit.provider ≠ worker.provider     (validate.ts:38-47; worker
- *           defaults to 'claude', validate.ts:4) — the model-diversity rule
- *        5. no dependency cycle (Kahn toposort)  (validate.ts:54-92)
- *
- *  (B) tend's AUDIT-ROUTING convention — `assertAuditRoutesToFeature`. The audit
- *      gate must sit on the node whose id is the BARE feature id. This is *not* a
- *      pleach load invariant — pleach will happily LOAD a dotted-id node that
- *      carries `accept.audit` (confirmed by the maintainer, jahala/pleach#9). But
- *      if tend *emits* one, pleach's ingester keys the AuditResult write off
- *      `verdict.node`, so the verdict lands on a phantom `<feature>.<step>`
- *      instead of the real feature. It's a tend GENERATION rule, enforced here on
- *      the emitting side — the A2 fix.
- *
- * The true cross-repo proof is the e2e: a real feature driven through pleach,
- * demonstrated green in jahala/pleach#9 (real claude builders → real codex audit
- * → tend verified-close, both negative controls discriminating). This test is the
- * unit-speed drift guard — it catches divergence without importing pleach (no
- * hard cross-repo dependency).
- *
- * When pleach extracts its invariants into a vendorable predicate module
- * (jahala/pleach#9), the (A) mirror here is replaced by a vendored copy of
- * pleach's actual predicates + a drift test; (B) stays tend-side regardless.
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { generatePlan, AUDIT_PROVIDER } from './generator.js';
-import type { Feature, Step } from '../../core/types.js';
-import type { Plan } from '../../core/bridge/plan.js';
-
-// ─── (A) Mirror of pleach's validatePlan load invariants ─────────────────────
-// Source: pleach/src/core/validate.ts. DO NOT vendor the real validatePlan here —
-// we assert the invariants, not the code. Re-verify on every contract bump.
-
-/** The default worker provider as defined in pleach/src/core/validate.ts:4. */
-const DEFAULT_WORKER_PROVIDER = 'claude';
-
-class PlanInvalidError extends Error {
-  constructor(public readonly reasons: string[]) {
-    super(`Plan invalid: ${reasons.join('; ')}`);
-    this.name = 'PlanInvalidError';
-  }
-}
-
-function assertConductorValid(plan: Plan): { order: string[] } {
-  const reasons: string[] = [];
-
-  // Invariant 1: at least one node (validate.ts:9-11)
-  if (plan.nodes.length === 0) {
-    throw new PlanInvalidError(['plan has no nodes']);
-  }
-
-  // Invariant 2: no duplicate node ids (validate.ts:14-24)
-  const seen = new Set<string>();
-  const duplicates = new Set<string>();
-  for (const node of plan.nodes) {
-    if (seen.has(node.id)) duplicates.add(node.id);
-    seen.add(node.id);
-  }
-  for (const id of duplicates) {
-    reasons.push(`duplicate node id: '${id}'`);
-  }
-
-  const idSet = new Set(plan.nodes.map((n) => n.id));
-
-  // Invariant 3: every needs reference must resolve to a node id (validate.ts:29-35)
-  for (const node of plan.nodes) {
-    for (const dep of node.needs) {
-      if (!idSet.has(dep)) {
-        reasons.push(`node '${node.id}' needs unknown id: '${dep}'`);
-      }
-    }
-  }
-
-  // Invariant 4: model diversity — audit provider must differ from worker provider
-  // (validate.ts:38-47). DEFAULT_WORKER_PROVIDER is 'claude' (validate.ts:4).
-  for (const node of plan.nodes) {
-    if (node.accept.audit) {
-      const workerProvider = node.worker.provider ?? DEFAULT_WORKER_PROVIDER;
-      if (node.accept.audit.provider === workerProvider) {
-        reasons.push(
-          `node '${node.id}': audit provider '${node.accept.audit.provider}' must differ from worker provider (model diversity rule)`,
-        );
-      }
-    }
-  }
-
-  if (reasons.length > 0) {
-    throw new PlanInvalidError(reasons);
-  }
-
-  // Invariant 5: no dependency cycle — Kahn's toposort (validate.ts:54-92)
-  const inDegree = new Map<string, number>();
-  const adjacency = new Map<string, string[]>();
-
-  for (const node of plan.nodes) {
-    if (!inDegree.has(node.id)) inDegree.set(node.id, 0);
-    if (!adjacency.has(node.id)) adjacency.set(node.id, []);
-  }
-
-  for (const node of plan.nodes) {
-    for (const dep of node.needs) {
-      const successors = adjacency.get(dep) ?? [];
-      successors.push(node.id);
-      adjacency.set(dep, successors);
-      inDegree.set(node.id, (inDegree.get(node.id) ?? 0) + 1);
-    }
-  }
-
-  const queue: string[] = [];
-  for (const [id, deg] of inDegree) {
-    if (deg === 0) queue.push(id);
-  }
-
-  const order: string[] = [];
-  while (queue.length > 0) {
-    const id = queue.shift() as string;
-    order.push(id);
-    for (const successor of adjacency.get(id) ?? []) {
-      const newDeg = (inDegree.get(successor) ?? 0) - 1;
-      inDegree.set(successor, newDeg);
-      if (newDeg === 0) queue.push(successor);
-    }
-  }
-
-  if (order.length !== plan.nodes.length) {
-    throw new PlanInvalidError(['dependency cycle detected in plan nodes']);
-  }
-
-  return { order };
-}
-
-// ─── (B) tend's audit-routing generation convention ──────────────────────────
-//
-// NOT a pleach load invariant (jahala/pleach#9): pleach won't reject a dotted-id
-// node carrying accept.audit. But tend must not emit one — the ingester keys the
-// AuditResult write off `verdict.node`, so the audit must ride the bare feature
-// id or the verdict lands on a phantom `<feature>.<step>`. The A2 fix guards this
-// on the emitting (generation) side.
-
-/** Every node that carries `accept.audit` must have id === the bare feature id. */
-function assertAuditRoutesToFeature(plan: Plan, featureId: string): void {
-  for (const node of plan.nodes) {
-    if (node.accept.audit !== undefined) {
-      expect(node.id).toBe(featureId);
-    }
-  }
-}
-
-// ─── Fixtures ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-function makeFeature(overrides: Partial<Feature> = {}): Feature {
-  return {
-    id: 'demo-feat',
-    title: 'Demo Feature',
-    status: 'planned',
-    ...overrides,
-  };
-}
-
-function makeStep(id: string, overrides: Partial<Step> = {}): Step {
-  return { id, title: `Step ${id}`, ...overrides };
-}
-
-// ─── (A) Positive: generatePlan output satisfies pleach's load invariants ─────
-
-describe("cross-repo: generatePlan output satisfies pleach's load invariants", () => {
-  it('0 steps + 1 check: single collapsed node passes all load invariants', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'zero-steps',
-      what: 'do a thing',
-      checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'works', validates: 'what' }],
-    });
-    expect(() => assertConductorValid(generatePlan(feature))).not.toThrow();
-  });
-
-  it('1 step + 1 check: collapsed node passes all load invariants', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'one-step',
-      what: 'do one thing',
-      checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'works', validates: 'what' }],
-      steps: [
-        makeStep('s1', {
-          step_type: 'agent',
-          description: 'Test: assert X.\n\nImplement: build X.',
-          traces_to: ['c1'],
-        }),
-      ],
-    });
-    const plan = generatePlan(feature);
-    expect(() => assertConductorValid(plan)).not.toThrow();
-    // 1-step collapses: only 1 node, id = bare feature id (not 'one-step.s1')
-    expect(plan.nodes).toHaveLength(1);
-    expect(plan.nodes[0]!.id).toBe('one-step');
-  });
-
-  it('N=2 steps with intra-feature dependency: step nodes + integration node pass all load invariants', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'multi-step',
-      what: 'ship multi-step capability',
-      checks: [
-        { id: 'c1', description: 'unit works', validates: 'what' },
-        { id: 'c2', description: 'build passes', validates: 'how' },
-      ],
-      steps: [
-        makeStep('s1', {
-          step_type: 'agent',
-          description: 'Test: src/x.test.ts asserts X.\nRun: npx vitest run src/x.test.ts.\n\nImplement: write X.',
-          traces_to: ['c1'],
-          dependencies: [],
-        }),
-        makeStep('s2', {
-          step_type: 'command',
-          description: 'npm run build',
-          traces_to: ['c2'],
-          dependencies: ['s1'], // s2 depends on s1 — intra-feature ordering edge
-        }),
-      ],
-    });
-    const plan = generatePlan(feature);
-    expect(() => assertConductorValid(plan)).not.toThrow();
-
-    // ≥2 steps: 2 step nodes + 1 integration node = 3 total
-    expect(plan.nodes).toHaveLength(3);
-    expect(plan.nodes.slice(0, 2).map((n) => n.id)).toEqual(['multi-step.s1', 'multi-step.s2']);
-    const integrationNode = plan.nodes[2]!;
-    expect(integrationNode.id).toBe('multi-step');
-    expect(integrationNode.needs).toContain('multi-step.s1');
-    expect(integrationNode.needs).toContain('multi-step.s2');
-
-    // s2 needs s1 → composite id in needs (intra-plan ordering, resolves to a node)
-    const s2Node = plan.nodes.find((n) => n.id === 'multi-step.s2')!;
-    expect(s2Node.needs).toContain('multi-step.s1');
-  });
-
-  it('feature with smoke.cmd: smoke propagates to ALL nodes; plan still passes invariants', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'smoky',
-      what: 'verified capability',
-      smoke: { cmd: 'npx vitest run tests/e2e.test.ts' },
-      checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'e2e passes', validates: 'what' }],
-      steps: [
-        makeStep('s1', { step_type: 'agent', description: 'Test: X.\n\nImplement: Y.', traces_to: ['c1'] }),
-        makeStep('s2', { step_type: 'command', description: 'npm run build', dependencies: ['s1'] }),
-      ],
-    });
-    const plan = generatePlan(feature);
-    expect(() => assertConductorValid(plan)).not.toThrow();
-    // Smoke propagates to all nodes (a tend generation behavior — harmless to pleach)
-    for (const node of plan.nodes) {
-      expect(node.accept.smoke).toBe('npx vitest run tests/e2e.test.ts');
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('Invariant 4 — model diversity: audit provider differs from the default worker provider', () => {
-    // The conductor's DEFAULT_WORKER_PROVIDER is 'claude'; AUDIT_PROVIDER must differ.
-    // If tend changed AUDIT_PROVIDER to 'claude', this test (and pleach) would reject.
-    expect(AUDIT_PROVIDER).not.toBe(DEFAULT_WORKER_PROVIDER);
-
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'diversity-check',
-      what: 'audit diversity',
-      checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'works', validates: 'what' }],
-    });
-    const plan = generatePlan(feature);
-    const auditNode = plan.nodes.find((n) => n.accept.audit !== undefined);
-    expect(auditNode).toBeDefined();
-    const workerProvider = auditNode!.worker.provider ?? DEFAULT_WORKER_PROVIDER;
-    expect(auditNode!.accept.audit!.provider).not.toBe(workerProvider);
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── (B) Positive: generatePlan obeys tend's audit-routing convention ─────────
-
-describe('tend convention: the audit gate routes to the bare feature id (NOT a pleach load invariant)', () => {
-  it('0 steps: the sole audit node is the bare feature id', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'zero-steps',
-      what: 'do a thing',
-      checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'works', validates: 'what' }],
-    });
-    const plan = generatePlan(feature);
-    assertAuditRoutesToFeature(plan, 'zero-steps');
-    const auditNode = plan.nodes.find((n) => n.accept.audit !== undefined);
-    expect(auditNode).toBeDefined();
-    expect(auditNode!.id).toBe('zero-steps');
-  });
-
-  it('1 step: audit lives on the bare-feature-id collapsed node, not <feature>.s1', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'one-step',
-      what: 'do one thing',
-      checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'works', validates: 'what' }],
-      steps: [makeStep('s1', { step_type: 'agent', description: 'Test: X.\n\nImplement: Y.', traces_to: ['c1'] })],
-    });
-    const plan = generatePlan(feature);
-    expect(plan.nodes[0]!.accept.audit?.command).toBe('tend audit one-step');
-    assertAuditRoutesToFeature(plan, 'one-step');
-  });
-
-  it('N=2 steps: audit lives ONLY on the bare-feature-id integration node; step nodes are audit-free', () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature({
-      id: 'multi-step',
-      what: 'ship multi-step capability',
-      checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'unit works', validates: 'what' }],
-      steps: [
-        makeStep('s1', { step_type: 'agent', description: 'Test: X.\n\nImplement: Y.', traces_to: ['c1'] }),
-        makeStep('s2', { step_type: 'command', description: 'npm run build', dependencies: ['s1'] }),
-      ],
-    });
-    const plan = generatePlan(feature);
-    for (const stepNode of plan.nodes.slice(0, 2)) {
-      expect(stepNode.accept.audit).toBeUndefined();
-    }
-    expect(plan.nodes[2]!.accept.audit?.command).toBe('tend audit multi-step');
-    assertAuditRoutesToFeature(plan, 'multi-step');
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── (A) Negative: assertConductorValid discriminates (catches real drift) ────
-
-describe("cross-repo: assertConductorValid rejects plans that violate pleach's load invariants", () => {
-  it('NEGATIVE: dangling needs (unknown node id) → throws PlanInvalidError', () => {
-    // A node whose `needs` points at an id no node carries. pleach rejects this at
-    // load (validate.ts:29-35). We hand-craft it because generatePlan never emits it.
-    const badPlan: Plan = {
-      goal: 'catch drift',
-      source: 'docs/tend/features/bad-feat.tend.html',
-      nodes: [
-        {
-          id: 'bad-feat.s1',
-          worker: {},
-          work: { prompt: 'do the thing' },
-          needs: ['bad-feat.nonexistent'], // ← dangling: no node with this id exists
-          accept: {},
-          policy: { maxAttempts: 2, onDead: 'resume', reauditWhen: ['compacted'] },
-          closes: [],
-        },
-      ],
-    };
-    expect(() => assertConductorValid(badPlan)).toThrowError(PlanInvalidError);
-    expect(() => assertConductorValid(badPlan)).toThrowError(/needs unknown id: 'bad-feat.nonexistent'/);
-  });
-
-  it('NEGATIVE: model diversity violated (audit provider == worker provider) → throws', () => {
-    // audit + worker both 'claude' — emitted if tend set AUDIT_PROVIDER to 'claude'
-    // without changing the worker default. pleach rejects this (validate.ts:38-47).
-    const badPlan: Plan = {
-      goal: 'diversity violation',
-      source: 'docs/tend/features/bad-feat.tend.html',
-      nodes: [
-        {
-          id: 'bad-feat',
-          worker: { provider: undefined }, // defaults to 'claude' in pleach
-          work: { prompt: 'do it' },
-          needs: [],
-          accept: {
-            audit: {
-              command: 'tend audit bad-feat',
-              provider: 'claude', // ← same as DEFAULT_WORKER_PROVIDER → diversity violation
-            },
-          },
-          policy: { maxAttempts: 2, onDead: 'resume', reauditWhen: ['compacted'] },
-          closes: [],
-        },
-      ],
-    };
-    expect(() => assertConductorValid(badPlan)).toThrowError(PlanInvalidError);
-    expect(() => assertConductorValid(badPlan)).toThrowError(/model diversity rule/);
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── (B) Negative: the audit-routing convention discriminates ─────────────────
-
-describe('tend convention: assertAuditRoutesToFeature catches a mis-routed audit', () => {
-  it('NEGATIVE: audit on a step-id-keyed node → assertion fails (would mis-write the verdict)', () => {
-    // The pre-A2 shape: audit on a `<feature>.<step>` node. pleach would LOAD this
-    // fine — it is NOT a validatePlan error — but its ingester would write the
-    // verdict to 'bad-feat.s1' (a phantom), so the real feature never updates. That
-    // silent mis-write is exactly why tend guards the convention on the emitting side.
-    const badPlan: Plan = {
-      goal: 'mis-routed audit',
-      source: 'docs/tend/features/bad-feat.tend.html',
-      nodes: [
-        {
-          id: 'bad-feat.s1', // ← composite id carrying the audit: the A2 regression
-          worker: {},
-          work: { prompt: 'do the thing' },
-          needs: [],
-          accept: { audit: { command: 'tend audit bad-feat', provider: AUDIT_PROVIDER } },
-          policy: { maxAttempts: 2, onDead: 'resume', reauditWhen: ['compacted'] },
-          closes: [],
-        },
-      ],
-    };
-    // pleach's load invariants PASS — it is a structurally valid plan...
-    expect(() => assertConductorValid(badPlan)).not.toThrow();
-    // ...but tend's audit-routing convention catches the mis-route.
-    expect(() => assertAuditRoutesToFeature(badPlan, 'bad-feat')).toThrow();
-  });
-});

-// ─── generate: assemble Plan (c1 / c4 / step i003) ─────────────────────────────
-//
-// v1.1.1 node shape (A2 fix):
-//   ≥2 steps → N step nodes (id = <feature>.<step>) + 1 integration node (id = bare feature id)
-//   1 step   → 1 node (id = bare feature id, carries both step work and accept.audit)
-//   0 steps  → 1 node (id = bare feature id, carries accept.audit)
-//

-/**
- * `src/bin/tend.ts` — the argv dispatcher — verified END-TO-END against the
- * BUILT dist binary plus structural guards on the source.
- *
- * This file is the integration evidence for the `cli` parent feature's
- * surface-level checks. It is split into four describe blocks, one per check it
- * proves, so an auditor can map test → check directly:
- *
- *   - c001              — `tend --help` lists every project-level subcommand
- *                          (spawns the real binary, exercises the switch,
- *                          asserts every name in SUBCOMMANDS).
- *   - c-fast-cold-start — no framework tax: package.json carries no commander /
- *                          yargs, the dispatcher uses dynamic `await import(...)`,
- *                          and a warm `node dist/bin/tend.js --help` dispatches
- *                          well under the budget (structural proof + a non-flaky
- *                          `node` measurement — never npx, whose npm-resolution
- *                          overhead is not the CLI's design).
- *   - c-non-agentic-only — no subcommand mutates FEATURE state from the CLI: the
- *                          dispatcher and every src/cli source file are free of
- *                          feature-write symbols, agentic SDKs, and interactive
- *                          prompts. (Project-level oo-meta/oo-data splices in
- *                          init + rename are config writes, not feature edits —
- *                          asserted explicitly as the one allowed structural
- *                          write.)
- *   - c-shared-render   — the ANSI color table is declared once, in render.ts;
- *                          no src/cli source file re-declares raw escape codes.
- *
- * The spawn tests require `npm run build` first — they exercise dist/, not src/.
- * A missing build fails loudly (a skipped test is not green) rather than passing
- * silently. Source-guard tests read src/ directly and need no build.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
-import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, mkdtempSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
-import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
-
-const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);
-const __dirname = dirname(__filename);
-const REPO_ROOT = join(__dirname, '..', '..');
-const CLI = join(REPO_ROOT, 'dist', 'bin', 'tend.js');
-const BIN_SRC = join(__dirname, 'tend.ts');
-const CLI_DIR = join(REPO_ROOT, 'src', 'cli');
-
-/**
- * The project-level subcommands the `cli` feature claims as its surface, each of
- * which must be listed in USAGE and routed by a lazy-import `case` arm.
- * `execute` was added when the cli-execute subpage was built.
- * `doctor`, `audit`, `preview-thumbnail`, `preview-cards`, `negctrl` were
- * added as CLI subcommands for project-level helpers (per PR #28/#29).
- */
-const SUBCOMMANDS = [
-  'init',
-  'rename',
-  'rename-feature',
-  'serve',
-  'ui',
-  'validate',
-  'aggregate',
-  'sync',
-  'execute',
-  'next',
-  'doctor',
-  'audit',
-  'preview-thumbnail',
-  'preview-cards',
-  'negctrl',
-];
-
-/** Run the built CLI; return {stdout, stderr, status, ms}. */
-function runCli(args: string[]): {
-  stdout: string;
-  stderr: string;
-  status: number | null;
-  ms: number;
-} {
-  const start = process.hrtime.bigint();
-  const res = spawnSync('node', [CLI, ...args], {
-    cwd: REPO_ROOT,
-    encoding: 'utf8',
-    timeout: 60_000,
-  });
-  const ms = Number(process.hrtime.bigint() - start) / 1e6;
-  return { stdout: res.stdout ?? '', stderr: res.stderr ?? '', status: res.status, ms };
-}
-
-/** Run the built CLI with an explicit cwd (for fixture projects in tmpdir). */
-function runCliIn(cwd: string, args: string[]): { stdout: string; stderr: string; status: number | null } {
-  const res = spawnSync('node', [CLI, ...args], { cwd, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 60_000 });
-  return { stdout: res.stdout ?? '', stderr: res.stderr ?? '', status: res.status };
-}
-
-/**
- * Write a fixture tend project under `root`: a garden polyglot at
- * docs/tend/overview.html plus one feature polyglot. Mirrors the minimal
- * polyglot shape scanAllFeaturesStrict reads (oo-meta + oo-data blocks). Used
- * by the `tend validate --strict` CI-gate test, which needs the REAL binary to
- * read a REAL project off disk.
- */
-function writeFixtureProject(root: string, garden: object, feature: object): void {
-  const featuresDir = join(root, 'docs', 'tend', 'features');
-  mkdirSync(featuresDir, { recursive: true });
-  const block = (data: object, meta: string): string => {
-    const json = JSON.stringify(data, null, 2).replace(/<\/script/g, '<\\/script');
-    return (
-      '<!doctype html>\n<html><body>\n' +
-      `<script id="oo-meta" type="application/json">\n${meta}\n</script>\n` +
-      `<script id="oo-data" type="application/json">\n${json}\n</script>\n` +
-      '</body></html>\n'
-    );
-  };
-  writeFileSync(
-    join(root, 'docs', 'tend', 'overview.html'),
-    block(garden, '{"kind":"garden","template_version":"1"}'),
-    'utf8',
-  );
-  const f = feature as { id: string };
-  writeFileSync(
-    join(featuresDir, `${f.id}.tend.html`),
-    block(feature, '{"kind":"feature","template_version":"1"}'),
-    'utf8',
-  );
-}
-
-/** Read every .ts source file under src/cli (excluding tests). */
-function cliSourceFiles(): { name: string; text: string }[] {
-  return readdirSync(CLI_DIR)
-    .filter((f) => f.endsWith('.ts') && !f.endsWith('.test.ts'))
-    .map((name) => ({ name, text: readFileSync(join(CLI_DIR, name), 'utf8') }));
-}

-// clear instruction rather than silently skipping (a skipped test is not green).
-const built = existsSync(CLI);

-// ─── c-fast-cold-start — no framework tax ──────────────────────────────────────
-//
-// The robust proof is STRUCTURAL, not a wall-clock assertion against npx (whose
-// 300ms npm-resolution overhead is not the CLI's design). Two structural facts
-// guarantee "no framework tax", plus one non-flaky warm `node` dispatch budget.
-
-describe('c-fast-cold-start: no command-framework tax', () => {
-  it('package.json declares no CLI framework dependency', () => {
-    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(REPO_ROOT, 'package.json'), 'utf8')) as {
-      dependencies?: Record<string, string>;
-      devDependencies?: Record<string, string>;
-    };
-    const allDeps = { ...(pkg.dependencies ?? {}), ...(pkg.devDependencies ?? {}) };
-    for (const framework of ['commander', 'yargs', 'oclif', 'cac', 'meow', 'minimist']) {
-      expect(allDeps, `package.json must not depend on ${framework}`).not.toHaveProperty(framework);
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('every subcommand dispatch arm loads its module lazily via dynamic import', () => {
-    const src = readFileSync(BIN_SRC, 'utf8');
-    // Each `case '<name>': { ... break; }` arm must contain an `await import(` —
-    // Node only loads the module a command actually uses, so unused subcommands
-    // never touch the module cache. Per-arm (not a global count) so removing the
-    // lazy import from ANY one subcommand discriminates.
-    for (const cmd of SUBCOMMANDS) {
-      const arm = new RegExp(`case '${cmd}':\\s*\\{([\\s\\S]*?)\\bbreak;`, 'm').exec(src);
-      expect(arm, `bin/tend.ts has no dispatch arm for "${cmd}"`).not.toBeNull();
-      expect(arm![1], `the "${cmd}" arm must lazily \`await import(...)\` its module`).toContain(
-        'await import(',
-      );
-    }
-    // And there is no top-level static import of a command framework.
-    expect(src).not.toMatch(/from\s+['"](commander|yargs|oclif|cac|meow|minimist)['"]/);
-  });
-
-  it.runIf(built)('a warm `node dist/bin/tend.js --help` dispatch stays well under budget', () => {
-    // Warm-up run (primes the disk/module cache) — not measured.
-    runCli(['--help']);
-    // Measured run: `node` invocation only (NOT npx). The handful of dynamic
-    // imports + a console.log have no framework startup cost; the generous 1.5s
-    // ceiling is a non-flaky guard against a regression that adds a heavy eager
-    // import to the dispatch path, not a tight benchmark.
-    const { status, ms } = runCli(['--help']);
-    expect(status).toBe(0);
-    expect(ms, `--help dispatch took ${ms.toFixed(0)}ms`).toBeLessThan(1500);

-// ─── c-non-agentic-only — no feature mutation from the CLI surface ─────────────
-
-describe('c-non-agentic-only: the CLI never mutates feature state', () => {
-  // Two honest invariants, matching the check's two clauses:
-  //
-  //   (A) NON-AGENTIC — the CLI needs no LLM / MCP session to run. It must not
-  //       import the agentic SDK, nor call the MCP write-tool / side-effect
-  //       engine functions (the code paths an agent drives). An interactive
-  //       setup prompt (init's y/N confirm) is NOT agentic — it is human
-  //       keyboard input — so node:readline is deliberately NOT forbidden.
-  //
-  //   (B) NO FEATURE MUTATION — no subcommand calls a feature-write code path
-  //       (writeFeature / writeCatalog / writeGardenPolyglot / writePolyglotAtomic
-  //       / applyFeature* / applyCatalogUpdate). These are the only ways a
-  //       feature polyglot's oo-data gets mutated; all live in src/mcp/tools/.
-  //
-  // We match real importable SYMBOLS / module specifiers — not MCP wire-names
-  // like `tend_update_feature`, which legitimately appear as *prose* in the
-  // CLAUDE.md guidance that `tend init` scaffolds for the user's agent. Writing
-  // a doc that names a tool is not calling that tool.
-  const FORBIDDEN = [
-    // (A) agentic runtime + side-effect engine (the apply* pipeline an MCP write drives)
-    '@anthropic-ai/sdk',
-    'applyFeatureCreate',
-    'applyFeatureUpdate',
-    'applyFeatureDelete',
-    'applyCatalogUpdate',
-    // (B) feature / catalog / polyglot write code paths
-    'writeFeature',
-    'writeCatalog',
-    'writeGardenPolyglot',
-    'writePolyglotAtomic',
-  ];
-
-  it('src/bin/tend.ts references no agentic / feature-write symbol', () => {
-    const src = readFileSync(BIN_SRC, 'utf8');
-    for (const symbol of FORBIDDEN) {
-      expect(src, `bin/tend.ts must not reference ${symbol}`).not.toContain(symbol);
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('no src/cli source file references an agentic / feature-write symbol', () => {
-    for (const { name, text } of cliSourceFiles()) {
-      for (const symbol of FORBIDDEN) {
-        expect(text, `src/cli/${name} must not reference ${symbol}`).not.toContain(symbol);
-      }
-    }
-  });
-
-  // The allowed structural writes: project-level config + derived refresh.
-  // `init` and `rename` splice oo-meta/oo-data on the GARDEN polyglot to set
-  // project_name / project_id — project configuration, not feature editing.
-  // `sync` splices oo-data only to re-render kind:diagram media content from
-  // its stored spec after a style upgrade — refreshing a derived snapshot,
-  // never authored content. Pin the exact file set so the allowance can never
-  // silently widen to feature mutation. (spliceOoData / spliceOoMeta are
-  // therefore intentionally absent from FORBIDDEN above.)
-  it('project-level oo-meta/oo-data splices are confined to init + rename + sync', () => {
-    const splicers = cliSourceFiles().filter(
-      ({ text }) => text.includes('spliceOoData') || text.includes('spliceOoMeta'),
-    );
-    const names = splicers.map((f) => f.name).sort();
-    expect(names).toEqual(['init.ts', 'rename-feature.ts', 'rename.ts', 'sync.ts']);
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── c-shared-render — one color table, declared once in render.ts ─────────────
-
-describe('c-shared-render: ANSI color is declared once, in render.ts', () => {
-  it('no src/cli source file other than render.ts emits raw ANSI escape codes', () => {
-    // The color primitives (green/yellow/dim/bold) wrap the only `\x1b[...m`
-    // escape sequences in the CLI. Any other source file declaring its own
-    // escape codes would be a duplicate color path — exactly what this forbids.
-    const ansiRe = /\\x1b\[|\\u001b\[|\\033\[/;
-    for (const { name, text } of cliSourceFiles()) {
-      if (name === 'render.ts') continue;
-      expect(ansiRe.test(text), `src/cli/${name} declares raw ANSI escape codes`).toBe(false);
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('every cli source file that colorizes output imports the colorizers from render.ts', () => {
-    // render.ts is the sole home of green/yellow/dim/bold. A file that calls any
-    // colorizer must import it from render.js — never re-implement it. The import
-    // specifier may be `./render.js` (siblings) or `../cli/render.js` (init.ts);
-    // both resolve to the same module, so accept any path ending in render.js.
-    const COLORIZERS = ['green', 'yellow', 'dim', 'bold'];
-    const importsRender = /from\s+['"][^'"]*render\.js['"]/;
-    for (const { name, text } of cliSourceFiles()) {
-      if (name === 'render.ts') continue;
-      const usesColor = COLORIZERS.some((c) => new RegExp(`\\b${c}\\(`).test(text));
-      if (usesColor) {
-        expect(importsRender.test(text), `src/cli/${name} calls a colorizer but does not import render.js`).toBe(
-          true,
-        );
-      }
-    }
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── tend validate --strict — the CI audit-rot gate (audit-staleness c007) ─────
-//
-// `tend validate --strict` exits non-zero when any VERIFIED feature cites stale
-// evidence (verified_but_stale > 0); plain `tend validate` keeps staleness a
-// non-blocking warning and exits 0 on the same project. Exercised END-TO-END
-// against the BUILT dist binary reading a REAL fixture project off disk — the
-// only surface that proves the argv flag → exit-code wiring.
-
-describe('validate --strict: the CI audit-rot gate (built dist)', () => {
-  let proj: string;
-
-  beforeEach(() => {
-    proj = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'tend-strict-cli-'));
-    // A real source file the verdict cites; its content will NOT match the
-    // recorded sha → the verdict is stale (drifted), not missing.
-    mkdirSync(join(proj, 'src'), { recursive: true });
-    writeFileSync(join(proj, 'src', 'gate-evidence.ts'), '// shipped content\n', 'utf8');
-
-    const featureId = 'gate-feat';
-    const feature = {
-      id: featureId,
-      title: 'Gate Feature',
-      status: 'verified',
-      // Claim the cited file so it is not flagged coverage_unclaimed (a
-      // structural cross-ref error that would flip valid=false on its own).
-      // The verdict's drifted sha is what makes it stale — the gate's signal.
-      coverage_files: ['src/gate-evidence.ts'],
-      audit: {
-        ran_at: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z',
-        result: 'pass',
-        verdicts: [
-          {
-            check_id: 'c1',
-            verdict: 'pass',
-            evidence_path: 'src/gate-evidence.ts',
-            evidence_sha: 'deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef', // does NOT match
-          },
-        ],
-      },
-    };
-    const garden = {
-      id: 'garden',
-      title: 'Gate Garden',
-      status: 'planned',
-      catalog: { schema_version: '1', project_id: 'gate', status: 'draft' },
-      // features_aggregate becomes catalog.features (composeCatalogFromGarden),
-      // so the feature is registered → no missing_from_catalog structural error.
-      features_aggregate: [{ id: featureId, title: 'Gate Feature', status: 'verified' }],
-    };
-    writeFixtureProject(proj, garden, feature);
-  });
-
-  afterEach(() => {
-    rmSync(proj, { recursive: true, force: true });
-  });
-
-  it('build present (run `npm run build` if this fails)', () => {
-    expect(built, `${CLI} missing — run \`npm run build\` first`).toBe(true);
-  });
-
-  it.runIf(built)('`validate --strict` exits 1 and names the verified-but-stale feature', () => {
-    const { status, stderr, stdout } = runCliIn(proj, ['validate', '--strict']);
-    expect(status, `expected non-zero exit\nstdout:\n${stdout}\nstderr:\n${stderr}`).toBe(1);
-    expect(stderr).toContain('verified_but_stale');
-    expect(stderr).toContain('gate-feat');
-  });
-
-  it.runIf(built)('plain `validate` (no --strict) exits 0 on the same project — staleness stays a warning', () => {
-    const { status, stdout, stderr } = runCliIn(proj, ['validate']);
-    // No structural errors (the feature is registered, deps intact); stale
-    // evidence is only a warning, so valid=true and the plain gate passes.
-    expect(status, `expected exit 0\nstdout:\n${stdout}\nstderr:\n${stderr}`).toBe(0);
-    // The drift IS surfaced (as a non-blocking warning), just not fatal.
-    expect(stdout + stderr).toContain('audit_evidence_stale');
-  });
-});

-/**
- * `tend audit <feature>` CLI — integration tests against the BUILT dist binary.
- *
- * These spawn `node dist/bin/tend.js audit __fixture__ --cwd <fixture>` and
- * recover the emitted AuditResult from real stdout via `extractJson`. They pin
- * the egress contract end-to-end (compute → emit → extract → schema-parse) and
- * the COMPUTE-ONLY invariant: the fixture polyglot is byte-identical before vs
- * after, and audit.ts imports no write-path symbol.
- *
- * Requires `npm run build` first (they exercise dist/, not src/). The passing
- * fixture run drives the real negctrl (a throwaway git worktree) — slow but the
- * point: the seam, the emit, and the no-write guarantee are exercised for real,
- * never mocked.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
-import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
-import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { AuditResultSchema } from '../core/bridge/plan.js';
-import { extractJson } from '../core/bridge/emit.js';
-import { readFeature } from '../core/files.js';
-
-const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);
-const __dirname = dirname(__filename);
-const REPO_ROOT = join(__dirname, '..', '..');
-const CLI = join(REPO_ROOT, 'dist', 'bin', 'tend.js');
-const PASSING = join(REPO_ROOT, 'tests', 'fixtures', 'audit-emit', 'passing');
-
-/** Run the built CLI; return {stdout, stderr, status}. */
-function runCli(args: string[]): { stdout: string; stderr: string; status: number | null } {
-  const res = spawnSync('node', [CLI, ...args], {
-    cwd: REPO_ROOT,
-    encoding: 'utf8',
-    timeout: 300_000,
-  });
-  return { stdout: res.stdout ?? '', stderr: res.stderr ?? '', status: res.status };
-}
-
-// The CLI tests need the build present. If dist is missing, fail loudly with a
-// clear instruction rather than silently skipping (a skipped test is not green).
-const built = existsSync(CLI);
-
-describe('tend audit CLI — emits a recoverable AuditResult (built dist)', () => {
-  it('build present (run `npm run build` if this fails)', () => {
-    expect(built, `${CLI} missing — run \`npm run build\` first`).toBe(true);
-  });
-
-  it.runIf(built)(
-    'emits a block extractJson + AuditResultSchema accept; verdict pass + discriminated; exit 0',
-    () => {
-      const { stdout, status } = runCli(['audit', '__fixture__', '--cwd', PASSING]);
-      expect(status, `CLI exited ${status}\nstdout:\n${stdout}`).toBe(0);
-      const result = AuditResultSchema.parse(extractJson(stdout));
-      expect(result.verdicts).toHaveLength(1);
-      expect(result.verdicts[0]!.verdict).toBe('pass');
-      expect(result.verdicts[0]!.negctrl).toEqual({ ran: true, discriminated: true });
-    },
-    180_000,
-  );
-
-  it.runIf(built)(
-    'the human summary goes to stderr, leaving stdout block clean and recoverable amid any prose',
-    () => {
-      const { stdout, stderr } = runCli(['audit', '__fixture__', '--cwd', PASSING]);
-      // Diagnostics live on stderr, not stdout.
-      expect(stderr).toContain('__fixture__');
-      // Even wrapped in extra chatter, the block is recoverable (robustness).
-      const noisy = `preamble from some wrapper\n${stdout}\nepilogue noise\n`;
-      const result = AuditResultSchema.parse(extractJson(noisy));
-      expect(result.verdicts[0]!.check).toBe('c1');
-    },
-    180_000,
-  );
-
-  it.runIf(built)(
-    'COMPUTE-ONLY: the fixture polyglot oo-data is byte-identical before vs after the run',
-    async () => {
-      const before = await readFeature('__fixture__', PASSING);
-      runCli(['audit', '__fixture__', '--cwd', PASSING]);
-      const after = await readFeature('__fixture__', PASSING);
-      expect(after).toEqual(before);
-      expect(after.audit).toBeUndefined();
-      expect(after.status).toBe(before.status);
-    },
-    180_000,
-  );
-});
-
-describe('tend audit CLI — compute-only by construction (static guard)', () => {
-  it('audit.ts imports no write-path symbol', () => {
-    const src = readFileSync(join(__dirname, 'audit.ts'), 'utf8');
-    for (const forbidden of [
-      'tend_update_feature',
-      'spliceOoData',
-      'writeFeature',
-      'writePolyglotAtomic',
-      'writeGardenPolyglot',
-    ]) {
-      expect(src, `audit.ts must not reference ${forbidden}`).not.toContain(forbidden);
-    }
-  });
-});

-/**
- * Integration tests for `tend doctor` — detect + repair common project issues.
- *
- * Builds a real temp tend project on disk, introduces aggregate drift (a feature
- * on disk not in garden's features_aggregate), then exercises:
- *   - report mode: names the drift, recommends --fix, returns 0
- *   - fix mode: runs aggregate, drift clears, returns 0
- *   - clean project: reports healthy, returns 0
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, vi } from 'vitest';
-import { mkdtemp, mkdir, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { join } from 'node:path';
-import { readCatalog } from '../core/files.js';
-import { REASON_CODES } from '../core/reason-codes.js';
-
-// ─── Fixture helpers (mirrors validation.integration.test.ts shape) ────────────
-
-let tmp: string;
-
-async function makeTendDirs(root: string): Promise<void> {
-  await mkdir(join(root, 'docs', 'tend', 'features'), { recursive: true });
-}
-
-/** Minimal polyglot whose oo-data block parses. */
-function polyglot(data: object, meta = '{"kind":"feature","template_version":"1"}'): string {
-  const json = JSON.stringify(data, null, 2).replace(/<\/script/g, '<\\/script');
-  return (
-    '<!doctype html>\n<html><body>\n' +
-    `<script id="oo-meta" type="application/json">\n${meta}\n</script>\n` +
-    '<script id="oo-data" type="application/json">\n' +
-    json +
-    '\n</script>\n</body></html>\n'
-  );
-}
-
-/** Write the garden polyglot with optional features_aggregate pre-populated. */
-async function writeGarden(
-  features: Array<{ id: string; title: string; status: string }> = [],
-): Promise<void> {
-  const data = {
-    id: 'garden',
-    title: 'Test Garden',
-    status: 'planned',
-    catalog: { schema_version: '1', project_id: 'test', status: 'draft' },
-    features_aggregate: features,
-  };
-  await writeFile(
-    join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'overview.html'),
-    polyglot(data, '{"kind":"garden","template_version":"1"}'),
-    'utf8',
-  );
-}
-
-/** Write a feature polyglot under docs/tend/features/<id>.tend.html. */
-async function writeFeature(id: string, extra: object = {}): Promise<void> {
-  const data = { id, title: id, status: 'planned', ...extra };
-  await writeFile(
-    join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', `${id}.tend.html`),
-    polyglot(data),
-    'utf8',
-  );
-}
-
-// ─── Console capture helper ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-async function captureOutput(fn: () => Promise<number>): Promise<{ code: number; lines: string[] }> {
-  const lines: string[] = [];
-  const logSpy = vi.spyOn(console, 'log').mockImplementation((...args: unknown[]) => {
-    lines.push(args.map(String).join(' '));
-  });
-  const warnSpy = vi.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation((...args: unknown[]) => {
-    lines.push(args.map(String).join(' '));
-  });
-  let code: number;
-  try {
-    code = await fn();
-  } finally {
-    logSpy.mockRestore();
-    warnSpy.mockRestore();
-  }
-  return { code, lines };
-}
-
-// ─── Lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-beforeEach(async () => {
-  tmp = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'tend-doctor-'));
-  await makeTendDirs(tmp);
-});
-
-afterEach(async () => {
-  await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
-});
-
-// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('runDoctor — aggregate drift', () => {
-  it('report mode: names the drift and recommends --fix, returns 0', async () => {
-    // Garden index is empty; a feature file exists on disk → aggregate drift
-    await writeGarden([]);
-    await writeFeature('new-feature');
-
-    const { runDoctor } = await import('./doctor.js');
-    const { code, lines } = await captureOutput(() => runDoctor([], tmp));
-
-    expect(code).toBe(0);
-    const output = lines.join('\n');
-    // Must name the issue — missing_from_catalog or similar drift
-    expect(output).toMatch(/missing_from_catalog|aggregate|drift|issue|fix/i);
-    // Must suggest --fix
-    expect(output).toMatch(/--fix/);
-  });
-
-  it('fix mode: runs aggregate so garden features_aggregate includes the feature, returns 0', async () => {
-    // Garden index is empty; feature file exists → drift
-    await writeGarden([]);
-    await writeFeature('new-feature');
-
-    const { runDoctor } = await import('./doctor.js');
-    const { code } = await captureOutput(() => runDoctor(['--fix'], tmp));
-
-    expect(code).toBe(0);
-
-    // After fix, the garden's features list must include new-feature
-    const catalog = await readCatalog(tmp);
-    expect(catalog.features.some((f) => f.id === 'new-feature')).toBe(true);
-  });
-
-  it('clean project: reports healthy with no issues, returns 0', async () => {
-    // Feature is properly registered in the garden index
-    await writeGarden([{ id: 'clean-feat', title: 'Clean Feat', status: 'planned' }]);
-    await writeFeature('clean-feat');
-
-    const { runDoctor } = await import('./doctor.js');
-    const { code, lines } = await captureOutput(() => runDoctor([], tmp));
-
-    expect(code).toBe(0);
-    const output = lines.join('\n');
-    expect(output).toMatch(/healthy|clean|no issue/i);
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── Stale-evidence detection — canonical reason codes ────────────────────────
-//
-// doctor.ts must detect stale-evidence warnings regardless of whether
-// validation.ts emits legacy aliases or canonical REASON_CODES identifiers.
-// This describe block dynamically mocks runValidate per test (vi.doMock +
-// vi.resetModules) so it doesn't bleed into the integration tests above.
-
-// Minimal valid ValidateResult shape — only fields doctor reads.
-function makeValidateResult(warningTypes: string[]): object {
-  return {
-    valid: true,
-    file_errors: [],
-    cross_ref_errors: [],
-    warnings: warningTypes.map((type) => ({ type, message: `${type} detected`, affected_node: 'feat-x' })),
-    coverage: { ghostClaims: [], unclaimed: [], multiClaimed: [] },
-    drift_verdict: 'stale-evidence',
-    recommended_next_command: '/tend audit feat-x',
-    verified_but_stale: 0,
-    verified_but_stale_features: [],
-  };
-}
-
-describe('runDoctor — stale-evidence detection', () => {
-  beforeEach(() => {
-    vi.resetModules();
-  });
-
-  afterEach(() => {
-    vi.resetModules();
-  });
-
-  const cases: Array<{ label: string; type: string }> = [
-    // ── Legacy alias strings (what validation.ts emits today) ─────────────────
-    { label: 'audit_evidence_stale (legacy alias)', type: 'audit_evidence_stale' },
-    { label: 'audit_evidence_missing (legacy alias)', type: 'audit_evidence_missing' },
-    { label: 'mock_only_audit_evidence (legacy alias)', type: 'mock_only_audit_evidence' },
-    // ── Canonical reason codes (REASON_CODES source of truth) ─────────────────
-    { label: 'stale_evidence (canonical)', type: REASON_CODES.stale_evidence.code },
-    { label: 'missing_evidence (canonical)', type: REASON_CODES.missing_evidence.code },
-    { label: 'mock_only_evidence (canonical)', type: REASON_CODES.mock_only_evidence.code },
-  ];
-
-  for (const { label, type } of cases) {
-    it(`detects a stale-evidence warning when validation emits: ${label}`, async () => {
-      const result = makeValidateResult([type]);
-      vi.doMock('../core/validate.js', () => ({
-        runValidate: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(result),
-      }));
-
-      // Fresh import after vi.doMock so doctor picks up the mocked runValidate.
-      const { runDoctor } = await import('./doctor.js');
-      const { code, lines } = await captureOutput(() => runDoctor([], '/irrelevant'));
-
-      expect(code).toBe(0);
-      const output = lines.join('\n');
-      // Doctor must surface the stale-evidence warning — not report "healthy".
-      expect(output).not.toMatch(/healthy — no issues detected/);
-      expect(output).toMatch(/stale evidence|audit/i);
-    });
-  }
-});

-/**
- * Tests for the `tend execute` CLI command.
- *
- * Strategy mirrors src/cli/next.test.ts and src/mcp/tools/output-execution-plan.test.ts:
- * write a small fixture project under tmpdir() (catalog + feature polyglots +
- * an adapter config pointing at the absolute dist/ generator path), point
- * process.cwd() at it, capture stdout/stderr during a `runExecute(args)`
- * invocation, and assert both the on-disk plan files and the streamed status.
- *
- * The MCP tool `tend_output_execution_plan` and this CLI share the SAME core
- * orchestration (`generateExecutionPlan` in src/core/execute.ts). These tests
- * prove the CLI surface — arg parsing, the write contract, non-agentic
- * operation, and per-feature streaming — not the orchestration internals
- * (those are covered by output-execution-plan.test.ts + execute.test.ts).
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, vi } from 'vitest';
-import { mkdtemp, mkdir, rm, readFile, writeFile, access } from 'node:fs/promises';
-import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { join, resolve, dirname } from 'node:path';
-import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
-import { runExecute } from './execute.js';
-import { writeJSON } from '../core/files.js';
-import type { Catalog, Feature, AdapterConfig } from '../core/types.js';
-
-const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
-
-// ─── Absolute dist generator path (built by `npm run build`, checked into repo) ─
-
-const ROOT = resolve(import.meta.url.replace('file://', ''), '../../..');
-const MARKDOWN_GENERATOR = join(ROOT, 'dist/adapters/markdown/generator.js');
-
-// ─── Fixtures ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-function makeCatalog(overrides: Partial<Catalog> = {}): Catalog {
-  return {
-    schema_version: '1',
-    project_id: 'test-project',
-    status: 'draft',
-    features: [],
-    ...overrides,
-  };
-}
-
-function makeFeature(id: string, overrides: Partial<Feature> = {}): Feature {
-  return {
