-// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-// c002 — whole-project mode emits plans only for non-planned... see note below.
-//
-// The slot/checks text says "in-progress or verified". The DEFAULT approval gate
-// (filterByApproval without force) is { planned, in-progress }; verified is only
-// eligible with force. Batch mode (resolveTargets without an id) selects unblocked
-// features WITH steps. So whole-project mode without force emits plans for
-// planned + in-progress features that have steps and are unblocked; a verified
-// feature is skipped by the approval gate unless --force is passed. We test the
-// real, honest behavior: a planned feature with steps gets a plan; a planned
-// feature WITHOUT steps does not; a verified feature is skipped without --force.
-// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-
-describe('tend execute — whole-project mode (c002)', () => {
-  it('omitting --feature emits plans for every unblocked feature with steps; step-less features get none', async () => {
-    const withSteps = makeFeature('alpha', { status: 'planned', steps: [makeStep('s1')] });
-    const inProgress = makeFeature('beta', { status: 'in-progress', steps: [makeStep('s1')] });
-    const noSteps = makeFeature('gamma', { status: 'planned' });
-    await writeCatalogFile(
-      makeCatalog({
-        features: [
-          { id: 'alpha', title: 'alpha', status: 'planned' },
-          { id: 'beta', title: 'beta', status: 'in-progress' },
-          { id: 'gamma', title: 'gamma', status: 'planned' },
-        ],
-      }),
-    );
-    await writeFeatureFile(withSteps);
-    await writeFeatureFile(inProgress);
-    await writeFeatureFile(noSteps);
-    await writeMarkdownAdapter();
-
-    await runExecute(['--adapter', 'markdown']);
-
-    const outputDir = join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'output', 'markdown');
-    expect(await fileExists(join(outputDir, 'alpha.md'))).toBe(true);
-    expect(await fileExists(join(outputDir, 'beta.md'))).toBe(true);
-    // gamma has no steps → batch mode pre-filters it; no plan file.
-    expect(await fileExists(join(outputDir, 'gamma.md'))).toBe(false);
-
-    const out = capturedStdout();
-    expect(out).toContain('alpha');
-    expect(out).toContain('beta');
-  });
-
-  it('a verified feature is skipped without --force, and included with --force', async () => {
-    const verified = makeFeature('done-feat', { status: 'verified', steps: [makeStep('s1')] });
-    await writeCatalogFile(
-      makeCatalog({ features: [{ id: 'done-feat', title: 'done-feat', status: 'verified' }] }),
-    );
-    await writeFeatureFile(verified);
-    await writeMarkdownAdapter();
-
-    // Without --force: targeted by id but the approval gate skips it.
-    await runExecute(['--adapter', 'markdown', '--feature', 'done-feat']);
-    const planPath = join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'output', 'markdown', 'done-feat.md');
-    expect(await fileExists(planPath)).toBe(false);
-    expect(capturedStdout()).toContain('skip');
-
-    // With --force: the plan file is written.
-    logSpy.mockClear();
-    await runExecute(['--adapter', 'markdown', '--feature', 'done-feat', '--force']);
-    expect(await fileExists(planPath)).toBe(true);
-  });
-});

-// c003 — no MCP server required; runs directly from a shell / CI runner
-// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-
-describe('tend execute — runs without an MCP server (c003)', () => {
-  // RUNTIME: in a clean tmp project with no server process, runExecute produces
-  // the plan file and exits 0. (The whole test file runs without any `tend
-  // serve` process; success here is the integration proof of "works from a
-  // shell / CI runner with no MCP session".)
-  it('produces the plan file with exit 0 in a clean project (no server running)', async () => {
-    const feature = makeFeature('ci-feat', { status: 'planned', steps: [makeStep('s1')] });
-    await writeCatalogFile(
-      makeCatalog({ features: [{ id: 'ci-feat', title: 'ci-feat', status: 'planned' }] }),
-    );
-    await writeFeatureFile(feature);
-    await writeMarkdownAdapter();
-
-    await runExecute(['--adapter', 'markdown', '--feature', 'ci-feat']);
-
-    expect(await fileExists(join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'output', 'markdown', 'ci-feat.md'))).toBe(true);
-    expect(exitCode ?? 0).toBe(0);
-  });
-
-  // SOURCE GUARD: the execute path spawns no subprocess and starts no server.
-  // A static guard is more discriminating than spying on node:child_process
-  // (un-spyable in ESM): it pins the absence at the import site, where a
-  // mutation that shelled out to `tend serve` could not hide. The CLI module
-  // and the shared core orchestration it delegates to must both be free of
-  // child_process and the MCP server module.
-  it('neither src/cli/execute.ts nor src/core/execute.ts imports child_process or the MCP server', () => {
-    const cliSrc = readFileSync(join(__dirname, 'execute.ts'), 'utf8');
-    const coreSrc = readFileSync(join(__dirname, '..', 'core', 'execute.ts'), 'utf8');
-    for (const [name, src] of [
-      ['src/cli/execute.ts', cliSrc],
-      ['src/core/execute.ts', coreSrc],
-    ] as const) {
-      expect(src, `${name} must not import node:child_process`).not.toMatch(
-        /from\s+['"]node:child_process['"]/,
-      );
-      expect(src, `${name} must not start/import the MCP server`).not.toContain('mcp/server');
-      expect(src, `${name} must not call startServer`).not.toContain('startServer');
-    }
-  });
-});

-  it('--save-dev: attempts install and warns on failure when package.json exists', async () => {

-    // Hermetic failure: blank PATH makes the spawned npm unresolvable, so the
-    // install throws instantly (ENOENT) and the warn path runs offline. The
-    // old "no real registry" assumption stopped holding on 2026-06-04 when a
-    // third party published "tend-cli" — a live resolve can now SLOWLY
-    // succeed, and npm's retry cycle outlives the test timeout.

-    process.env['PATH'] = '/nonexistent-hermetic';
-    try {
-      const lines = await captureLog(() => init(['--save-dev']));
-      const output = lines.join('\n');

-    } finally {
-      process.env['PATH'] = savedPath;
-    }
-  });

-/**
- * negctrl — negative-control integration tests (function-direct edition).
- *
- * Mirrors tests/scripts/negctrl.spec.ts but calls runNegctrl() directly
- * instead of spawning the .mjs script via node. Stdout is captured via
- * vi.spyOn(process.stdout, 'write'); the function returns the exit code
- * rather than calling process.exit.
- *
- * Invariants verified (identical to the .mjs spec):
- *   1. DISCRIMINATES: mutation breaks unit → returned code 0, stdout "DISCRIMINATES".
- *   2. DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE: trivially-passing test → code 1, stdout "DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE".
- *   3. SAFETY: live target file byte-identical before/after both runs.
- *   4. No leftover /tmp worktrees after each run.
- *   5. AMBIGUOUS find: 0 or >1 matches → code 2.
- *   6. INVALID BASELINE: red test on clean code → code 2, stderr "baseline".
- *   7. UNTRACKED FILES: test that depends on an untracked helper file → code 0 after fix.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
-import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { execSync } from 'node:child_process';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
-import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
-import { runNegctrl } from './negctrl.js';
-
-const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);
-const __dirname = dirname(__filename);
-const REPO_ROOT = join(__dirname, '..', '..');
-
-// ── Target: src/core/progress.ts ─────────────────────────────────────────────
-// computeProgress counts steps where status === 'done' || status === 'skipped'.
-// Negating this breaks the logic: completed steps become 0, incomplete become 1.
-// The discriminating test: src/core/progress.test.ts
-//   "returns 100% when all steps are done" → expects 100, gets 0 on break.
-const TARGET_FILE = 'src/core/progress.ts';
-const FIND_FRAGMENT = `s.status === 'done' || s.status === 'skipped'`;
-const REPLACE_FRAGMENT = `s.status === 'NEVER_MATCH_SENTINEL_NEGCTRL'`;
-const DISCRIMINATING_TEST = `npx vitest run src/core/progress.test.ts`;
-
-/** Read the live target file's current bytes. */
-function readTarget(): string {
-  return readFileSync(join(REPO_ROOT, TARGET_FILE), 'utf8');
-}
-
-/**
- * Assert negctrl left the target file byte-identical to its pre-run content.
- * Uses a before-snapshot, not git status, so it holds even when the file has
- * uncommitted edits.
- */
-function assertTargetRestored(before: string): void {
-  const after = readTarget();
-  expect(
-    after === before,
-    'negctrl did not restore the target file to its pre-run content (mutation leaked into the live tree).',
-  ).toBe(true);
-}
-
-/** Assert no negctrl-owned worktrees were left behind. */
-function assertNoOrphanWorktrees(): void {
-  const result = execSync('git worktree list', { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: REPO_ROOT });
-  const tmpEntries = result
-    .split('\n')
-    .filter((line) => line.startsWith('/tmp/'));
-  expect(
-    tmpEntries,
-    `Leftover /tmp worktrees found:\n${tmpEntries.join('\n')}`,
-  ).toHaveLength(0);
-}
-
-// ── Stdout/stderr capture helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-/** Capture everything written to process.stdout.write during fn(). */
-function captureStdout(fn: () => number): { output: string; code: number } {
-  const chunks: string[] = [];
-  const spy = vi.spyOn(process.stdout, 'write').mockImplementation((chunk) => {
-    chunks.push(typeof chunk === 'string' ? chunk : chunk.toString());
-    return true;
-  });
-  let code: number;
-  try {
-    code = fn();
-  } finally {
-    spy.mockRestore();
-  }
-  return { output: chunks.join(''), code };
-}
-
-/** Capture everything written to process.stderr.write during fn(). */
-function captureStderr(fn: () => number): { output: string; code: number } {
-  const chunks: string[] = [];
-  const spy = vi.spyOn(process.stderr, 'write').mockImplementation((chunk) => {
-    chunks.push(typeof chunk === 'string' ? chunk : chunk.toString());
-    return true;
-  });
-  let code: number;
-  try {
-    code = fn();
-  } finally {
-    spy.mockRestore();
-  }
-  return { output: chunks.join(''), code };
-}
-
-/** Capture both stdout and stderr simultaneously. */
-function captureAll(fn: () => number): { stdout: string; stderr: string; code: number } {
-  const outChunks: string[] = [];
-  const errChunks: string[] = [];
-  const outSpy = vi.spyOn(process.stdout, 'write').mockImplementation((chunk) => {
-    outChunks.push(typeof chunk === 'string' ? chunk : chunk.toString());
-    return true;
-  });
-  const errSpy = vi.spyOn(process.stderr, 'write').mockImplementation((chunk) => {
-    errChunks.push(typeof chunk === 'string' ? chunk : chunk.toString());
-    return true;
-  });
-  let code: number;
-  try {
-    code = fn();
-  } finally {
-    outSpy.mockRestore();
-    errSpy.mockRestore();
-  }
-  return { stdout: outChunks.join(''), stderr: errChunks.join(''), code };
-}
-
-// ─── Test suite ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('negctrl DISCRIMINATES verdict', () => {
-  it(
-    'returns 0 and writes DISCRIMINATES when mutation breaks the unit and test catches it',
-    () => {
-      const { output, code } = captureStdout(() =>
-        runNegctrl(
-          ['--file', TARGET_FILE, '--find', FIND_FRAGMENT, '--replace', REPLACE_FRAGMENT, '--test', DISCRIMINATING_TEST],
-          REPO_ROOT,
-        ),
-      );
-      expect(code, `runNegctrl returned ${code}\nstdout: ${output}`).toBe(0);
-      expect(output).toContain('DISCRIMINATES');
-      expect(output).not.toContain('DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE');
-    },
-    120_000,
-  );
-});
-
-describe('negctrl DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE verdict', () => {
-  it(
-    'returns 1 and writes DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE when test always passes regardless of mutation',
-    () => {
-      const { output, code } = captureStdout(() =>
-        runNegctrl(
-          ['--file', TARGET_FILE, '--find', FIND_FRAGMENT, '--replace', REPLACE_FRAGMENT, '--test', 'true'],
-          REPO_ROOT,
-        ),
-      );
-      expect(code, `runNegctrl returned ${code}\nstdout: ${output}`).toBe(1);
-      expect(output).toContain('DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE');
-      expect(output).not.toContain('DISCRIMINATES\n');
-    },
-    120_000,
-  );
-});
-
-describe('negctrl SAFETY — live tree is never touched', () => {
-  it(
-    'leaves the target source file unmodified after a DISCRIMINATES run',
-    () => {
-      const before = readTarget();
-      captureAll(() =>
-        runNegctrl(
-          ['--file', TARGET_FILE, '--find', FIND_FRAGMENT, '--replace', REPLACE_FRAGMENT, '--test', DISCRIMINATING_TEST],
-          REPO_ROOT,
-        ),
-      );
-      assertTargetRestored(before);
-    },
-    120_000,
-  );
-
-  it(
-    'leaves the target source file unmodified after a DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE run',
-    () => {
-      const before = readTarget();
-      captureAll(() =>
-        runNegctrl(
-          ['--file', TARGET_FILE, '--find', FIND_FRAGMENT, '--replace', REPLACE_FRAGMENT, '--test', 'true'],
-          REPO_ROOT,
-        ),
-      );
-      assertTargetRestored(before);
-    },
-    120_000,
-  );
-
-  it(
-    'leaves no leftover worktrees after a DISCRIMINATES run',
-    () => {
-      captureAll(() =>
-        runNegctrl(
-          ['--file', TARGET_FILE, '--find', FIND_FRAGMENT, '--replace', REPLACE_FRAGMENT, '--test', DISCRIMINATING_TEST],
-          REPO_ROOT,
-        ),
-      );
-      assertNoOrphanWorktrees();
-    },
-    120_000,
-  );
-
-  it(
-    'leaves no leftover worktrees after a DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE run',
-    () => {
-      captureAll(() =>
-        runNegctrl(
-          ['--file', TARGET_FILE, '--find', FIND_FRAGMENT, '--replace', REPLACE_FRAGMENT, '--test', 'true'],
-          REPO_ROOT,
-        ),
-      );
-      assertNoOrphanWorktrees();
-    },
-    120_000,
-  );
-});
-
-describe('negctrl find-not-unique guard', () => {
-  it(
-    'returns 2 when --find string is not found in target file (0 matches)',
-    () => {
-      const { stderr, code } = captureAll(() =>
-        runNegctrl(
-          ['--file', TARGET_FILE, '--find', '__THIS_STRING_DOES_NOT_EXIST_IN_THE_FILE__', '--replace', 'anything', '--test', 'true'],
-          REPO_ROOT,
-        ),
-      );
-      expect(code).toBe(2);
-      expect(stderr).toMatch(/0.*match/i);
-    },
-    30_000,
-  );
-
-  it(
-    'returns 2 when --find string matches more than once (>1 matches)',
-    () => {
-      // "status" appears many times in progress.ts — guaranteed >1 match.
-      const { stderr, code } = captureAll(() =>
-        runNegctrl(
-          ['--file', TARGET_FILE, '--find', 'status', '--replace', 'anything', '--test', 'true'],
-          REPO_ROOT,
-        ),
-      );
-      expect(code).toBe(2);
-      expect(stderr).toMatch(/[2-9]\d*|[1-9]\d+ match/i);
-    },
-    30_000,
-  );
-});
-
-describe('negctrl invalid-baseline guard', () => {
-  it(
-    'returns 2 when the cited test does not pass on UNMODIFIED code (red baseline)',
-    () => {
-      const { stderr, code } = captureAll(() =>
-        runNegctrl(
-          ['--file', TARGET_FILE, '--find', FIND_FRAGMENT, '--replace', REPLACE_FRAGMENT, '--test', 'false'],
-          REPO_ROOT,
-        ),
-      );
-      expect(code, `expected return code 2 (invalid baseline), got ${code}`).toBe(2);
-      expect(stderr).toMatch(/baseline/i);
-    },
-    120_000,

-// ── Untracked-file mirroring ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
-//
-// Bug: mirrorWorkingState() used `git diff HEAD | git apply`, which only
-// mirrors tracked-file changes. An UNTRACKED file (not yet `git add`ed)
-// that the test depends on was absent from the worktree → baseline failed
-// → negctrl returned 2 (indeterminate) even though the test was fine.
-//
-// Fix: after applying the tracked diff, also copy untracked-non-ignored
-// files into the worktree via `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z`.
-//
-// Fixture:
-//   Committed: mod.mjs (exports value=42), mod.test.mjs (asserts value===EXPECTED)
-//   Untracked: helper.mjs (exports EXPECTED=42) — mod.test.mjs imports it
-//
-// Without fix: worktree has no helper.mjs → `node mod.test.mjs` fails to
-//              resolve the import → baseline non-zero → returns 2.
-// With fix:    helper.mjs is copied → baseline passes → mutation of mod.mjs
-//              (42 → 0) breaks the assertion → returns 0 (DISCRIMINATES).
-
-describe('negctrl mirrors untracked non-ignored files into the worktree', () => {
-  let repoDir: string;
-
-  beforeEach(() => {
-    // Create a fresh isolated git repo in a temp dir.
-    repoDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'negctrl-untracked-'));
-
-    execSync('git init', { cwd: repoDir, stdio: 'pipe' });
-    execSync('git config user.email "test@test.com"', { cwd: repoDir, stdio: 'pipe' });
-    execSync('git config user.name "Test"', { cwd: repoDir, stdio: 'pipe' });
-
-    // mod.mjs — the committed source file being mutated.
-    writeFileSync(
-      join(repoDir, 'mod.mjs'),
-      `export const value = 42;\n`,
-    );
-
-    // mod.test.mjs — the committed test that imports the UNTRACKED helper.
-    // Uses node:assert so no test-runner deps are needed.
-    writeFileSync(
-      join(repoDir, 'mod.test.mjs'),
-      [
-        `import { value } from './mod.mjs';`,
-        `import { EXPECTED } from './helper.mjs';`,
-        `import assert from 'node:assert';`,
-        `assert.strictEqual(value, EXPECTED, \`Expected \${EXPECTED} got \${value}\`);`,
-      ].join('\n') + '\n',
-    );
-
-    // Commit mod.mjs + mod.test.mjs (helper.mjs is intentionally NOT committed).
-    execSync('git add mod.mjs mod.test.mjs', { cwd: repoDir, stdio: 'pipe' });
-    execSync('git commit -m "initial"', { cwd: repoDir, stdio: 'pipe' });
-
-    // helper.mjs — UNTRACKED; the test file imports it.
-    writeFileSync(
-      join(repoDir, 'helper.mjs'),
-      `export const EXPECTED = 42;\n`,
-    );
-  });
-
-  afterEach(() => {
-    rmSync(repoDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
-  });
-
-  it(
-    'returns 0 (DISCRIMINATES) when the cited test depends on an untracked helper file',
-    () => {
-      const { stdout, stderr, code } = captureAll(() =>
-        runNegctrl(
-          [
-            '--file',    'mod.mjs',
-            '--find',    'export const value = 42;',
-            '--replace', 'export const value = 0;',
-            '--test',    'node mod.test.mjs',
-          ],
-          repoDir,
-        ),
-      );
-      expect(
-        code,
-        `Expected 0 (DISCRIMINATES) but got ${code}.\nstdout: ${stdout}\nstderr: ${stderr}\n` +
-        `(exit 2 = baseline failed, likely because helper.mjs was not mirrored into the worktree)`,
-      ).toBe(0);
-      expect(stdout).toContain('DISCRIMINATES');
-      expect(stdout).not.toContain('DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE');
-    },
-    60_000,
-  );
-});

-/**
- * Tests for `tend rename-feature <old-id> <new-id>`.
- *
- * Test-first per CLAUDE.md rule #2. Each describe block covers one
- * behavioural contract:
- *
- *   - Refusal cases — invalid args, missing old, existing new, garden id.
- *   - Happy rename — new file written, old deleted, id field updated,
- *     sibling refs rewired, garden features_aggregate updated, board.html
- *     refreshed best-effort, audits preserved (evidence_sha intact).
- *   - Parent / child rewiring — a child's parent field is rewritten; a
- *     parent's subpages[] has the old id replaced by the new id.
- *   - Prose-mention worklist — narratives mentioning the old id are listed
- *     (not rewritten) in the cascade report.
- *
- * No internal mocks — real tmp dirs, real file writes.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, vi } from 'vitest';
-import { mkdtemp, mkdir, rm, writeFile, readFile, access } from 'node:fs/promises';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { join } from 'node:path';
-import { renameFeature } from './rename-feature.js';
-
-// ─── Fixture helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-let tmp: string;
-let stdout: string[];
-let stderr: string[];
-
-beforeEach(async () => {
-  tmp = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'tend-rename-feature-'));
-  await mkdir(join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features'), { recursive: true });
-  stdout = [];
-  stderr = [];
-  vi.spyOn(console, 'log').mockImplementation((...args: unknown[]) => {
-    stdout.push(args.map(String).join(' '));
-  });
-  vi.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation((...args: unknown[]) => {
-    stderr.push(args.map(String).join(' '));
-  });
-  vi.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation((...args: unknown[]) => {
-    stderr.push(args.map(String).join(' '));
-  });
-});
-
-afterEach(async () => {
-  vi.restoreAllMocks();
-  await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
-});
-
-// ─── Minimal polyglot builder ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-function polyglot(data: object): string {
-  const json = JSON.stringify(data, null, 2).replace(/<\/script/g, '<\\/script');
-  return (
-    '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n' +
-    '# tend feature artifact\n' +
-    ": << 'OO_HTML'\n" +
-    '<!doctype html>\n<html><body>\n' +
-    '<script id="oo-meta" type="application/json">\n' +
-    '{"schema_version":"1","kind":"feature","tend_version":"1.0.0"}\n' +
-    '</script>\n' +
-    '<script id="oo-data" type="application/json">\n' +
-    json +
-    '\n</script>\n' +
-    '<!-- OO:STYLE:START -->\n<!-- OO:STYLE:END -->\n' +
-    '<!-- OO:RENDER:START -->\n<!-- OO:RENDER:END -->\n' +
-    '<!-- OO:CLIENT:START -->\n<!-- OO:CLIENT:END -->\n' +
-    '</body></html>\n' +
-    'OO_HTML\n' +
-    '# OO:SHELL:START\necho ok\n# OO:SHELL:END\n'
-  );
-}
-
-function gardenPolyglot(
-  features: Array<{ id: string; title: string; status: string }> = [],
-): string {
-  const data = {
-    id: 'garden',
-    title: 'Test Garden',
-    status: 'planned',
-    catalog: { schema_version: '1', project_id: 'test', status: 'draft' },
-    features_aggregate: features,
-  };
-  const json = JSON.stringify(data, null, 2);
-  return (
-    '<!doctype html>\n<html><body>\n' +
-    '<script id="oo-meta" type="application/json">\n' +
-    '{"schema_version":"1","kind":"garden","tend_version":"1.0.0"}\n' +
-    '</script>\n' +
-    '<script id="oo-data" type="application/json">\n' +
-    json +
-    '\n</script>\n' +
-    '</body></html>\n'
-  );
-}
-
-async function writeFeatureFile(id: string, data: object): Promise<void> {
-  await writeFile(
-    join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', `${id}.tend.html`),
-    polyglot(data),
-    'utf8',
-  );
-}
-
-async function writeGarden(
-  features: Array<{ id: string; title: string; status: string }> = [],
-): Promise<void> {

-    join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'overview.html'),
-    gardenPolyglot(features),
-    'utf8',
-  );
-}
-
-async function readFeatureData(id: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
-  const text = await readFile(
-    join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', `${id}.tend.html`),
-    'utf8',
-  );
-  const match = /<script id="oo-data" type="application\/json">\n([\s\S]*?)\n<\/script>/.exec(text);
-  if (!match?.[1]) throw new Error(`oo-data not found in ${id}`);
-  return JSON.parse(match[1]) as Record<string, unknown>;
-}
-
-async function readGardenData(): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {

-  const match = /<script id="oo-data" type="application\/json">\n([\s\S]*?)\n<\/script>/.exec(text);

-  return JSON.parse(match[1]) as Record<string, unknown>;
-}
-
-async function featureExists(id: string): Promise<boolean> {

-    await access(join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', `${id}.tend.html`));
-    return true;
-  } catch {
-    return false;
-  }
-}

-// ─── Refusal cases ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-describe('renameFeature — refusal cases', () => {

-// ─── Polyglot builder helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-/** Build a minimal complete polyglot text with a given OO:STYLE body. */
-function buildPolyglot(opts: {
-  id: string;
-  title: string;
-  styleBody?: string;
-  renderBody?: string;
-  clientBody?: string;
-  shellBody?: string;
-  ooDataJson?: string;
-  customZone?: string;
-}): string {
-  const {
-    id,
-    title,
-    styleBody = '/* STALE_STYLE_MARKER */',
-    renderBody = `<div data-render-mount="body-flow"></div>`,
-    clientBody = `<script>/* stale client */</script>`,
-    shellBody = `# OO:SHELL:START\necho stale\n# OO:SHELL:END`,
-    ooDataJson = JSON.stringify({ id, title, status: 'planned' }, null, 2),
-    customZone = '',
-  } = opts;
-
-  const customSection = customZone
-    ? `\n<!-- OO:CUSTOM:START -->\n${customZone}\n<!-- OO:CUSTOM:END -->\n`
-    : '';
-
-  return [
-    '#!/usr/bin/env bash',
-    `# tend feature artifact: ${id}`,
-    `: << 'OO_HTML'`,
-    '<!DOCTYPE html>',
-    '<html lang="en">',
-    '<head>',
-    '<meta charset="utf-8"/>',
-    `<title>${id} · tend</title>`,
-    '',
-    '<!-- OO:STYLE:START -->',
-    styleBody,
-    '<!-- OO:STYLE:END -->',
-    '',
-    '</head>',
-    '<body>',
-    '',
-    '<!-- OO:RENDER:START -->',
-    renderBody,
-    '<!-- OO:RENDER:END -->',
-    '',
-    '<!-- OO:DATA:START -->',
-    `<script id="oo-meta" type="application/json">`,
-    JSON.stringify({ schema_version: '1', kind: 'feature', tend_version: '1.0.0' }, null, 2),
-    '</script>',
-    '',
-    `<script id="oo-data" type="application/json">`,
-    ooDataJson,
-    '</script>',
-    '<!-- OO:DATA:END -->',
-    '',
-    '<!-- OO:CLIENT:START -->',
-    clientBody,
-    '<!-- OO:CLIENT:END -->',
-    customSection,
-    '<script>window.stop();</script>',
-    '</body>',
-    '</html>',
-    'OO_HTML',
-    '',
-    shellBody,
-    '',
-  ].join('\n');
-}
-
-/** Write a polyglot file to the features dir. */
-async function seedPolyglot(id: string, text: string): Promise<void> {
-  await writeFile(join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', `${id}.tend.html`), text, 'utf8');
-}
-
-/** Read the polyglot back. */
-async function readPolyglot(id: string): Promise<string> {
-  return readFile(join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', `${id}.tend.html`), 'utf8');
-}
-
-/** Extract the content between start and end markers (exclusive). */
-function extractSection(text: string, startMarker: string, endMarker: string): string {
-  const start = text.indexOf(startMarker);
-  const end = text.indexOf(endMarker);
-  if (start === -1 || end === -1) return '';
-  return text.slice(start + startMarker.length, end);
-}

-// c003: idempotent skip — second run must not rewrite a polyglot already matching partials
-describe('runSync — idempotent skip (c003)', () => {
-  it('skips polyglot on second run when content already matches canonical partials', async () => {
-    // First run: stale sentinel → file rewritten
-    await seedPolyglot('idem-test', buildPolyglot({ id: 'idem-test', title: 'Idempotent' }));
-    await runSync(tmp);
-
-    // Capture mtime after first run
-    const { stat } = await import('node:fs/promises');
-    const filePath = join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', 'idem-test.tend.html');
-    const mtimeAfterFirst = (await stat(filePath)).mtimeMs;
-
-    // Second run: content now matches partials → file must not be rewritten
-    stdout.length = 0;
-    await runSync(tmp);
-
-    const mtimeAfterSecond = (await stat(filePath)).mtimeMs;
-    // mtime must not change (no write occurred)
-    expect(mtimeAfterSecond).toBe(mtimeAfterFirst);

-    expect(stdout.join('\n')).not.toContain('idem-test');
-  });

-// ─── Diagram re-render (Phase 3 E4) ──────────────────────────────────────────
-//
-// When `tend sync` updates the partials, it must also re-render all
-// media entries with kind === 'diagram' from their stored spec, overwriting
-// entry.content (and updating entry.spec_sha). This is the style-upgrade path:
-// token changes in oo-style.css propagate into stored SVG without manual
-// re-authoring.
-
-/**
- * Canonical SHA-1 of a spec — uses the SHARED canonicalSpecJson (the recursive
- * key-sort the MCP write side-effect also uses), so this asserts sync and the
- * write path agree on spec_sha. A shallow top-level-key-only replacer would
- * drop nested keys (nodes/edges/from/to) and silently diverge from the write
- * path — the bug this test now guards against.
- */
-function specSha(spec: Record<string, unknown>): string {
-  return createHash('sha1').update(canonicalSpecJson(spec)).digest('hex');
-}
-

-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { deriveAuditResult, capAuditResult } from './audit-result.js';
-import type { Feature, AuditVerdict } from './types.js';
-
-const check = (id: string) =>
-  ({ id, description: id, validates: 'what', method: 'synthetic-test', status: 'draft' }) as const;
-
-function f(checks: string[], verdicts: Array<[string, 'pass' | 'partial' | 'fail']>): Pick<Feature, 'checks' | 'audit'> {
-  return {
-    checks: checks.map(check) as Feature['checks'],
-    audit: verdicts.length
-      ? { verdicts: verdicts.map(([check_id, verdict]) => ({ check_id, verdict })) }
-      : undefined,
-  };
-}
-
-describe('deriveAuditResult', () => {
-  it('no verdicts → undefined (no audit result)', () => {
-    expect(deriveAuditResult(f(['c1', 'c2'], []))).toBeUndefined();
-    expect(deriveAuditResult({ checks: [], audit: undefined })).toBeUndefined();
-  });
-
-  it('every check has a pass verdict → pass', () => {
-    expect(deriveAuditResult(f(['c1', 'c2'], [['c1', 'pass'], ['c2', 'pass']]))).toBe('pass');
-  });
-
-  it('any current-check fail → fail', () => {
-    expect(deriveAuditResult(f(['c1', 'c2'], [['c1', 'pass'], ['c2', 'fail']]))).toBe('fail');
-  });
-
-  it('a partial verdict → partial (not pass)', () => {
-    expect(deriveAuditResult(f(['c1', 'c2'], [['c1', 'pass'], ['c2', 'partial']]))).toBe('partial');
-  });
-
-  it('an unverdicted check → partial, NOT pass (the gamed case)', () => {
-    // 3 checks, only 2 have pass verdicts. Hand-set result:pass must not survive.
-    expect(deriveAuditResult(f(['c1', 'c2', 'c3'], [['c1', 'pass'], ['c2', 'pass']]))).toBe('partial');
-  });
-
-  it('orphan verdict (check_id not in checks[]) is ignored, never fails the result', () => {
-    // both real checks pass; a stale orphan c9:fail must not flip result to fail.
-    expect(deriveAuditResult(f(['c1', 'c2'], [['c1', 'pass'], ['c2', 'pass'], ['c9', 'fail']]))).toBe('pass');
-  });
-
-  it('legacy: no checks[] → derive from verdicts alone', () => {
-    expect(deriveAuditResult(f([], [['c1', 'pass'], ['c2', 'pass']]))).toBe('pass');
-    expect(deriveAuditResult(f([], [['c1', 'pass'], ['c2', 'fail']]))).toBe('fail');
-    expect(deriveAuditResult(f([], [['c1', 'pass'], ['c2', 'partial']]))).toBe('partial');
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── deferred verdict semantics ───────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-function deferred(check_id: string): AuditVerdict {
-  return { check_id, verdict: 'deferred', deferred_reason: 'needs human review', deferred_category: 'human' };
-}
-
-function withVerdicts(
-  checkIds: string[],
-  verdicts: AuditVerdict[],
-): Pick<Feature, 'checks' | 'audit'> {
-  return {
-    checks: checkIds.map(check) as Feature['checks'],
-    audit: { verdicts },
-  };
-}
-
-describe('deriveAuditResult — deferred semantics', () => {
-  it('all-pass-except-deferred → pass (deferred excluded from the requirement)', () => {
-    // c1 passes, c2 deferred — deferred is excluded; every non-deferred check passes → pass
-    expect(
-      deriveAuditResult(
-        withVerdicts(['c1', 'c2'], [
-          { check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'pass' },
-          deferred('c2'),
-        ]),
-      ),
-    ).toBe('pass');
-  });
-
-  it('deferred + fail → fail (fail still dominates)', () => {
-    expect(
-      deriveAuditResult(
-        withVerdicts(['c1', 'c2', 'c3'], [
-          { check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'pass' },
-          { check_id: 'c2', verdict: 'fail' },
-          deferred('c3'),
-        ]),
-      ),
-    ).toBe('fail');
-  });
-
-  it('deferred + partial → partial', () => {
-    expect(
-      deriveAuditResult(
-        withVerdicts(['c1', 'c2', 'c3'], [
-          { check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'pass' },
-          { check_id: 'c2', verdict: 'partial' },
-          deferred('c3'),
-        ]),
-      ),
-    ).toBe('partial');
-  });
-
-  it('all-deferred → partial (zero machine-proven checks can never verify)', () => {
-    // No non-deferred check exists → nothing is machine-verified → partial,
-    // NOT a vacuous pass (closes the defer-everything gaming hole).
-    expect(
-      deriveAuditResult(
-        withVerdicts(['c1', 'c2'], [deferred('c1'), deferred('c2')]),
-      ),
-    ).toBe('partial');
-  });
-
-  it('deferred + unverdicted non-deferred check → partial (not pass)', () => {
-    // c1 deferred, c2 has no verdict → unverdicted c2 → partial
-    expect(
-      deriveAuditResult(
-        withVerdicts(['c1', 'c2'], [deferred('c1')]),
-      ),
-    ).toBe('partial');
-  });
-
-  it('existing pass/partial/fail verdicts are unaffected by deferred logic (pass case)', () => {
-    expect(
-      deriveAuditResult(
-        withVerdicts(['c1', 'c2'], [
-          { check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'pass' },
-          { check_id: 'c2', verdict: 'pass' },
-        ]),
-      ),
-    ).toBe('pass');
-  });
-
-  it('existing pass/partial/fail verdicts are unaffected (fail case)', () => {
-    expect(
-      deriveAuditResult(
-        withVerdicts(['c1', 'c2'], [
-          { check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'pass' },
-          { check_id: 'c2', verdict: 'fail' },
-        ]),
-      ),
-    ).toBe('fail');
-  });
-});
-
-describe('capAuditResult', () => {
-  it('caps an over-claim down to the derived value (pass over partial → partial)', () => {
-    expect(capAuditResult('pass', 'partial')).toBe('partial');
-    expect(capAuditResult('pass', 'fail')).toBe('fail');
-  });
-
-  it('preserves a deliberate lower claim (ingester negctrl partial over derived pass)', () => {
-    expect(capAuditResult('partial', 'pass')).toBe('partial');
-    expect(capAuditResult('fail', 'pass')).toBe('fail');
-  });
-
-  it('a coherent pass stays pass', () => {
-    expect(capAuditResult('pass', 'pass')).toBe('pass');
-  });
-
-  it('absent claim uses the derived value', () => {
-    expect(capAuditResult(undefined, 'pass')).toBe('pass');
-  });
-
-  it('no verdicts (derived undefined) → undefined regardless of claim', () => {
-    expect(capAuditResult('pass', undefined)).toBeUndefined();
-  });
-});

-/**
- * audit-compute.ts — the compute-only per-check audit core.
- *
- * `computeAuditResult(featureId, opts)` reads a feature's checks via the core
- * read layer and, for each check carrying a `negctrl` spec, drives the negative
- * control (the bundled `tend negctrl` runner — src/cli/negctrl.ts) to decide whether the cited
- * test discriminates. It assembles a typed AuditResult and performs NO write —
- * the polyglot is never mutated. These tests pin:
- *
- *   - a discriminating check → verdict `pass`, negctrl {ran:true, discriminated:true};
- *   - a non-discriminating check (negctrl exit 1) → verdict capped at `partial`,
- *     negctrl {ran:true, discriminated:false};
- *   - an indeterminate run (negctrl exit 2) → never `pass`;
- *   - ONE real end-to-end run against the on-disk `passing` fixture using the
- *     real negctrl (slow — proves the seam, not a mock);
- *   - the compute-only invariant: the fixture polyglot's oo-data is byte-identical
- *     before vs after, and audit-compute.ts imports zero write-path symbols.
- *
- * The fast verdict-assembly cases stub the negctrl runner at the documented seam
- * (`opts.negctrlRunner`); the AuditResult assembly, the discriminator gate, and
- * the compute-only guarantee are exercised for real.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
-import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { computeAuditResult, type NegctrlOutcome, type NegctrlRunner } from './audit-compute.js';
-import { AuditResultSchema } from './plan.js';
-import { readFeature } from '../files.js';
-// Test files are exempt from the layering invariant (layering.test.ts excludes *.test.ts).
-// The real end-to-end test needs the actual negctrl runner from the CLI layer.
-import { runNegctrl } from '../../cli/negctrl.js';
-
-const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);
-const __dirname = dirname(__filename);
-const REPO_ROOT = join(__dirname, '..', '..', '..');
-const FIXTURES = join(REPO_ROOT, 'tests', 'fixtures', 'audit-emit');
-const PASSING = join(FIXTURES, 'passing');
-const NON_DISCRIMINATING = join(FIXTURES, 'non-discriminating');
-
-/** A stub runner that always reports the given exit code (no real worktree). */
-function stubRunner(exitCode: 0 | 1 | 2 | null): NegctrlRunner {
-  return (): NegctrlOutcome => ({ exitCode, stdout: `stub exit ${exitCode}` });
-}
-
-describe('computeAuditResult — verdict assembly (stubbed negctrl seam)', () => {
-  it('a discriminating check yields verdict pass + negctrl {ran:true, discriminated:true}', async () => {
-    const result = await computeAuditResult('__fixture__', {
-      cwd: PASSING,
-      negctrlRunner: stubRunner(0),
-    });
-    AuditResultSchema.parse(result); // schema-valid
-    expect(result.verdicts).toHaveLength(1);
-    const v = result.verdicts[0]!;
-    expect(v.check).toBe('c1');
-    expect(v.verdict).toBe('pass');
-    expect(v.negctrl).toEqual({ ran: true, discriminated: true });
-  });
-
-  it('a non-discriminating check (negctrl exit 1) caps the verdict at partial', async () => {
-    const result = await computeAuditResult('__fixture__', {
-      cwd: NON_DISCRIMINATING,
-      negctrlRunner: stubRunner(1),
-    });
-    const v = result.verdicts[0]!;
-    expect(v.negctrl).toEqual({ ran: true, discriminated: false });
-    expect(v.verdict).not.toBe('pass');
-    expect(v.verdict).toBe('partial');
-  });
-
-  it('an indeterminate negctrl run (exit 2) is never pass', async () => {
-    const result = await computeAuditResult('__fixture__', {
-      cwd: PASSING,
-      negctrlRunner: stubRunner(2),
-    });
-    const v = result.verdicts[0]!;
-    expect(v.verdict).not.toBe('pass');
-    // exit 2 = the control could not run → ran false, discriminated false.
-    expect(v.negctrl).toEqual({ ran: false, discriminated: false });
-  });
-
-  it('returns a plain serialisable object (drift defaults to [])', async () => {
-    const result = await computeAuditResult('__fixture__', {
-      cwd: PASSING,
-      negctrlRunner: stubRunner(0),
-    });
-    expect(Array.isArray(result.drift)).toBe(true);
-    expect(() => structuredClone(result)).not.toThrow();
-  });
-});
-
-describe('computeAuditResult — real negctrl end-to-end (slow)', () => {
-  it(
-    'drives the REAL negctrl against the passing fixture → pass + discriminated',
-    async () => {
-      // Inject the real CLI runner — the seam is the only path to the worktree.
-      const negctrlRunner: NegctrlRunner = (spec, cwd) => {
-        let stdout = '';
-        const code = runNegctrl(
-          ['--file', spec.file, '--find', spec.find, '--replace', spec.replace, '--test', spec.test],
-          cwd,
-          (s) => { stdout += s; },
-        );
-        const exitCode: 0 | 1 | 2 | null =
-          code === 0 ? 0 : code === 1 ? 1 : code === 2 ? 2 : null;
-        return { exitCode, stdout };
-      };
-      const result = await computeAuditResult('__fixture__', { cwd: PASSING, negctrlRunner });
-      AuditResultSchema.parse(result);
-      const v = result.verdicts[0]!;
-      expect(v.negctrl).toEqual({ ran: true, discriminated: true });
-      expect(v.verdict).toBe('pass');
-    },
-    180_000,
-  );
-});
-
-describe('computeAuditResult — compute-only invariant', () => {
-  it('does not mutate the fixture polyglot (oo-data byte-identical before vs after)', async () => {
-    const before = await readFeature('__fixture__', PASSING);
-    await computeAuditResult('__fixture__', { cwd: PASSING, negctrlRunner: stubRunner(0) });
-    const after = await readFeature('__fixture__', PASSING);
-    // No audit was written, status unchanged, the whole oo-data is identical.
-    expect(after).toEqual(before);
-    expect(after.audit).toBeUndefined();
-    expect(after.status).toBe(before.status);
-  });
-
-  it('audit-compute.ts imports no write-path symbol (static guard)', () => {
-    const src = readFileSync(join(__dirname, 'audit-compute.ts'), 'utf8');
-    for (const forbidden of [
-      'tend_update_feature',
-      'spliceOoData',
-      'writeFeature',
-      'writePolyglotAtomic',
-      'writeGardenPolyglot',
-    ]) {
-      expect(src, `audit-compute.ts must not reference ${forbidden}`).not.toContain(forbidden);
-    }
-  });
-});
-
-// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-// P0.2 / D5 — recipe floor: audit-compute refuses pass on trivial recipes
-//
-// Current: verdictForCheck in audit-compute.ts only gates on negctrl bits.
-//   A check whose verification_recipe is "check manually" (< 20 chars or
-//   matching the trivial pattern) can receive a `pass` verdict if negctrl
-//   discriminates. The recipe floor is not enforced at compute time.
-//
-// Target: verdictForCheck (or the computeAuditResult call site) adds a
-//   recipe-floor gate BEFORE accepting negctrl bits:
-//   - recipe.trim().length < 20  → cap at partial, reason: 'trivial recipe (<20 chars)'
-//   - recipe matches TRIVIAL_RE  → cap at partial, reason: 'trivial recipe (matches trivial pattern)'
-//   TRIVIAL_RE = /^(check( it)? manually|it works|tests? pass(es)?|run (the )?tests?|manual(ly)?|works)\b/i
-//   (finalized list; open to extension in Phase 1.5)
-//
-// This is NOT a write-block, NOT a validate error. It is an audit-compute
-// enforcement only: the skill tend-audit gains the same instruction in Phase 1.5.
-//
-// Enforcement point: verdictForCheck (pure) — check phase, before accepting bits.
-// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-const TRIVIAL_RECIPE = join(FIXTURES, 'trivial-recipe');
-
-describe('D5 — recipe floor: trivial recipe caps verdict at partial (RED, P0.2/D5)', () => {
-  // RED (P0.2/D5)
-  it(
-    'a discriminating negctrl is capped at partial when verification_recipe is "check manually" (matches trivial pattern)',
-    async () => {
-      // The trivial-recipe fixture has the same negctrl spec as `passing`
-      // (discrimination succeeds) but recipe = "check manually".
-      // Today: computeAuditResult returns 'pass' because only negctrl bits gate it.
-      // After fix: recipe floor intercepts and returns 'partial' with a reason.
-      const result = await computeAuditResult('__fixture__', {
-        cwd: TRIVIAL_RECIPE,
-        negctrlRunner: stubRunner(0), // discriminates (exit 0)
-      });
-
-      const v = result.verdicts[0]!;
-      // Recipe floor must cap at partial — 'pass' is the wrong answer here.
-      expect(v.verdict).toBe('partial');
-      // The reason must mention the trivial recipe.
-      expect(v.reasons.some((r) => /trivial|recipe|manual/i.test(r))).toBe(true);
-    },
-  );
-
-  // RED (P0.2/D5)
-  it(
-    'a recipe under 20 chars caps at partial even if it is not in the trivial-pattern list',
-    async () => {
-      // This uses the stubbed runner to test the floor at the unit level.
-      // We need a check fixture in memory; since computeAuditResult reads from disk,
-      // we test the exported recipe-floor predicate directly (Phase 1.5 exports it).
-
-      const { isTrivialRecipe } = await import('./audit-compute.js');
-
-      // Under 20 chars, not matching the pattern → still trivial by length.
-      expect(isTrivialRecipe('run test')).toBe(true);          // < 20 chars
-      expect(isTrivialRecipe('check manually')).toBe(true);    // pattern match
-      expect(isTrivialRecipe('it works')).toBe(true);          // pattern match
-      expect(isTrivialRecipe('tests pass')).toBe(true);        // pattern match
-      expect(isTrivialRecipe('works')).toBe(true);             // pattern match
-      // Substantive recipes (>= 20 chars, no pattern match) must return false.
-      expect(isTrivialRecipe('Run vitest -t "c1" and confirm it flips red when the sum line is broken.')).toBe(false);
-    },
-  );
-
-  // This invariant holds today AND must hold after D5 is fixed.
-  it(
-    'a substantive recipe (>=20 chars, no trivial pattern) does not block a pass verdict',
-    async () => {
-      // The standard passing fixture has a non-trivial recipe (>20 chars).
-      // This test passes today; it must still pass after the recipe floor is added.
-      const result = await computeAuditResult('__fixture__', {
-        cwd: PASSING,
-        negctrlRunner: stubRunner(0),
-      });
-      const v = result.verdicts[0]!;
-      expect(v.verdict).toBe('pass');
-    },
-  );
-});

deleted file mode 100644
index d6f94e5..0000000
--- a/src/core/bridge/emit.test.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,86 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * emit.ts — delimited AuditResult emit/extract round-trip tests.
- *
- * The egress contract (docs/bridge/tend-umbel-build-spec.md §3 + §5): the audit
- * WORKER prints its AuditResult as the final stdout message wrapped in a stable
- * sentinel-delimited block, and the conductor recovers it via `extractJson` even
- * when the worker emitted prose before and after the block. These tests pin:
- *
- *   - emit → extract → AuditResultSchema.parse round-trips an AuditResult intact;
- *   - extraction survives leading + trailing prose around the block;
- *   - when two blocks are present, the LAST wins (final stdout is the answer).
- *
- * Pure functions, no I/O — the whole file is deterministic.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { emitAuditResult, extractJson } from './emit.js';
-import { AuditResultSchema, type AuditResult } from './plan.js';
-
-const sampleResult: AuditResult = {
-  verdicts: [
-    {
-      check: 'c1',
-      verdict: 'pass',
-      negctrl: { ran: true, discriminated: true },
-      reasons: [],
-    },
-  ],
-  drift: [],
-};
-
-describe('emitAuditResult + extractJson — delimited round-trip', () => {
-  it('emits a block extractJson recovers, parsing back to the original AuditResult', () => {
-    const block = emitAuditResult(sampleResult);
-    const parsed = AuditResultSchema.parse(extractJson(block));
-    expect(parsed).toEqual(sampleResult);
-  });
-
-  it('recovers the block when surrounded by leading and trailing prose', () => {
-    const block = emitAuditResult(sampleResult);
-    const noisy = `chatter line 1\nthinking...\n${block}\ntrailing prose\nbye\n`;
-    const parsed = AuditResultSchema.parse(extractJson(noisy));
-    expect(parsed).toEqual(sampleResult);
-  });
-
-  it('recovers the LAST block when two are present (final stdout wins)', () => {
-    const first: AuditResult = {
-      verdicts: [{ check: 'old', verdict: 'fail', reasons: ['stale attempt'] }],
-      drift: [],
-    };
-    const second: AuditResult = {
-      verdicts: [{ check: 'new', verdict: 'pass', negctrl: { ran: true, discriminated: true }, reasons: [] }],
-      drift: [],
-    };
-    const noisy = `${emitAuditResult(first)}\n...retry...\n${emitAuditResult(second)}\n`;
-    const parsed = AuditResultSchema.parse(extractJson(noisy));
-    expect(parsed.verdicts[0]!.check).toBe('new');
-  });
-
-  it('throws when no delimited block is present (no silent empty parse)', () => {
-    expect(() => extractJson('just prose, no block here')).toThrow();
-  });
-
-  it('recovers the full JSON when a verdict reason contains an inner ``` fence', () => {
-    // A finding/reason that quotes a fenced code snippet embeds a bare triple-
-    // backtick inside a JSON string value. A naive first-`CLOSE` scan slices at
-    // that inner fence → unterminated/invalid JSON. The real closing fence is the
-    // newline-anchored one the wrap emits, so the body must survive intact.
-    const fenced: AuditResult = {
-      verdicts: [
-        {
-          check: 'c1',
-          verdict: 'fail',
-          reasons: ['test did not exercise the unit; repro:\n```\nnpx vitest run x\n```\nstill passes against a mock'],
-        },
-      ],
-      drift: [],
-    };
-    const block = emitAuditResult(fenced);
-    const parsed = AuditResultSchema.parse(extractJson(block));
-    expect(parsed).toEqual(fenced);
-    expect(parsed.verdicts[0]!.reasons[0]).toContain('```');
-  });
-});
diff --git a/src/core/bridge/ingester.test.ts b/src/core/bridge/ingester.test.ts

index 9854a61..0000000
--- a/src/core/bridge/ingester.test.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,427 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * Tests for the deterministic ingester — the single tend writer for the conductor.
- *
- * Source of record: docs/bridge/tend-umbel-build-spec.md §4 (the tend seam).
- *
- * Four behaviours, all grounded in tend's real data model:
- *
- *   - deriveResult: the roll-up rule + the negctrl-enforcement hardening. A pass
- *     requires every verdict 'pass' AND every one negctrl-discriminated; any
- *     'fail' → 'fail'; everything else → 'partial'. Pure, table-driven.
- *   - mapVerdicts: rename the neutral AuditResult verdict shape onto tend's
- *     stored AuditVerdict (check → check_id, evidencePath → evidence_path, …).
- *   - readClosed: read the garden's denormalized features_aggregate and return
- *     exactly the verified-status ids. Reads via tend's canonical garden helper
- *     (readCatalog), NOT a raw file parse.
- *   - emitVerdict: map → derive → write through tend's REAL gated update path →
- *     read back the status tend recorded. The negctrl-enforcement is the load-
- *     bearing case: an undiscriminated pass derives 'partial', so tend's
- *     verified⇐pass gate refuses verified and the call returns {closed:false}.
- *
- * The write goes through applyFeatureUpdate + writeFeature — the same gated core
- * the tend_update_feature MCP tool calls under the hood — so the verified gate is
- * exercised live against a real feature polyglot on disk, never mocked.
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
-import { mkdtemp, mkdir, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { join } from 'node:path';
-import { readFeature, writeFeature, writeCatalog } from '../files.js';
-import type { AuditResult, Verdict } from './plan.js';
-import { AuditResultSchema, VerdictSchema } from './plan.js';
-import type { Catalog, Check, Feature } from '../types.js';
-import { deriveResult, mapVerdicts, readClosed, emitVerdict } from './ingester.js';
-
-// ─── Fixtures ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-/** A discriminated pass verdict — the only kind that can roll up to 'pass'. */
-function passDiscriminated(check: string): AuditResult['verdicts'][number] {
-  return {
-    check,
-    verdict: 'pass',
-    negctrl: { ran: true, discriminated: true },
-    evidencePath: `tests/${check}.test.ts`,
-    reasons: [],
-  };
-}
-
-function auditResult(verdicts: AuditResult['verdicts']): AuditResult {
-  return AuditResultSchema.parse({ verdicts, drift: [] });
-}
-
-/** A done Verdict carrying an AuditResult as its output. */
-function doneVerdict(node: string, output: unknown): Verdict {
-  return VerdictSchema.parse({
-    node,
-    status: 'done',
-    output,
-    evidence: { filesTouched: [] },
-    attempts: 1,
-  });
-}
-
-function makeCatalog(overrides: Partial<Catalog> = {}): Catalog {
-  return {
-    schema_version: '1',
-    project_id: 'test',
-    status: 'draft',
-    features: [],
-    ...overrides,
-  };
-}
-
-/** Create a unique temp project root for each test. */
-async function makeProjectRoot(): Promise<string> {
-  const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'tend-ingester-'));
-  await mkdir(join(root, 'docs', 'tend', 'features'), { recursive: true });
-  return root;
-}
-
-/**
- * Scaffold a real in-progress feature polyglot on disk with the given check ids,
- * plus the garden so writeFeature can stamp the breadcrumb. Returns the root.
- * The feature is written as a true polyglot (writeFeature assembles it from the
- * canonical partials), so the gate runs against a real artifact.
- */
-async function seedFeature(
-  root: string,
-  id: string,
-  checkIds: string[],
-): Promise<void> {
-  const checks: Check[] = checkIds.map((cid) => ({
-    id: cid,
-    description: `check ${cid}`,
-    validates: 'what',
-    method: 'synthetic-test',
-  }));
-  const feature: Feature = {
-    id,
-    title: id,
-    status: 'in-progress',
-    what: 'a thing',
-    checks,
-  };
-  // Garden first so writeFeature finds a project_name; then the feature, and
-  // register it in the catalog so readClosed sees it via features_aggregate.
-  await writeCatalog(
-    makeCatalog({ features: [{ id, title: id, status: 'in-progress' }] }),
-    root,
-  );
-  await writeFeature(feature, root);
-}
-
-// ─── deriveResult ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('deriveResult', () => {
-  type Verdicts = AuditResult['verdicts'];
-
-  const cases: Array<{ name: string; verdicts: Verdicts; expected: 'pass' | 'partial' | 'fail' }> = [
-    {
-      name: "all pass + all discriminated → 'pass'",
-      verdicts: [passDiscriminated('c1'), passDiscriminated('c2')],
-      expected: 'pass',
-    },
-    {
-      name: "any fail → 'fail' (even alongside discriminated passes)",
-      verdicts: [passDiscriminated('c1'), { check: 'c2', verdict: 'fail', reasons: [] }],
-      expected: 'fail',
-    },
-    {
-      name: "all pass but one negctrl.discriminated:false → 'partial'",
-      verdicts: [
-        passDiscriminated('c1'),
-        { check: 'c2', verdict: 'pass', negctrl: { ran: true, discriminated: false }, reasons: [] },
-      ],
-      expected: 'partial',
-    },
-    {
-      name: "all pass but one negctrl absent → 'partial'",
-      verdicts: [passDiscriminated('c1'), { check: 'c2', verdict: 'pass', reasons: [] }],
-      expected: 'partial',
-    },
-    {
-      name: "a partial verdict among passes → 'partial'",
-      verdicts: [passDiscriminated('c1'), { check: 'c2', verdict: 'partial', reasons: [] }],
-      expected: 'partial',
-    },
-  ];
-
-  for (const { name, verdicts, expected } of cases) {
-    it(name, () => {
-      expect(deriveResult(auditResult(verdicts).verdicts)).toBe(expected);
-    });
-  }
-});
-
-// ─── mapVerdicts ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('mapVerdicts', () => {
-  it('renames the neutral verdict shape onto tend AuditVerdict, field by field', () => {
-    const ar = auditResult([
-      {
-        check: 'c1',
-        verdict: 'pass',
-        negctrl: { ran: true, discriminated: true },
-        evidencePath: 't.ts',
-        evidenceSha: 'ab',
-        validatesJobSatisfied: true,
-        reasons: [],
-      },
-    ]);
-
-    const mapped = mapVerdicts(ar);
-
-    expect(mapped).toHaveLength(1);
-    expect(mapped[0]).toEqual({
-      check_id: 'c1',
-      verdict: 'pass',
-      evidence_path: 't.ts',
-      evidence_sha: 'ab',
-      validates_job_satisfied: true,
-    });
-    // negctrl is NOT carried — tend's stored AuditVerdict has no structured
-    // negctrl field yet ([ROADMAP], build-spec §4). The discriminated bit lives
-    // only in the derived result.
-    expect(mapped[0]).not.toHaveProperty('negctrl');
-  });
-
-  it('maps one element per input verdict, preserving order', () => {
-    const ar = auditResult([
-      { check: 'c1', verdict: 'pass', negctrl: { ran: true, discriminated: true }, reasons: [] },
-      { check: 'c2', verdict: 'fail', reasons: [] },
-    ]);
-    const mapped = mapVerdicts(ar);
-    expect(mapped.map((m) => m.check_id)).toEqual(['c1', 'c2']);
-    expect(mapped.map((m) => m.verdict)).toEqual(['pass', 'fail']);
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── readClosed ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('readClosed', () => {
-  let root: string;
-
-  beforeEach(async () => { root = await makeProjectRoot(); });
-  afterEach(async () => { await rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true }); });
-
-  it("returns exactly the verified-status ids from the garden's features_aggregate", async () => {
-    await writeCatalog(
-      makeCatalog({
-        features: [
-          { id: 'a', title: 'A', status: 'verified' },
-          { id: 'b', title: 'B', status: 'in-progress' },
-          { id: 'c', title: 'C', status: 'planned' },
-        ],
-      }),
-      root,
-    );
-
-    const closed = await readClosed(root);
-
-    expect(closed).toEqual(new Set(['a']));
-    expect(closed.has('b')).toBe(false);
-    expect(closed.has('c')).toBe(false);
-  });
-
-  it('returns an empty Set when the aggregate is empty', async () => {
-    await writeCatalog(makeCatalog({ features: [] }), root);
-    const closed = await readClosed(root);
-    expect(closed).toEqual(new Set());
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── emitVerdict — verified path ──────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('emitVerdict — verified path', () => {
-  let root: string;
-
-  beforeEach(async () => { root = await makeProjectRoot(); });
-  afterEach(async () => { await rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true }); });
-
-  it('all-pass + every negctrl.discriminated → tend verifies the feature, returns {closed:true}', async () => {
-    await seedFeature(root, 'feat-x', ['c1', 'c2']);
-
-    const v = doneVerdict(
-      'feat-x',
-      auditResult([passDiscriminated('c1'), passDiscriminated('c2')]),
-    );
-
-    const out = await emitVerdict(v, root);
-
-    expect(out).toEqual({ closed: true });
-    const after = await readFeature('feat-x', root);
-    expect(after.audit?.result).toBe('pass');
-    expect(after.status).toBe('verified');
-  });
-
-  it('a non-done verdict closes nothing and writes nothing', async () => {
-    await seedFeature(root, 'feat-x', ['c1']);
-
-    const failed = VerdictSchema.parse({
-      node: 'feat-x',
-      status: 'failed',
-      output: auditResult([passDiscriminated('c1')]),
-      evidence: { filesTouched: [] },
-      attempts: 1,
-    });
-
-    const out = await emitVerdict(failed, root);
-
-    expect(out).toEqual({ closed: false });
-    const after = await readFeature('feat-x', root);
-    expect(after.audit).toBeUndefined();
-    expect(after.status).toBe('in-progress');
-  });
-
-  it('a done verdict whose output is not an AuditResult closes nothing and writes nothing', async () => {
-    await seedFeature(root, 'feat-x', ['c1']);
-
-    const notAudit = doneVerdict('feat-x', { some: 'other shape' });
-
-    const out = await emitVerdict(notAudit, root);
-
-    expect(out).toEqual({ closed: false });
-    const after = await readFeature('feat-x', root);
-    expect(after.audit).toBeUndefined();
-    expect(after.status).toBe('in-progress');
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── emitVerdict — partial & fail gating ──────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('emitVerdict — partial & fail gating', () => {
-  let root: string;
-
-  beforeEach(async () => { root = await makeProjectRoot(); });
-  afterEach(async () => { await rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true }); });
-
-  // The load-bearing case: an undiscriminated pass can never reach verified.
-  it('NEGCTRL-ENFORCEMENT: an all-pass-but-non-discriminated AuditResult derives partial → NOT verified, {closed:false}', async () => {
-    await seedFeature(root, 'feat-x', ['c1', 'c2']);
-
-    const v = doneVerdict(
-      'feat-x',
-      auditResult([
-        passDiscriminated('c1'),
-        { check: 'c2', verdict: 'pass', negctrl: { ran: true, discriminated: false }, reasons: [] },
-      ]),
-    );
-
-    const out = await emitVerdict(v, root);
-
-    expect(out).toEqual({ closed: false });
-    const after = await readFeature('feat-x', root);
-    expect(after.audit?.result).toBe('partial');
-    expect(after.status).not.toBe('verified');
-    expect(after.status).toBe('in-progress');
-  });
-
-  it("FAIL: an AuditResult containing any 'fail' derives fail → NOT verified, {closed:false}", async () => {
-    await seedFeature(root, 'feat-x', ['c1', 'c2']);
-
-    const v = doneVerdict(
-      'feat-x',
-      auditResult([
-        passDiscriminated('c1'),
-        { check: 'c2', verdict: 'fail', reasons: ['the unit is broken'] },
-      ]),
-    );
-
-    const out = await emitVerdict(v, root);
-
-    expect(out).toEqual({ closed: false });
-    const after = await readFeature('feat-x', root);
-    expect(after.audit?.result).toBe('fail');
-    expect(after.status).not.toBe('verified');
-    expect(after.status).toBe('in-progress');
-  });
-
-  // The ingester omits `status` on a non-pass (the transition guard rejects an
-  // in-progress no-op). A previously-VERIFIED feature must still be demoted when
-  // a non-pass audit lands — that fall-out-of-verified is what tend's
-  // enforceVerifiedInvariant guarantees, and the ingester depends on it.
-  it('demotes an already-verified feature to in-progress on a non-discriminated pass, {closed:false}', async () => {
-    // Seed a feature ALREADY at status verified with a passing audit on disk.
-    await writeCatalog(
-      makeCatalog({ features: [{ id: 'feat-v', title: 'feat-v', status: 'verified' }] }),
-      root,
-    );
-    await writeFeature(
-      {
-        id: 'feat-v',
-        title: 'feat-v',
-        status: 'verified',
-        what: 'a thing',
-        checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'check c1', validates: 'what', method: 'synthetic-test' }],
-        audit: { result: 'pass', verdicts: [{ check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'pass' }] },
-      },
-      root,
-    );
-
-    const v = doneVerdict(
-      'feat-v',
-      auditResult([
-        { check: 'c1', verdict: 'pass', negctrl: { ran: true, discriminated: false }, reasons: [] },
-      ]),
-    );
-
-    const out = await emitVerdict(v, root);
-
-    expect(out).toEqual({ closed: false });
-    const after = await readFeature('feat-v', root);
-    expect(after.audit?.result).toBe('partial');
-    expect(after.status).toBe('in-progress');
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── deriveResult — deferred exclusion ────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('deriveResult — deferred excluded from all-pass requirement', () => {
-  // deriveResult operates on the bridge AuditResult's verdicts, which only
-  // have 'pass' | 'partial' | 'fail' (the bridge schema hasn't changed — deferred

-  let root: string;

-      },
-      root,

-    // Now emit a discriminated pass for c1 via the ingester
-    const v = doneVerdict(

-    // The ingester merges its verdicts with the existing audit. After this:

-    const out = await emitVerdict(v, root);

-    expect(out).toEqual({ closed: true });

-/**

- * The schema is the co-owned neutral contract between tend and umbel, vendored

- * tests pin the three behaviours the bridge depends on:
- *
- *   - every `work` variant round-trips (prompt | {test,phases} | command);
- *   - an AuditResult round-trips with a three-valued verdict + negctrl bits;
- *   - a Verdict cannot carry an agent-authored `verified` key — the union is
- *     mechanical-status-only, so zod strips it.
- *
- * Also asserts the single-source invariant (i003): exactly one definition of
- * each *Schema lives under src/. The downstream consumers don't exist yet, so
- * their import assertions are it.todo placeholders — never faked green.

-
-// ── i003: single-source invariant ────────────────────────────────────────────
-//
-// Exactly one definition of each *Schema may exist under src/. A second copy is
-// the failure mode this guard exists to catch — two parallel sources of truth
-// drift silently. We scan src/ text for `export { ... as PlanSchema }` style
-// re-exports and `const Plan = z` definitions.
-//
-// negctrl: add a second `export { Foo as PlanSchema }` line anywhere under src/
-//   → this test must fail → DISCRIMINATES.
-describe('i003 — single source of truth for the bridge schemas', () => {
-  // Walk src/ collecting .ts file contents (excluding test files, which only
-  // import the schemas, never define them).
-  function srcFiles(): string[] {
-    // Resolve via the build-spec-adjacent module: the schema lives in this dir.
-    // Read the bridge module + scan siblings by reading the directory tree.
-    const { readdirSync } = require('node:fs') as typeof import('node:fs');
-    const out: string[] = [];
-    const walk = (dir: string): void => {
-      for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
-        const full = join(dir, entry.name);
-        if (entry.isDirectory()) {
-          if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === 'dist') continue;
-          walk(full);
-        } else if (entry.name.endsWith('.ts') && !entry.name.endsWith('.test.ts')) {
-          out.push(full);
-        }
-      }
-    };
-    walk(join(REPO_ROOT, 'src'));
-    return out;
-  }
-
-  it('defines each schema exactly once under src/', () => {
-    const files = srcFiles();
-    for (const schemaName of ['PlanSchema', 'NodeSchema', 'VerdictSchema', 'AuditResultSchema']) {
-      const defining = files.filter((f) => {
-        const src = readFileSync(f, 'utf8');
-        // A *definition* is the `as <Schema>` export alias (§1 emits exactly one).
-        return src.includes(`as ${schemaName}`);
-      });
-      expect(defining, `${schemaName} defined in: ${defining.join(', ')}`).toHaveLength(1);
-      expect(defining[0]).toBe(join(REPO_ROOT, 'src', 'core', 'bridge', 'plan.ts'));
-    }
-  });
-
-  // Consumer-import assertions: each downstream consumer must import these
-  // schemas from src/core/bridge/plan.ts — zero second copies.
-  it('src/adapters/umbel imports the schemas from src/core/bridge/plan.ts', () => {
-    const src = readFileSync(
-      join(REPO_ROOT, 'src', 'adapters', 'umbel', 'generator.ts'),
-      'utf8',
-    );
-    // The adapter lives at src/adapters/umbel/, so it reaches the single source
-    // via ../../core/bridge/plan.js — the same module, no second copy.
-    expect(src).toMatch(/from '\.\.\/\.\.\/core\/bridge\/plan\.js'/);
-    for (const schemaName of ['PlanSchema', 'NodeSchema', 'VerdictSchema', 'AuditResultSchema']) {
-      expect(src.includes(`as ${schemaName}`)).toBe(false);
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('src/core/bridge/ingester.ts imports the schemas from src/core/bridge/plan.ts', () => {
-    const src = readFileSync(
-      join(REPO_ROOT, 'src', 'core', 'bridge', 'ingester.ts'),
-      'utf8',
-    );
-    // Imports the schema module from the single source.
-    expect(src).toMatch(/from '\.\/plan\.js'/);
-    // Defines no second copy of any *Schema (the single-source invariant above
-    // already enforces this project-wide; this pins it on the ingester too).
-    for (const schemaName of ['PlanSchema', 'NodeSchema', 'VerdictSchema', 'AuditResultSchema']) {
-      expect(src.includes(`as ${schemaName}`)).toBe(false);
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('the audit-emit compute path imports the AuditResult type from src/core/bridge/plan.ts', () => {
-    const src = readFileSync(
-      join(REPO_ROOT, 'src', 'core', 'bridge', 'audit-compute.ts'),
-      'utf8',
-    );
-    // Pulls the AuditResult shape from the single source — no second copy.
-    expect(src).toMatch(/from '\.\/plan\.js'/);
-    for (const schemaName of ['PlanSchema', 'NodeSchema', 'VerdictSchema', 'AuditResultSchema']) {
-      expect(src.includes(`as ${schemaName}`)).toBe(false);
-    }
-  });
-});

-// ─── Fixture builders ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-function emptyCatalog(): Catalog {

-    project_id: 't',
-    status: 'draft',
-    features: [],
-  };

-
-function persona(id: string, jobs?: string[]): CatalogPersona {

-  if (jobs) out.jobs = jobs;

-function opp(id: string, overrides?: Partial<CatalogOpportunity>): CatalogOpportunity {

-function graph(

-    existing_paths?: Set<string>;
-    existing_polyglots?: Set<string>;

-  if (opts.personas) catalog.personas = opts.personas;
-  if (opts.opportunities) catalog.opportunities = opts.opportunities;
-  if (opts.journey_phases) catalog.journey_phases = opts.journey_phases;
-  const g: ConstraintGraph = { features, catalog };
-  if (opts.existing_paths) g.existing_paths = opts.existing_paths;
-  if (opts.existing_polyglots) g.existing_polyglots = opts.existing_polyglots;
-  return g;
-}
-
-function find(violations: ReturnType<typeof allViolations>, id: ConstraintId, node?: string) {

-    expect(hit).toBeDefined();

-  it('returns empty array for a clean feature (slot checked, step has Test:, check has recipe)', () => {

-    const f = feature({

-      parent: 'parent-feat',

-      what: 'A capability',

-      checks: [
-        {
-          id: 'c1',
-          description: 'verifies what',
-          validates: 'what',
-          verification_recipe: 'Run vitest -t "c1"',
-        },
-      ],
-      steps: [

-          description: 'Test: assert X in foo.test.ts. Implement: write code.',
-          traces_to: ['c1'],

-});

-/**
- * diagram.test.ts — acceptance tests for renderDiagram (editorial layer E2).
- *
- * Owns ed-c003 (byte-identical determinism) and ed-c004 (token-only colors).
- *
- * Golden-file strategy: each spec_type fixture renders to a stored .svg golden
- * under ./golden-diagrams/. The test asserts the live render equals the stored
- * golden byte-for-byte. To (re)generate goldens after an intentional layout
- * change, run with UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 — then eyeball the diff before committing.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
-import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
-import {
-  renderDiagram,
-  DiagramError,
-  type FlowSpec,
-  type LayersSpec,
-  type JourneySpec,
-  type CompareSpec,
-  type AnatomySpec,
-  type DiagramSpec,
-} from './index.js';
-
-const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
-const GOLDEN_DIR = join(HERE, 'golden-diagrams');
-const UPDATE = process.env['UPDATE_GOLDENS'] === '1';
-
-function goldenPath(name: string): string {
-  return join(GOLDEN_DIR, `${name}.svg`);
-}
-
-/** Assert a live render matches its stored golden (regenerating when asked). */
-function expectGolden(name: string, svg: string): void {
-  if (UPDATE) {
-    if (!existsSync(GOLDEN_DIR)) mkdirSync(GOLDEN_DIR, { recursive: true });
-    writeFileSync(goldenPath(name), svg);
-    return;
-  }
-  const golden = readFileSync(goldenPath(name), 'utf8');
-  expect(svg).toBe(golden);
-}
-
-// ── Fixtures (neutral ids, contract-sized: ≤6 nodes/bands) ──────────────────
-
-const FLOW: FlowSpec = {
-  spec_type: 'flow',
-  nodes: [
-    { id: 'n1', label: 'request' },
-    { id: 'n2', label: 'validate token' },
-    { id: 'n3', label: 'fetch user' },
-    { id: 'n4', label: 'respond' },
-  ],
-  edges: [
-    { from: 'n1', to: 'n2', label: 'parse' },
-    { from: 'n2', to: 'n3' },
-    { from: 'n3', to: 'n4' },
-  ],
-};
-
-// Same graph, nodes + edges supplied in a different input order. Topologically
-// identical to FLOW — the dagre layout must produce the same geometry.
-const FLOW_REORDERED: FlowSpec = {
-  spec_type: 'flow',
-  nodes: [
-    { id: 'n3', label: 'fetch user' },
-    { id: 'n1', label: 'request' },
-    { id: 'n4', label: 'respond' },
-    { id: 'n2', label: 'validate token' },
-  ],
-  edges: [
-    { from: 'n3', to: 'n4' },
-    { from: 'n2', to: 'n3' },
-    { from: 'n1', to: 'n2', label: 'parse' },

-
-const LAYERS: LayersSpec = {

-const JOURNEY: JourneySpec = {

-// ── ed-c004: token-only colors (the contract banned-list) ──────────────────

-const HEX = /#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,6}/;
-const NAMED = /\b(white|black|gray|grey|rgb\()/;

-describe('renderDiagram — ed-c004 token-only colors', () => {
-  for (const [name, spec] of Object.entries(FIXTURES)) {
-    it(`${name}: every color is a var(--token), no banned constructs`, () => {

-      expect(svg).not.toMatch(EFFECTS);
-      expect(svg).not.toMatch(DYNAMIC);

-      // Every fill= / stroke= attribute value is a var(--…) ref. (currentColor,
-      // raw hex, or named colors would all fail.)
-      const colorAttrs = svg.match(/(?:fill|stroke)="([^"]*)"/g) ?? [];
-      expect(colorAttrs.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
-      for (const attr of colorAttrs) {
-        const value = attr.replace(/^(?:fill|stroke)="/, '').replace(/"$/, '');

-        expect(value).toMatch(/^var\(--[\w-]+\)$/);

-
-// ── ed-c003: byte-identical determinism ─────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('renderDiagram — ed-c003 determinism', () => {

-// ─── generateExecutionPlan (shared orchestration: MCP tool + CLI) ──────────────
-//
-// generateExecutionPlan is the single orchestration both tend_output_execution_plan
-// (MCP) and `tend execute` (CLI) call. It is the home of the seven-step flow that
-// used to be inlined in the MCP tool. These tests pin the contract both surfaces
-// depend on: top-level failures THROW (typed ExecutionPlanError), per-feature
-// outcomes land in results[] with stable status/reason strings, and write mode
-// produces the plan files under docs/tend/output/<adapter>/.

-  let tmpDir: string;
-
-  function makeCatalog(overrides: Partial<Catalog> = {}): Catalog {
-    return { schema_version: '1', project_id: 'test', status: 'draft', features: [], ...overrides };
-  }
-  function makeFeature(id: string, overrides: Partial<Feature> = {}): Feature {
-    return { id, title: id, status: 'planned', ...overrides };
-  }
-  function makeStep(id: string) {
-    return { id, title: `Step ${id}`, status: 'pending' as const };
-  }
-  async function writeCatalogFile(catalog: Catalog): Promise<void> {
-    await writeJSON(join(tmpDir, 'docs', 'tend', 'catalog.json'), catalog);
-  }
-  async function writeFeatureFile(feature: Feature): Promise<void> {
-    const path = join(tmpDir, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', `${feature.id}.tend.html`);
-    const json = JSON.stringify(feature, null, 2).replace(/<\/script/g, '<\\/script');
-    await writeFile(
-      path,
-      '<!doctype html>\n<html><body>\n<script id="oo-data" type="application/json">\n' +
-        json +
-        '\n</script>\n</body></html>\n',
-      'utf8',
-    );
-  }
-  async function writeMarkdownAdapter(generator = MARKDOWN_GENERATOR): Promise<void> {

-      step_type_support: ['agent', 'command'],
-      model_support: [],
-      status_sync: { mode: 'manual' },

-    await writeJSON(join(tmpDir, 'docs', 'tend', 'adapters', 'markdown.json'), config);

-// ─── writeFeature concurrency ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
-//
-// check-atomic-write: concurrent writeFeature calls never corrupt the polyglot.
-// c-atomic-rename-isolation: two concurrent updates land as one valid state.
-
-describe('writeFeature concurrency', () => {
-  let tmp: string;
-
-  beforeEach(async () => {
-    tmp = await makeTempDir();
-    await makeTendDirs(tmp);
-  });
-  afterEach(async () => { await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true }); });
-
-  it('10 concurrent writeFeature calls on same feature produce a valid final polyglot (check-atomic-write)', async () => {
-    // Seed the polyglot so all writers are splicing, not assembling.
-    await writeFeature(minimalFeature, tmp);
-
-    // 10 concurrent writers each stamping a distinct title.
-    const writers = Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, i) =>
-      writeFeature({ ...minimalFeature, title: `Concurrent write ${i}` }, tmp),
-    );
-    await Promise.all(writers);
-
-    const polyglotPath = join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', 'test-feat.tend.html');
-    const text = await readFile(polyglotPath, 'utf8');
-
-    // The file must contain a closed oo-data block (never truncated mid-JSON).
-    expect(text).toContain('<script id="oo-data" type="application/json">');
-    expect(text).toContain('</script>');
-
-    // The oo-data block must parse as valid JSON.
-    const match = /<script id="oo-data" type="application\/json">\n([\s\S]*?)\n<\/script>/.exec(text);
-    expect(match).not.toBeNull();
-    const parsed = JSON.parse(match![1]!) as { title?: string };
-    expect(typeof parsed.title).toBe('string');
-    expect(parsed.title).toMatch(/^Concurrent write \d$/);
-  });
-
-  it('two concurrent writeFeature calls produce one valid state, never a truncated mix (c-atomic-rename-isolation)', async () => {
-    // Seed first so both concurrent writers are splicing an existing polyglot.
-    await writeFeature(minimalFeature, tmp);
-
-    const writerA = writeFeature({ ...minimalFeature, title: 'State A' }, tmp);
-    const writerB = writeFeature({ ...minimalFeature, title: 'State B' }, tmp);
-    await Promise.all([writerA, writerB]);
-
-    const polyglotPath = join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', 'test-feat.tend.html');
-    const text = await readFile(polyglotPath, 'utf8');
-
-    // Must be one of the two valid states — never a mix or partial write.
-    const match = /<script id="oo-data" type="application\/json">\n([\s\S]*?)\n<\/script>/.exec(text);
-    expect(match).not.toBeNull();
-    const parsed = JSON.parse(match![1]!) as { title?: string };
-    expect(['State A', 'State B']).toContain(parsed.title);
-
-    // The bash shebang must still be intact (no truncation of polyglot prefix).
-    expect(text.startsWith('#!/usr/bin/env bash')).toBe(true);
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── deleteFeature ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('deleteFeature', () => {
-  let tmp: string;
-
-  beforeEach(async () => {
-    tmp = await makeTempDir();
-    await makeTendDirs(tmp);
-  });
-  afterEach(async () => { await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true }); });
-
-  it('removes a feature polyglot by ID', async () => {
-    await writeFeature(minimalFeature, tmp);
-    await deleteFeature(minimalFeature.id, tmp);
-
-    const expectedPath = join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', 'test-feat.tend.html');
-    expect(await pathExists(expectedPath)).toBe(false);
-  });
-
-  it('throws when the feature does not exist', async () => {
-    await expect(deleteFeature('nonexistent-feat', tmp)).rejects.toThrow();
-  });
-});
