-/**
- * Tests for computeJudgmentWarnings — the pure judgment-staleness/coverage
- * helper called by runValidate. Re-hashes each judgment's §3 canonical text and
- * compares to the stored judged_sha (stale → judgment_stale); reports
- * judgment_missing for an applicable un-judged question ONLY on features that
- * already carry ≥1 judgment (the never-judged-feature gate — junction skills
- * introduce judgments; the warning catches PARTIAL/stale coverage, not the map).
- *
- * Both warnings are domain 'intent', severity 'info' — non-gating backlog.
- * No LLM, no disk read — pure over in-memory features.
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { computeJudgmentWarnings } from './validate.js';
-import { hashTargetText } from './side-effects.js';
-import type { Feature } from './types.js';
-
-function feat(overrides: Partial<Feature> = {}): Feature {
-  return { id: 'f', title: 'F', status: 'in-progress', ...overrides };
-}
-
-describe('computeJudgmentWarnings', () => {
-  it('returns no warnings when there are no judgments anywhere (never-judged map is silent)', () => {
-    const f = feat({ what: 'W', why: 'Y', impact: 'I', personas: ['p'] });
-    expect(computeJudgmentWarnings([f])).toEqual([]);
-  });
-
-  it('fires judgment_stale when the judged slot text drifted from the stored sha', () => {
-    const f = feat({
-      what: 'the NEW claim',
-      why: 'Y',
-      judgments: [
-        { question_id: 'what_relieves_why', target: 'slots:what+why', verdict: 'pass', judged_sha: 'staleshastaleshastaleshastaleshastalesha' },
-      ],
-    });
-    const warnings = computeJudgmentWarnings([f]);
-    const stale = warnings.find((w) => w.type === 'judgment_stale');
-    expect(stale).toBeDefined();
-    expect(stale?.severity).toBe('info');
-    expect(stale?.domain).toBe('intent');
-    expect(stale?.affected_node).toBe('f');
-  });
-
-  it('does NOT fire judgment_stale when the stored sha still matches current text', () => {
-    const base = feat({ what: 'W', why: 'Y' });
-    const sha = hashTargetText(base, { target: 'slots:what+why' });
-    const f = feat({
-      what: 'W',
-      why: 'Y',
-      judgments: [{ question_id: 'what_relieves_why', target: 'slots:what+why', verdict: 'pass', judged_sha: sha }],
-    });
-    expect(computeJudgmentWarnings([f]).some((w) => w.type === 'judgment_stale')).toBe(false);
-  });
-
-  it('fires judgment_missing for an applicable un-judged question on an already-judged feature', () => {
-    // Feature has one judgment (what_relieves_why) but impact is filled and has
-    // no impact_measurable judgment → judgment_missing for impact_measurable.
-    const base = feat({ what: 'W', why: 'Y', impact: 'I' });
-    const sha = hashTargetText(base, { target: 'slots:what+why' });
-    const f = feat({
-      what: 'W',
-      why: 'Y',
-      impact: 'I',
-      judgments: [{ question_id: 'what_relieves_why', target: 'slots:what+why', verdict: 'pass', judged_sha: sha }],
-    });
-    const warnings = computeJudgmentWarnings([f]);
-    const missing = warnings.find((w) => w.type === 'judgment_missing');
-    expect(missing).toBeDefined();
-    expect(missing?.severity).toBe('info');
-    expect(missing?.domain).toBe('intent');
-  });
-
-  it('does NOT fire judgment_missing for a question whose target slots are empty', () => {
-    // No impact slot → impact_measurable is INAPPLICABLE: it must not be named
-    // as missing even though the feature is judged. (one_bet, which IS
-    // applicable when what+why are filled, may still fire — that is correct.)
-    const base = feat({ what: 'W', why: 'Y' });
-    const sha = hashTargetText(base, { target: 'slots:what+why' });
-    const f = feat({
-      what: 'W',
-      why: 'Y',
-      judgments: [{ question_id: 'what_relieves_why', target: 'slots:what+why', verdict: 'pass', judged_sha: sha }],
-    });
-    const missing = computeJudgmentWarnings([f]).filter((w) => w.type === 'judgment_missing');
-    expect(missing.some((w) => w.message.includes('impact_measurable'))).toBe(false);
-  });
-
-  it('does NOT fire judgment_missing on planned features (status-gated to in-progress/verified)', () => {
-    const base = feat({ status: 'planned', what: 'W', why: 'Y', impact: 'I' });
-    const sha = hashTargetText(base, { target: 'slots:what+why' });
-    const f = feat({
-      status: 'planned',
-      what: 'W',
-      why: 'Y',
-      impact: 'I',
-      judgments: [{ question_id: 'what_relieves_why', target: 'slots:what+why', verdict: 'pass', judged_sha: sha }],
-    });
-    expect(computeJudgmentWarnings([f]).some((w) => w.type === 'judgment_missing')).toBe(false);
-  });
-
-  it('an n_a verdict counts as coverage — no judgment_missing for that question (j005)', () => {
-    // persona_load_bearing answered n_a; no missing should fire for it even
-    // though personas is non-empty.
-    const base = feat({ what: 'W', why: 'Y', personas: ['solo-dev'] });
-    const personaSha = hashTargetText(base, { target: 'persona:solo-dev' });
-    const wwSha = hashTargetText(base, { target: 'slots:what+why' });
-    const f = feat({
-      what: 'W',
-      why: 'Y',
-      personas: ['solo-dev'],
-      judgments: [
-        { question_id: 'persona_load_bearing', target: 'persona:solo-dev', verdict: 'n_a', judged_sha: personaSha },
-        { question_id: 'what_relieves_why', target: 'slots:what+why', verdict: 'pass', judged_sha: wwSha },
-      ],
-    });
-    const missing = computeJudgmentWarnings([f]).filter((w) => w.type === 'judgment_missing');
-    expect(missing.some((w) => w.message.includes('persona_load_bearing'))).toBe(false);
-  });
-
-  it('a feature-level check_discriminates n_a (target feature) covers ALL of the feature\'s check targets', () => {
-    // §11b convention: "all checks negctrl-proven — semantic re-ask redundant".
-    // One check_discriminates n_a with target 'feature' is the set-level
-    // skip-record; no per-check check_discriminates judgment_missing should fire.
-    const base = feat({
-      what: 'W',
-      why: 'Y',
-      checks: [
-        { id: 'c1', validates: 'what', method: 'synthetic-test' },
-        { id: 'c2', validates: 'why', method: 'synthetic-test' },
-        { id: 'c3', validates: 'impact', method: 'synthetic-test' },
-      ],
-    });
-    const wwSha = hashTargetText(base, { target: 'slots:what+why' });

-  it('without the feature-level n_a, every uncovered check target fires judgment_missing (the gate still holds)', () => {

-    const f = feat({

-      why: 'Y',

-        { id: 'c1', validates: 'what', method: 'synthetic-test' },

diff --git a/src/core/layering.test.ts b/src/core/layering.test.ts
deleted file mode 100644
index d5a1bd7..0000000
--- a/src/core/layering.test.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,133 +0,0 @@
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { join, dirname, resolve } from 'node:path';
-
-/**
- * Architecture invariant: `src/core/` is the foundation layer. It must NOT
- * import from its own consumers (`src/mcp/`, `src/cli/`). Such an edge is a
- * layering inversion — it creates import cycles (masked at runtime only by
- * `import type` erasure) and blocks extracting core for the plugin runtime.
- *
- * This test scans every core module and fails on any upward import. It is the
- * gate for the core->mcp/cli de-inversion refactor: RED while the edges exist,
- * GREEN once `runValidate`/`runAggregate` live in core and the negctrl decision
- * logic is lifted out of `core/bridge`.
- */
-
-const CORE_DIR = join(process.cwd(), 'src', 'core');
-
-// Matches a relative import that climbs into the mcp/ or cli/ sibling layers
-// from anywhere under src/core/ (one or two levels up).
-const FORBIDDEN = /from\s+['"](?:\.\.\/)+(?:mcp|cli)\//;
-
-function coreTsFiles(dir: string): string[] {
-  const out: string[] = [];
-  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
-    const full = join(dir, entry.name);
-    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
-      out.push(...coreTsFiles(full));
-    } else if (
-      entry.name.endsWith('.ts') &&
-      !entry.name.endsWith('.test.ts') &&
-      !entry.name.endsWith('.spec.ts') &&
-      !entry.name.endsWith('.d.ts')
-    ) {
-      out.push(full);
-    }
-  }
-  return out;
-}
-
-describe('layering invariant — src/core never imports src/mcp or src/cli', () => {
-  const files = coreTsFiles(CORE_DIR);
-
-  it('scans a non-trivial set of core modules (guards against a no-op test)', () => {
-    expect(files.length).toBeGreaterThan(20);
-  });
-
-  for (const file of files) {
-    const rel = file.slice(file.indexOf(join('src', 'core')));
-    it(`${rel} imports no consumer layer (mcp/ or cli/)`, () => {
-      const offenders = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')
-        .split('\n')
-        .map((line, i) => [i + 1, line] as const)
-        .filter(([, line]) => FORBIDDEN.test(line));
-      expect(
-        offenders,
-        `${rel} imports up into mcp/ or cli/:\n` +
-          offenders.map(([n, l]) => `  ${n}: ${l.trim()}`).join('\n'),
-      ).toEqual([]);
-    });
-  }
-});
-
-/**
- * Companion invariant: core's internal import graph is acyclic. The upward-edge
- * test above forbids core->consumer edges; this one forbids core<->core cycles.
- * A type-only cycle (e.g. `types.ts` re-exporting from a logic module that
- * imports `types.ts` back) survives `tsc` via import-type erasure but is a real
- * smell — the type leaf isn't a leaf. Keeping core a clean DAG is what lets it
- * be lifted into the plugin runtime as one unit.
- */
-describe('layering invariant — src/core has no internal import cycles', () => {
-  const files = coreTsFiles(CORE_DIR);
-  const fileSet = new Set(files);
-
-  // Resolve each relative import in `file` to an absolute core .ts path,
-  // keeping only edges that land on another scanned core module. `.js`
-  // specifiers map to their `.ts` source (the bundler/NodeNext convention).
-  function coreEdges(file: string): string[] {
-    const dir = dirname(file);
-    const src = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
-    const out: string[] = [];
-    const re = /from\s+['"](\.[^'"]+)['"]/g;
-    let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
-    while ((m = re.exec(src)) !== null) {
-      const target = resolve(dir, m[1]).replace(/\.js$/, '.ts');
-      if (fileSet.has(target)) out.push(target);
-    }
-    return out;
-  }
-
-  const graph = new Map<string, string[]>(files.map((f) => [f, coreEdges(f)]));
-
-  // First cycle found, as a path of nodes (or null). DFS with white/gray/black
-  // coloring; a back-edge to a gray node closes a cycle.
-  function findCycle(): string[] | null {
-    const color = new Map<string, 0 | 1 | 2>(files.map((f) => [f, 0]));
-    const stack: string[] = [];
-
-    function visit(node: string): string[] | null {
-      color.set(node, 1);
-      stack.push(node);
-      for (const next of graph.get(node) ?? []) {
-        if (color.get(next) === 1) {
-          return [...stack.slice(stack.indexOf(next)), next];
-        }
-        if (color.get(next) === 0) {
-          const found = visit(next);
-          if (found) return found;
-        }
-      }
-      stack.pop();
-      color.set(node, 2);
-      return null;
-    }
-
-    for (const f of files) {
-      if (color.get(f) === 0) {
-        const found = visit(f);
-        if (found) return found;
-      }
-    }
-    return null;
-  }
-
-  it('contains no circular import among core modules', () => {
-    const cycle = findCycle();
-    const pretty = cycle
-      ? cycle.map((f) => f.slice(f.indexOf(join('src', 'core')))).join('\n  → ')
-      : '';
-    expect(cycle, `core import cycle detected:\n  ${pretty}`).toBeNull();
-  });
-});
diff --git a/src/core/mock-detection.test.ts b/src/core/mock-detection.test.ts
deleted file mode 100644
index 691fd79..0000000
--- a/src/core/mock-detection.test.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,447 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * Unit tests for the mock-detection library.
- *
- * analyzeEvidence(testPath, productionPaths, repoRoot) classifies a test file
- * based on whether it mocks the production modules it imports.
- *
- * Spec (feature mcp-server.mock-detection):
- *   real       — imports production module(s), none are mocked
- *   partial    — imports production module(s), some but not all are mocked
- *   mock-only  — every production import is mocked (vi.mock or jest.mock)
- *   unknown    — non-TS/TSX file, or file does not exist
- *
- * Hard constraints:
- *   - False positive (clean → mock-only) is much worse than a miss.
- *   - When uncertain, return 'unknown' and skip.
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll, afterAll } from 'vitest';
-import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { join } from 'node:path';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { analyzeEvidence } from './mock-detection.js';
-
-// ─── Fixtures ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-/**
- * We create a mini-repo structure so relative imports in test fixtures
- * resolve correctly against the production paths.
- *
- * Layout:
- *   tmpDir/                   ← repoRoot
- *     src/
- *       auth/login.ts         ← production module
- *       core/foo.ts
- *       core/bar.ts
- *       core/a.ts
- *       core/b.ts
- *       core/thing.ts
- *       core/progress.ts
- *       core/graph.ts
- *       utils/helper.ts
- *       core/unrelated.ts
- *     tests/                  ← test files live here
- *       *.test.ts
- *
- * Test imports like `'../src/auth/login'` (relative from tests/) resolve to
- * `tmpDir/src/auth/login.ts` which matches the production path.
- */
-
-let tmpDir: string;
-
-beforeAll(() => {
-  tmpDir = join(tmpdir(), `mock-detection-test-${Date.now()}`);
-  // Create production module stubs
-  const prodDirs = [
-    'src/auth',
-    'src/core',
-    'src/utils',
-    'tests',
-  ];
-  for (const d of prodDirs) {
-    mkdirSync(join(tmpDir, d), { recursive: true });
-  }
-  const prodFiles = [
-    'src/auth/login.ts',
-    'src/core/foo.ts',
-    'src/core/bar.ts',
-    'src/core/a.ts',
-    'src/core/b.ts',
-    'src/core/thing.ts',
-    'src/core/progress.ts',
-    'src/core/graph.ts',
-    'src/core/unrelated.ts',
-    'src/utils/helper.ts',
-  ];
-  for (const f of prodFiles) {
-    writeFileSync(join(tmpDir, f), `export const stub = true;\n`, 'utf8');
-  }
-});
-
-afterAll(() => {
-  rmSync(tmpDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
-});
-
-/** Write a test fixture in tmpDir/tests/ and return its absolute path. */
-function writeFixture(name: string, content: string): string {
-  const p = join(tmpDir, 'tests', name);
-  writeFileSync(p, content, 'utf8');
-  return p;
-}
-
-// ─── mock-only ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('mock-only', () => {
-  it('vi.mock of the sole production import → mock-only', () => {
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'mock-only-vi.test.ts',
-      `
-import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
-import { handleLogin } from '../src/auth/login';
-vi.mock('../src/auth/login');
-it('test', () => {});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/auth/login.ts'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('mock-only');
-    expect(result.mockedModules.some((m) => m.includes('login'))).toBe(true);
-  });
-
-  it('vi.mock via variable call → mock-only', () => {
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'mock-only-dynamic.test.ts',
-      `
-import { describe, it, vi } from 'vitest';
-import { foo } from '../src/core/foo';
-vi.mock('../src/core/foo', () => ({ foo: vi.fn() }));
-it('test', () => {});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/core/foo.ts'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('mock-only');
-  });
-
-  it('jest.mock of the production import → mock-only', () => {
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'mock-only-jest.test.ts',
-      `
-import { describe, it, expect } from '@jest/globals';
-import { doThing } from '../src/core/thing';
-jest.mock('../src/core/thing');
-it('test', () => {});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/core/thing.ts'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('mock-only');
-  });
-
-  it('mocks the module and only accesses via vi.fn() reassignment → mock-only', () => {
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'mock-only-reassign.test.ts',
-      `
-import { vi } from 'vitest';
-import { handleLogin } from '../src/auth/login';
-vi.mock('../src/auth/login', () => ({ handleLogin: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ status: 200 }) }));
-it('returns 200', async () => {
-  const res = await handleLogin({ email: 'a@b.co', password: 'x' });
-  expect(res.status).toBe(200);
-});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/auth/login.ts'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('mock-only');
-  });
-
-  it('.tsx evidence file that mocks its production import → mock-only (.tsx branch is live)', () => {
-    // negctrl target: removing '.tsx' from the extension guard in analyzeEvidence
-    // (line: `if (ext !== '.ts' && ext !== '.tsx') return empty;`)
-    // must cause THIS test to fail — proving the branch discriminates.
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'mock-only-tsx.test.tsx',
-      `
-import { describe, it, vi } from 'vitest';
-import { handleLogin } from '../src/auth/login';
-vi.mock('../src/auth/login');
-it('test', () => {});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/auth/login.ts'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('mock-only');
-    expect(result.mockedModules.some((m) => m.includes('login'))).toBe(true);
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── partial mock ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('partial', () => {
-  it('mocks one of two production imports → partial', () => {
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'partial.test.ts',
-      `
-import { describe, it, vi } from 'vitest';
-import { foo } from '../src/core/foo';
-import { bar } from '../src/core/bar';
-vi.mock('../src/core/foo');
-it('test', () => {});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/core/foo.ts', 'src/core/bar.ts'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('partial');
-  });
-
-  it('vi.mock + vi.importActual on the same module → partial', () => {
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'partial-importactual.test.ts',
-      `
-import { vi } from 'vitest';
-import { foo } from '../src/core/foo';
-vi.mock('../src/core/foo');
-const actual = await vi.importActual('../src/core/foo');
-it('test', () => {});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/core/foo.ts'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('partial');
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── clean (real) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('real', () => {
-  it('imports production module without mocking → real', () => {
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'real.test.ts',
-      `
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { computeProgress } from '../src/core/progress';
-describe('progress', () => {
-  it('returns zero for empty', () => {
-    const r = computeProgress({ id: 'x', title: 'x', status: 'planned' });
-    expect(r.implementation).toBe(0);
-  });
-});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/core/progress.ts'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('real');
-  });
-
-  it('mocks a different module, not the production one → real', () => {
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'real-other-mock.test.ts',
-      `
-import { vi } from 'vitest';
-import { computeProgress } from '../src/core/progress';
-vi.mock('../src/core/unrelated');
-it('test', () => {});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/core/progress.ts'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('real');
-  });
-
-  it('no production paths relevant to this test → real (none to mock)', () => {
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'real-no-relevant.test.ts',
-      `
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { helper } from '../src/utils/helper';
-it('uses helper', () => {});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    // production path is something else entirely
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/core/graph.ts'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('real');
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── unknown ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('unknown', () => {
-  it('non-existent file → unknown (not a throw)', () => {
-    const result = analyzeEvidence('/tmp/does-not-exist-12345.test.ts', ['src/foo.ts'], '/tmp');
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('unknown');
-  });
-
-  it('.py file → unknown (no AST, no false positives)', () => {
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'test_thing.py',
-      `
-import pytest
-from src.thing import handle_login
-def test_login():
-    result = handle_login('a@b.co', 'x')
-    assert result['status'] == 200
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/thing.py'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('unknown');
-  });
-
-  it('.spec.js file → unknown (no TS, conservative)', () => {
-    const p = writeFixture(
-      'thing.spec.js',
-      `
-const { doThing } = require('../core/thing');
-jest.mock('../core/thing');
-test('works', () => {});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const result = analyzeEvidence(p, ['src/core/thing.js'], tmpDir);
-    expect(result.kind).toBe('unknown');
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── AuditSignal integration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('AuditSignal union', () => {
-  it('AuditSignal type discriminates on "type" field', async () => {
-    const { computeMockSignals } = await import('./mock-detection.js');
-    // A verdict with a mock-only test should produce a mock-only signal.
-    // The evidence_path is repo-relative; computeMockSignals resolves it against repoRoot.
-    const relPath = 'tests/signal-mock.test.ts';
-    writeFixture(
-      'signal-mock.test.ts',
-      `
-import { vi } from 'vitest';
-import { handleLogin } from '../src/auth/login';
-vi.mock('../src/auth/login');
-it('test', () => {});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const signals = computeMockSignals(
-      [{ check_id: 'c001', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: relPath }],
-      ['src/auth/login.ts'],
-      tmpDir,
-    );
-    expect(signals.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
-    expect(signals[0].type).toBe('mock-only');
-    expect(signals[0].verdict_id).toBe('c001');
-  });
-
-  it('signals are empty when no verdicts are mock-only', async () => {
-    const { computeMockSignals } = await import('./mock-detection.js');
-    const relPath = 'tests/signal-real.test.ts';
-    writeFixture(
-      'signal-real.test.ts',
-      `
-import { computeProgress } from '../src/core/progress';
-it('test', () => {});
-`.trim(),
-    );
-    const signals = computeMockSignals(
-      [{ check_id: 'c002', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: relPath }],
-      ['src/core/progress.ts'],
-      tmpDir,
-    );
-    expect(signals).toHaveLength(0);
-  });
-});
-
-// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-// P0.2 / D3 — mock-detection default-on (RED tests)
-//
-// Current behaviour (validate.ts:641-643):
-//   const productionPaths = f.coverage_files ?? [];
-//   if (productionPaths.length === 0) continue;   // <── bypass gate
-//   ...computeMockSignals(verdicts, productionPaths, root)
-//
-// Target behaviour:
-//   When an audit verdict cites a .ts/.tsx test file as evidence, mock-detection
-//   runs regardless of whether coverage_files is set. Unit-under-test resolution
-//   order (conservative — false positives are worse than false negatives):
-//     1. coverage_files (explicit, most reliable)
-//     2. WHERE-slot backtick paths (extracted from feature.where, e.g.
-//        `src/auth.ts` → ['src/auth.ts'])
-//     3. If neither yields paths, skip (return 'unknown' → no false positive)
-//
-//   The computeMockSignals function itself is correct — the gap is in the
-//   caller's early-exit bypass. Phase 1.3 removes the bypass and adds a
-//   unit-under-test resolver (extractPathsFromWhereSlot or similar).
-//
-// Limits:
-//   - Only .ts/.tsx evidence files are analysed (analyzeEvidence already
-//     returns 'unknown' for others).
-//   - The where-slot extraction is best-effort (backtick paths only, no
-//     glob expansion). Paths that don't resolve on disk produce 'unknown'.
-//   - Dependencies-resolved code claims are NOT used (too many false positives
-//     — shared utility files listed as deps would wrongly trigger detection).
-// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-// P0.2 / D3 — mock-detection default-on: WHERE-slot path extractor (unit tests)
-//
-// Current behaviour (validate.ts:641-643):
-//   const productionPaths = f.coverage_files ?? [];
-//   if (productionPaths.length === 0) continue;   // <── bypass gate
-//   ...computeMockSignals(verdicts, productionPaths, root)
-//
-// Target behaviour: bypass removed; unit-under-test paths resolved via:
-//   1. coverage_files (explicit, most reliable)
-//   2. WHERE-slot backtick paths extracted by exportProductionPathsFromWhere()
-//   3. If neither yields paths → skip (no false positive)
-//
-// Phase 1.3 adds `extractProductionPathsFromWhere(whereSlot: string): string[]`
-// exported from mock-detection.ts. The integration-level bypass test lives in
-// validation.integration.test.ts (D3 section).
-//
-// Limits documented in p0-findings/p02-hollow-green.md.

-/**
- * Tests for computeNextAction — T2.4.
- *
- * Strategy mirrors project-health.test.ts: each test writes a small fixture
- * project under tmpdir(), runs computeNextAction, and asserts the action
- * + reason codes + not_chosen. A dogfood snapshot at the bottom runs
- * against the actual tend project and asserts SHAPE (verdict is one of
- * the legal forms, reasons are valid codes) — not specific feature ids,
- * because the project state changes day-to-day.
- *
- * Algorithm coverage:
- *   - Hard routing: broken_refs → audit (rule 1)
- *   - Hard routing: cycle_detected → change (rule 2)
- *   - Hard routing: stale_evidence on verified → audit (rule 3)
- *   - Hard routing: mock_only_evidence on verified → audit (rule 4)
- *   - Hard routing: false_done → audit (rule 5)
- *   - Hard routing: orphan_check on feature with steps → plan (rule 6)
- *   - Scoring: critical opportunity + small wins
- *   - Scoring: verified-deps feature preferred over blocked-deps feature
- *   - Bootstrap: empty project → /tend brainstorm
- *   - Determinism: byte-for-byte stable on same input
- *   - Output: action non-empty, ≥1 reason code, codes in REASON_CODES
- *   - Output: explanation derives from REASON_CODES.long_explanation
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
-import { mkdtemp, mkdir, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';
-import { computeNextAction } from './next-action.js';
-import { writeFeature, writeCatalog } from './files.js';
-import { buildCoherence } from './project-health.js';
-import { runValidate } from './validate.js';
-import { REASON_CODES, type ReasonCode } from './reason-codes.js';
-import type { Catalog, Feature } from './types.js';
-
-// ─── Fixture helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-function makeCatalog(overrides: Partial<Catalog> = {}): Catalog {
-  return {
-    schema_version: '1',
-    project_id: 'test',
-    status: 'draft',
-    features: [],
-    ...overrides,
-  };
-}
-
-function makeFeature(id: string, overrides: Partial<Feature> = {}): Feature {
-  return {
-    id,
-    title: id,
-    status: 'planned',
-    ...overrides,
-  };
-}
-
-async function writeProject(
-  tmp: string,
-  catalog: Catalog,
-  features: Feature[],
-): Promise<void> {
-  await mkdir(join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features'), { recursive: true });
-  await writeCatalog(catalog, tmp);
-  for (const f of features) {
-    await writeFeature(f, tmp);
-  }
-}
-
-// ─── Suite ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('computeNextAction', () => {
-  let tmp: string;
-
-  beforeEach(async () => {
-    tmp = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'tend-next-action-'));
-  });
-
-  afterEach(async () => {
-    await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
-  });
-
-  // ── Output shape invariants ────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-  describe('output shape', () => {
-    it('always returns a non-empty action string', async () => {
-      await writeProject(tmp, makeCatalog(), []);
-      const result = await computeNextAction(tmp);
-      expect(typeof result.action).toBe('string');
-      expect(result.action.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
-    });
-
-    it('always returns at least one reason code', async () => {
-      await writeProject(tmp, makeCatalog(), []);
-      const result = await computeNextAction(tmp);
-      expect(result.reason_codes.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
-    });
-
-    it('every reason code is a valid REASON_CODES key', async () => {
-      const features: Feature[] = [
-        makeFeature('feat-a', { status: 'planned' }),
-      ];
-      const catalog = makeCatalog({
-        features: features.map((f) => ({ id: f.id, title: f.id, status: f.status })),
-      });
-      await writeProject(tmp, catalog, features);

-        }
-      }
-    });
-
-    it('explanation derives from REASON_CODES.long_explanation', async () => {
-      const features: Feature[] = [
-        makeFeature('feat-a', {
-          status: 'in-progress',
-          progress: { implementation: 100, verification: 0 },
-        }),
-      ];
-      const catalog = makeCatalog({
-        features: features.map((f) => ({ id: f.id, title: f.id, status: f.status })),

-      await writeProject(tmp, catalog, features);
-      const result = await computeNextAction(tmp);
-
-      // Pick the first reason code and verify its long_explanation appears
-      // in the explanation prose (substring match — the generator wraps
-      // each code's sentence in a feature-id-tagged prefix).

-
-  // ── Hard routing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-  describe('hard routing: broken_refs', () => {
-    it('routes to /tend audit on the feature with a broken dependency ref', async () => {

-
-  describe('hard routing: stale_evidence on verified', () => {
-    it('routes to /tend audit when a verified feature has a stale verdict', async () => {
-      // A verified feature with a verdict pointing at an evidence file
-      // whose recorded sha differs from disk → stale.
-      const { writeFile } = await import('node:fs/promises');
-      const evidencePath = join(tmp, 'src', 'foo.ts');
-      await mkdir(join(tmp, 'src'), { recursive: true });
-      await writeFile(evidencePath, 'one', 'utf8');
-      // capture stale sha (different from current content)
-      const features: Feature[] = [
-        makeFeature('feat-a', {
-          status: 'verified',
-          progress: { implementation: 100, verification: 100 },
-          audit: {
-            result: 'pass',
-            verdicts: [
-              {
-                check_id: 'c001',
-                verdict: 'pass',

-                evidence_sha: '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000',
-              },
-            ],
-          },

-
-  describe('hard routing: false_done', () => {
-    it('routes to /tend audit when impl=100 and ver<100', async () => {

-  describe('scoring: value beats loudness', () => {

-// ─── Mock-only / stale verdicts drop from real verification ──────────────────
-
-/**
- * The un-foolable-verification promise: a `pass` verdict whose evidence test
- * mocks the production module it claims to verify provides zero evidence and
- * must NOT count toward verification. These tests run the WHOLE read pipeline
- * (computeProjectHealth) — signals are collected from disk, the adjusted
- * verification % is recomputed, and the cockpit's false_done figure reflects it.
- *
- * Fixture: a production module under src/, an evidence test that mocks it, and
- * an evidence test that imports it for real. The mocked verdict must be excluded.
- */
-describe('computeProjectHealth — mock-only verdicts drop from real verification', () => {
-  let tmp: string;
-
-  beforeEach(async () => {
-    tmp = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'tend-ph-mock-'));
-    // Production modules the evidence tests will mock-vs-import.
-    await mkdir(join(tmp, 'src', 'core'), { recursive: true });
-    await mkdir(join(tmp, 'tests'), { recursive: true });
-    await writeFile(join(tmp, 'src', 'core', 'mod-a.ts'), 'export const a = 1;\n', 'utf8');
-    await writeFile(join(tmp, 'src', 'core', 'mod-b.ts'), 'export const b = 2;\n', 'utf8');
-    await writeFile(join(tmp, 'src', 'core', 'mod-c.ts'), 'export const c = 3;\n', 'utf8');
-    await writeFile(join(tmp, 'src', 'core', 'mod-d.ts'), 'export const d = 4;\n', 'utf8');
-    // Two REAL evidence tests (import production, never mock it).
-    await writeFile(
-      join(tmp, 'tests', 'a.test.ts'),
-      "import { a } from '../src/core/mod-a';\nit('t', () => { expect(a).toBe(1); });\n",
-      'utf8',
-    );
-    await writeFile(
-      join(tmp, 'tests', 'b.test.ts'),
-      "import { b } from '../src/core/mod-b';\nit('t', () => { expect(b).toBe(2); });\n",
-      'utf8',
-    );
-    // Two MOCK-ONLY evidence tests (import production, then mock it — theatre).
-    await writeFile(
-      join(tmp, 'tests', 'c.test.ts'),
-      "import { vi } from 'vitest';\nimport { c } from '../src/core/mod-c';\nvi.mock('../src/core/mod-c');\nit('t', () => {});\n",
-      'utf8',
-    );
-    await writeFile(
-      join(tmp, 'tests', 'd.test.ts'),
-      "import { vi } from 'vitest';\nimport { d } from '../src/core/mod-d';\nvi.mock('../src/core/mod-d');\nit('t', () => {});\n",
-      'utf8',
-    );
-  });
-
-  afterEach(async () => {
-    await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
-  });
-
-  /** A feature claiming all 4 verdicts pass — but 2 cite mock-only tests. */
-  function mockTheatreFeature(): Feature {
-    return makeFeature('feat-mock', {
-      status: 'in-progress',
-      // The feature CLAIMS full verification (the gameable number).
-      progress: { implementation: 100, verification: 100 },
-      coverage_files: ['src/core/mod-a.ts', 'src/core/mod-b.ts', 'src/core/mod-c.ts', 'src/core/mod-d.ts'],
-      checks: [
-        { id: 'c1', description: 'a', validates: 'what', method: 'synthetic-test', status: 'pass' },
-        { id: 'c2', description: 'b', validates: 'why', method: 'synthetic-test', status: 'pass' },
-        { id: 'c3', description: 'c', validates: 'how', method: 'synthetic-test', status: 'pass' },
-        { id: 'c4', description: 'd', validates: 'fit', method: 'synthetic-test', status: 'pass' },
-      ],
-      audit: {
-        ran_at: '2026-06-01T00:00:00Z',
-        result: 'pass',
-        verdicts: [
-          { check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'tests/a.test.ts' },
-          { check_id: 'c2', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'tests/b.test.ts' },
-          { check_id: 'c3', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'tests/c.test.ts' },
-          { check_id: 'c4', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'tests/d.test.ts' },
-        ],
-      },
-    });
-  }
-
-  it('counts the 2 mock-only verdicts in the truth block', async () => {
-    const feature = mockTheatreFeature();
-    const catalog = makeCatalog({ features: [{ id: feature.id, title: feature.id, status: feature.status }] });
-    await writeProject(tmp, catalog, [feature]);
-
-    const health = await computeProjectHealth(tmp);
-
-    expect(health.truth.mock_only).toBe(2);
-    expect(health.reason_codes).toContain('mock_only_evidence');
-  });
-
-  it('real verification drops to 50, flipping the feature into false_done despite a claimed 100', async () => {
-    const feature = mockTheatreFeature();
-    const catalog = makeCatalog({ features: [{ id: feature.id, title: feature.id, status: feature.status }] });
-    await writeProject(tmp, catalog, [feature]);
-
-    const health = await computeProjectHealth(tmp);
-
-    // impl=100 but only 2 of 4 verdicts survive the mock filter → real
-    // verification is 50, not the stored/claimed 100. That makes it false_done.
-    expect(health.truth.false_done).toBe(1);
-    expect(health.reason_codes).toContain('false_done');
-  });
-
-  it('the same feature with all-real evidence is NOT false_done (control)', async () => {
-    // Point every verdict at a real (non-mocking) test → nothing excluded.
-    const feature = mockTheatreFeature();
-    feature.audit!.verdicts = [
-      { check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'tests/a.test.ts' },
-      { check_id: 'c2', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'tests/b.test.ts' },
-      { check_id: 'c3', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'tests/a.test.ts' },
-      { check_id: 'c4', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'tests/b.test.ts' },
-    ];
-    const catalog = makeCatalog({ features: [{ id: feature.id, title: feature.id, status: feature.status }] });
-    await writeProject(tmp, catalog, [feature]);
-
-    const health = await computeProjectHealth(tmp);
-
-    expect(health.truth.mock_only).toBe(0);
-    expect(health.truth.false_done).toBe(0);
-  });
-});

-// ─── Stale verdicts drop from real verification ──────────────────────────────
-
-/**
- * The staleness half of the un-foolable-verification promise: a `pass` verdict
- * whose cited evidence file has DRIFTED since the verdict was recorded (the
- * stored sha no longer matches the file on disk) must NOT count toward
- * verification — exactly the way a mock-only verdict is excluded. This is the
- * parallel of the mock-only block above, for the stale signal path.
- *
- * It runs the WHOLE read pipeline (computeProjectHealth): findStaleVerdicts
- * collects the drifted verdict id from disk, project-health routes it into the
- * signal-agnostic excluded set, computeTruth recomputes the feature's real
- * verification DOWN via computeProgress(f, excluded), and the cockpit's
- * false_done figure reflects the dropped verdict.
- *
- * Fixture: a feature claiming 4 pass verdicts and a stored verification of 100.
- * One verdict cites a real source file but records a non-matching evidence_sha
- * (stale). The other three carry no evidence_sha, so they are never stale. Real
- * verification is therefore 3/4 = 75, which flips the feature into false_done.
- */
-describe('computeProjectHealth — stale verdicts drop from real verification', () => {
-  let tmp: string;
-  /** A wrong sha — guarantees a mismatch against any real file content. */
-  const WRONG_SHA = 'deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef';
-
-  beforeEach(async () => {
-    tmp = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'tend-ph-stale-'));
-    // The single production file the stale verdict cites. It exists on disk, so
-    // the verdict is not "missing" — it is content-drifted (recorded sha wrong).
-    await mkdir(join(tmp, 'src', 'core'), { recursive: true });
-    await writeFile(join(tmp, 'src', 'core', 'drifted.ts'), 'export const x = 1;\n', 'utf8');
-  });
-
-  afterEach(async () => {
-    await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
-  });
-
-  /**
-   * A feature claiming all 4 verdicts pass — but verdict c1 cites a real file
-   * with a drifted (wrong) sha. The other three carry no evidence_sha.
-   */
-  function staleClaimFeature(): Feature {
-    return makeFeature('feat-stale', {
-      status: 'in-progress',
-      // The feature CLAIMS full verification (the gameable number).
-      progress: { implementation: 100, verification: 100 },
-      checks: [
-        { id: 'c1', description: 'a', validates: 'what', method: 'synthetic-test', status: 'pass' },
-        { id: 'c2', description: 'b', validates: 'why', method: 'synthetic-test', status: 'pass' },
-        { id: 'c3', description: 'c', validates: 'how', method: 'synthetic-test', status: 'pass' },
-        { id: 'c4', description: 'd', validates: 'fit', method: 'synthetic-test', status: 'pass' },
-      ],
-      audit: {
-        ran_at: '2026-06-01T00:00:00Z',
-        result: 'pass',
-        verdicts: [
-          // Stale: cites a real file, but the recorded sha does not match it.
-          { check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'src/core/drifted.ts', evidence_sha: WRONG_SHA },
-          // Fresh: no evidence_sha → nothing to compare → never stale.
-          { check_id: 'c2', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'tests/b.test.ts' },
-          { check_id: 'c3', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'tests/c.test.ts' },
-          { check_id: 'c4', verdict: 'pass', evidence_path: 'tests/d.test.ts' },
-        ],
-      },
-    });
-  }
-
-  it('counts the 1 stale verdict in the truth block', async () => {
-    const feature = staleClaimFeature();
-    const catalog = makeCatalog({ features: [{ id: feature.id, title: feature.id, status: feature.status }] });
-    await writeProject(tmp, catalog, [feature]);
-
-    const health = await computeProjectHealth(tmp);
-
-    expect(health.truth.stale).toBe(1);
-    expect(health.reason_codes).toContain('stale_evidence');
-  });
-
-  it('real verification drops to 75, flipping the feature into false_done despite a claimed 100', async () => {
-    const feature = staleClaimFeature();
-    const catalog = makeCatalog({ features: [{ id: feature.id, title: feature.id, status: feature.status }] });
-    await writeProject(tmp, catalog, [feature]);
-
-    const health = await computeProjectHealth(tmp);
-
-    // impl=100 but only 3 of 4 verdicts survive the staleness filter → real
-    // verification is 75, not the stored/claimed 100. That makes it false_done.
-    expect(health.truth.false_done).toBe(1);
-    expect(health.reason_codes).toContain('false_done');
-  });
-
-  it('the same feature with a matching sha on the cited file is NOT false_done (control)', async () => {
-    // Record the CORRECT sha for the cited file → nothing drifts, nothing is
-    // excluded, real verification stays 100. Isolates the stale path: only the
-    // sha mismatch in the primary test drives the exclusion.
-    const { createHash } = await import('node:crypto');
-    const sha = createHash('sha1').update('export const x = 1;\n').digest('hex');
-    const feature = staleClaimFeature();
-    feature.audit!.verdicts[0] = {
-      check_id: 'c1',
-      verdict: 'pass',
-      evidence_path: 'src/core/drifted.ts',
-      evidence_sha: sha,
-    };
-    const catalog = makeCatalog({ features: [{ id: feature.id, title: feature.id, status: feature.status }] });
-    await writeProject(tmp, catalog, [feature]);
-
-    const health = await computeProjectHealth(tmp);
-
-    expect(health.truth.stale).toBe(0);
-    expect(health.truth.false_done).toBe(0);
-  });
-});

-// ─── buildCoherence (pure grouping helper) ───────────────────────────────────

-describe('buildCoherence', () => {

-  it('buckets constraint warnings into friendly themes, merging same-label types', () => {

-  it('sorts groups by count descending', () => {

-/**

- * predicate is what makes the three views reconcile by construction.

-/**
- * classifyLifecycle — the pure classifier. Every active bet lands in exactly
- * one of four sequential stages (planned → building → built → verified) plus
- * at most one orthogonal warning flag (blocked on non-verified, at_risk on
- * verified). MECE by construction. Stage is impl-driven, not status-label
- * driven (NOW-not-narrative): an in-progress feature with 0% built is honestly
- * 'planned'. 'verified' is terminal — never blocked.
- */
-describe('classifyLifecycle', () => {
-  const verifiedDep = makeFeature('dep-done', { status: 'verified' });
-  const unverifiedDep = makeFeature('dep-todo', { status: 'in-progress' });
-
-  it('verified + clean → {verified, none}', () => {
-    const f = makeFeature('f', { status: 'verified' });
-    expect(classifyLifecycle(f, [f], new Set())).toEqual({ stage: 'verified', flag: 'none' });
-  });
-  it('verified + flagged stale/mock → {verified, at_risk}', () => {
-    const f = makeFeature('f', { status: 'verified' });
-    expect(classifyLifecycle(f, [f], new Set(['f']))).toEqual({ stage: 'verified', flag: 'at_risk' });
-  });
-  it('verified is terminal — never blocked, even with an unverified dependency', () => {
-    const f = makeFeature('f', { status: 'verified', dependencies: ['dep-todo'] });
-    expect(classifyLifecycle(f, [f, unverifiedDep], new Set())).toEqual({ stage: 'verified', flag: 'none' });
-  });
-  it('impl 100, not verified, deps satisfied → {built, none}', () => {
-    const f = makeFeature('f', { status: 'in-progress', progress: { implementation: 100, verification: 0 } });
-    expect(classifyLifecycle(f, [f], new Set())).toEqual({ stage: 'built', flag: 'none' });
-  });
-  it('impl 100, blocked → {built, blocked}', () => {
-    const f = makeFeature('f', {
-      status: 'in-progress',
-      progress: { implementation: 100, verification: 0 },
-      dependencies: ['dep-todo'],
-    });
-    expect(classifyLifecycle(f, [f, unverifiedDep], new Set())).toEqual({ stage: 'built', flag: 'blocked' });
-  });
-  it('0 < impl < 100 → {building, none}', () => {
-    const f = makeFeature('f', { status: 'in-progress', progress: { implementation: 50, verification: 0 } });
-    expect(classifyLifecycle(f, [f], new Set())).toEqual({ stage: 'building', flag: 'none' });
-  });
-  it('building + blocked → {building, blocked}', () => {
-    const f = makeFeature('f', {
-      status: 'in-progress',
-      progress: { implementation: 50, verification: 0 },
-      dependencies: ['dep-todo'],
-    });
-    expect(classifyLifecycle(f, [f, unverifiedDep], new Set())).toEqual({ stage: 'building', flag: 'blocked' });
-  });
-  it('impl 0 → {planned, none}', () => {
-    const f = makeFeature('f', { status: 'planned' });
-    expect(classifyLifecycle(f, [f], new Set())).toEqual({ stage: 'planned', flag: 'none' });
-  });
-  it('planned + blocked → {planned, blocked}', () => {
-    const f = makeFeature('f', { status: 'planned', dependencies: ['dep-todo'] });
-    expect(classifyLifecycle(f, [f, unverifiedDep], new Set())).toEqual({ stage: 'planned', flag: 'blocked' });
-  });
-  it('a dependency that IS verified does not block', () => {
-    const f = makeFeature('f', { status: 'planned', dependencies: ['dep-done'] });
-    expect(classifyLifecycle(f, [f, verifiedDep], new Set())).toEqual({ stage: 'planned', flag: 'none' });
-  });
-  it('missing progress defaults to planned (total over absent fields)', () => {
-    const f = makeFeature('f', { status: 'in-progress' });

-/**
- * Tests for the canonical reason-code vocabulary.

- * Vocabulary lock-in is real: every signal tend emits (validator warnings,
- * drift_verdict synthesis, `tend next` recommendations) cites these codes,
- * so removing or renaming one is a breaking change. The snapshot test
- * pins the inventory; the field tests pin each entry's well-formedness.
- */

-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { REASON_CODES, toKebab, type ReasonCode } from './reason-codes.js';

-describe('REASON_CODES', () => {

-  it('uses the key as the code value (snake_case stability)', () => {

-    }

-
-  it('has no duplicate codes', () => {

-  it('uses snake_case for every code (no kebab, no camelCase, no spaces)', () => {

-/**
- * Extract the oo-data block from a polyglot directly (no bash dependency).
- * Some test runs reassemble polyglots mid-suite; reading the file as text
- * and parsing the script block keeps the schema dogfood test robust against
- * bash-script-parsing concerns from concurrent reassembly.
- */
-function readOoDataFromPolyglot(path: string): unknown {
-  const text = readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
-  const match = /<script id="oo-data" type="application\/json">\n([\s\S]*?)\n<\/script>/.exec(text);
-  if (!match || !match[1]) {
-    throw new Error(`oo-data block not found in ${path}`);
-  }
-  return JSON.parse(match[1]);
-}

-// ─── Side-effects wiring: which writes trigger refreshHealthSnapshot ─────────
-//
-// These tests assert the *pipeline* behaviour — that the right writes refresh
-// the snapshot through the MCP-level integration. We exercise the same code
-// path as the MCP tools by calling `refreshHealthSnapshot` after each write
-// and asserting that the snapshot moved (or stayed put) accordingly. The tool
-// wrappers in src/mcp/tools/features.ts and catalog.ts call the refresh under
-// `touchesHealthFields` / always-on conditions; the perf guarantee for
-// narrative-only edits lives in the predicate.
-
-describe('refreshHealthSnapshot — pipeline integration', () => {
-  let tmp: string;
-
-  beforeEach(async () => {
-    tmp = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'tend-health-pipeline-'));
-    await mkdir(join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features'), { recursive: true });
-    await writeCatalog(makeCatalog(), tmp);
-  });
-
-  afterEach(async () => {
-    await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
-  });
-
-  it('feature create followed by refresh updates truth.total', async () => {
-    await refreshHealthSnapshot(tmp);
-    const before = (await readFeature('garden', tmp)).health_snapshot!;
-    expect(before.truth.total).toBe(0);

-    await writeFeature(makeFeature({ id: 'feat-a' }), tmp);
-    await refreshHealthSnapshot(tmp);
-
-    const after = (await readFeature('garden', tmp)).health_snapshot!;
-    expect(after.truth.total).toBe(1);
-  });
-
-  it('feature audit-verdict change followed by refresh moves truth.verified', async () => {
-    await writeFeature(
-      makeFeature({

-        status: 'in-progress',
-        progress: { implementation: 100, verification: 0 },

-    );
-    await refreshHealthSnapshot(tmp);
-    const before = (await readFeature('garden', tmp)).health_snapshot!;
-    expect(before.truth.verified).toBe(0);
-
-    // Audit verdict change: status moves to verified, progress.verification=100.
-    const f = await readFeature('feat-a', tmp);
-    f.status = 'verified';
-    f.audit = {
-      result: 'pass',
-      verdicts: [{ check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'pass' }],
-    };
-    f.progress = { implementation: 100, verification: 100 };
-    await writeFeature(f, tmp);
-    await refreshHealthSnapshot(tmp);
-
-    const after = (await readFeature('garden', tmp)).health_snapshot!;
-    expect(after.truth.verified).toBe(1);

-  it('catalog update followed by refresh moves value.weakest_opportunity_coverage', async () => {

-    expect(before.value.weakest_opportunity_coverage).toBeUndefined();

-    await writeCatalog(

-        ],
-      }),

-    await refreshHealthSnapshot(tmp);

-    const after = (await readFeature('garden', tmp)).health_snapshot!;
-    expect(after.value.weakest_opportunity_coverage).toBe('opp-x');

-
-  it('narrative-only / decisions-only edit does NOT move the snapshot (perf guarantee)', async () => {
-    await writeFeature(makeFeature({ id: 'feat-a' }), tmp);
-    await refreshHealthSnapshot(tmp);
-    const before = (await readFeature('garden', tmp)).health_snapshot!;
-
-    // Author narrative + decisions on the feature; no slot, no check, no
-    // status, no progress changes — purely cosmetic edits.

-      { id: 'd1', decision: 'Use a single string', rationale: 'simplicity' },

-    // If the MCP tool's touchesHealthFields predicate correctly skips this

-    const after = (await readFeature('garden', tmp)).health_snapshot!;

-    expect(after.verdict).toBe(before.verdict);
-    expect(after.reason_codes).toEqual(before.reason_codes);
-    expect(after.truth).toEqual(before.truth);
-    expect(after.flow).toEqual(before.flow);
-    expect(after.value).toEqual(before.value);

-describe('verified_at_commit stamping', () => {

-  it('stamps audit.verified_at_commit with git HEAD SHA when writing an audit in a git repo', () => {
-    // Arrange: initialise a real git repo so git rev-parse HEAD works.

-    execFileSync('git', ['config', 'user.email', 'test@test.com'], { cwd: tmp, stdio: 'ignore' });
-    execFileSync('git', ['config', 'user.name', 'Test'], { cwd: tmp, stdio: 'ignore' });
-    execFileSync('git', ['commit', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'init'], { cwd: tmp, stdio: 'ignore' });

-    const expectedSha = execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], {

-      encoding: 'utf8',
-    }).trim();

-    const before = makeFeature({ id: 'f', status: 'in-progress' });
-    const r = applyFeatureUpdate({

-      cwd: tmp,

-    expect(r.ok).toBe(true);

-      expect(expectedSha).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/);
-    }

-describe('verified gate — deferred tail', () => {
-  it('a feature with all-pass-except-deferred can reach verified (deferred derives pass)', () => {
-    // Design: `verified ⟸ audit.result === "pass"`, and deferred checks
-    // are excluded from the pass requirement. A feature with c1:pass + c2:deferred
-    // derives result:pass → can verify.
-    const before = makeFeature({
-      status: 'in-progress',
-      checks: [
-        { id: 'c1', description: 'x', validates: 'what', method: 'synthetic-test' },
-        { id: 'c2', description: 'y', validates: 'why', method: 'synthetic-test' },
-      ],
-    });
-    const r = applyFeatureUpdate({
-      before,
-      changes: {
-        status: 'verified',
-        audit: {
-          result: 'pass',
-          verdicts: [
-            { check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'pass' },
-            { check_id: 'c2', verdict: 'deferred', deferred_reason: 'requires live pilot', deferred_category: 'pilot' },
-          ],
-        },
-      },
-      catalogEntries: [],
-    });
-    expect(r.ok).toBe(true);
-    if (r.ok) {
-      expect(r.feature.status).toBe('verified');
-      expect(r.feature.audit?.result).toBe('pass');
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('a feature with a deferred + fail cannot verify (fail dominates, invariant reverts status)', () => {
-    const before = makeFeature({
-      status: 'in-progress',
-      checks: [
-        { id: 'c1', description: 'x', validates: 'what', method: 'synthetic-test' },
-        { id: 'c2', description: 'y', validates: 'why', method: 'synthetic-test' },
-      ],
-    });
-    const r = applyFeatureUpdate({
-      before,
-      changes: {
-        status: 'verified',
-        audit: {
-          result: 'pass',
-          verdicts: [
-            { check_id: 'c1', verdict: 'fail' },
-            { check_id: 'c2', verdict: 'deferred', deferred_reason: 'needs CI', deferred_category: 'ci' },
-          ],
-        },
-      },
-      catalogEntries: [],
-    });
-    // The update succeeds (ok: true) but enforceVerifiedInvariant reverts the

-    expect(r.ok).toBe(true);

-      expect(r.feature.status).not.toBe('verified');
-      expect(r.feature.audit?.result).toBe('fail');

-  it('all-deferred feature does NOT verify — zero machine-proven checks (caps to partial)', () => {

--- a/src/core/source-dirs.test.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,92 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * source-dirs.test.ts — the project-level "first-party source roots" resolver.
- *
- * tend historically hardcoded its OWN repo layout (`src/`, `schema/`, `skills/`,
- * …) in three independent scanners: the coverage walker, the audit-evidence
- * path filter, and the narrative-cite extractor. Any consuming project whose
- * code lives elsewhere (e.g. `petals/`) silently got zero coverage, dead
- * staleness detection, and unvalidated cites. This module is the single source
- * of truth those three scanners now read, configured per-project via the
- * garden's `source_dirs` field. These tests pin the resolver + the two regex
- * builders so the default (tend's own repo) is unchanged and an override works.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import {
-  DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS,
-  resolveSourceDirs,
-  buildEvidencePathPrefix,
-  buildCitePattern,
-} from './source-dirs.js';
-
-describe('resolveSourceDirs', () => {
-  it('returns the default first-party list when no config is present', () => {
-    expect(resolveSourceDirs(undefined)).toEqual(DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS);
-    expect(resolveSourceDirs(null)).toEqual(DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS);
-    expect(resolveSourceDirs({})).toEqual(DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS);
-  });
-
-  it('returns the configured dirs verbatim when set', () => {
-    expect(resolveSourceDirs({ source_dirs: ['petals'] })).toEqual(['petals']);
-    expect(resolveSourceDirs({ source_dirs: ['src', 'petals'] })).toEqual(['src', 'petals']);
-  });
-
-  it('trims surrounding whitespace from configured dirs', () => {
-    expect(resolveSourceDirs({ source_dirs: [' petals '] })).toEqual(['petals']);
-  });
-
-  it('falls back to default on invalid config (empty array, non-array, non-string, blank)', () => {
-    expect(resolveSourceDirs({ source_dirs: [] })).toEqual(DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS);
-    expect(resolveSourceDirs({ source_dirs: 'src' })).toEqual(DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS);
-    expect(resolveSourceDirs({ source_dirs: [123] })).toEqual(DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS);
-    expect(resolveSourceDirs({ source_dirs: ['   '] })).toEqual(DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS);
-  });
-
-  it('never returns a reference to the shared default array (caller can mutate safely)', () => {
-    const a = resolveSourceDirs(undefined);
-    expect(a).toEqual(DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS);
-    expect(a).not.toBe(DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS);
-  });
-});
-
-describe('buildEvidencePathPrefix', () => {
-  it('matches configured dirs plus the always-allowed tests/docs/dist', () => {
-    const re = buildEvidencePathPrefix(['petals']);
-    expect(re.test('petals/foo.ts')).toBe(true);
-    expect(re.test('tests/foo.test.ts')).toBe(true);
-    expect(re.test('docs/x.md')).toBe(true);
-    expect(re.test('dist/bundle.js')).toBe(true);
-    // src is not this project's source root, so a bare src/ path is not evidence.
-    expect(re.test('src/foo.ts')).toBe(false);
-    // Descriptive prose, not a path.
-    expect(re.test('a description of what happened')).toBe(false);
-  });
-
-  it('preserves tend default behavior, recognizing .github via its first segment', () => {
-    const re = buildEvidencePathPrefix(DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS);
-    expect(re.test('src/core/coverage.ts')).toBe(true);
-    expect(re.test('schema/polyglot.schema.json')).toBe(true);
-    expect(re.test('.github/workflows/ci.yml')).toBe(true);
-  });
-});
-
-describe('buildCitePattern', () => {
-  it('extracts backtick cites only for configured dirs', () => {
-    const re = buildCitePattern(['petals']);
-    expect('see `petals/foo.ts` and `src/bar.ts`'.match(re)).toEqual(['`petals/foo.ts`']);
-  });
-
-  it('matches the tend defaults', () => {
-    const re = buildCitePattern(DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS);
-    expect('`src/core/x.ts`'.match(re)).toEqual(['`src/core/x.ts`']);
-  });
-
-  it('returns a fresh global regex each call (no shared lastIndex across consumers)', () => {
-    const a = buildCitePattern(['src']);
-    const b = buildCitePattern(['src']);
-    expect(a).not.toBe(b);
-    expect(a.global).toBe(true);
-  });
-});

-/**
- * Tests for src/core/staleness.ts
- *
- * Covers:
- *   1. hashFile: deterministic, stable
- *   2. captureEvidenceSha: injects sha when file exists
- *   3. isVerdictStale: same content → not stale
- *   4. isVerdictStale: changed content → stale
- *   5. isVerdictStale: deleted file → stale with reason "evidence file missing"
- *   6. isVerdictStale: no evidence_path → not stale
- *   7. isVerdictStale: evidence_sha absent → not stale (pre-capture verdict)
- *   8. computeStaleness: multiple verdicts, only changed file flagged
- *   9. computeStaleness: verified feature with drifted file → signal emitted
- *  10. findStaleVerdicts: project-wide sweep
- *  11. AuditSignal union: discriminated by `type` (architecture assertion)
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
-import { writeFileSync, mkdirSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { join } from 'node:path';

-let tmpDir: string;
-
-beforeEach(() => {
-  tmpDir = join(tmpdir(), `staleness-test-${process.pid}-${Date.now()}`);
-  mkdirSync(tmpDir, { recursive: true });
-});
-
-afterEach(() => {
-  rmSync(tmpDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
-});
-
-function writeFile(name: string, content: string): string {
-  const p = join(tmpDir, name);
-  writeFileSync(p, content);
-  return p;
-}
-
-function makeFeature(overrides: Partial<Feature> = {}): Feature {
-  return { id: 'f', title: 'F', status: 'planned', ...overrides };
-}
-
-// ─── hashString ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('hashString', () => {
-  it('returns a 40-char SHA-1 hex string', () => {

-  it('is deterministic — same string, same hash', () => {

-  });
-
-  it('changes when the input string changes', () => {
-    expect(hashString('a')).not.toBe(hashString('b'));
-  });
-
-  it('matches Unix `shasum` for a known string (SHA-1 of "hello")', () => {
-    // echo -n hello | shasum  →  aaf4c61ddcc5e8a2dabede0f3b482cd9aea9434d
-    expect(hashString('hello')).toBe('aaf4c61ddcc5e8a2dabede0f3b482cd9aea9434d');
-  });
-
-  it('hashFile delegates to hashString — same digest for equal content', () => {
-    const content = 'shared bytes';
-    const p = writeFile('delegate.ts', content);
-    expect(hashFile(p)).toBe(hashString(content));
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── hashFile ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('hashFile', () => {

-  it('is deterministic — same file, same hash every call', () => {

-/**
- * Tests for src/core/tolerant-read.ts — tolerant readers.
- *
- * arch-b F3: runValidateTolerant bare catch swallows unexpected errors silently.
- * An exception from runValidate (TypeError, schema regression, permission error)
- * returns { valid: true, drift_verdict: 'clean' } — the cockpit shows GREEN when
- * the validation engine is actually broken. The fix: log the caught error to stderr
- * before returning the fallback, so operators can distinguish a crash from a benign
- * "project not initialised yet" ENOENT.
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect, vi, afterEach } from 'vitest';
-
-// ─── runValidateTolerant — unexpected error logging ──────────────────────────
-
-describe('runValidateTolerant — unexpected error logging (arch-b F3)', () => {
-  afterEach(() => {
-    vi.restoreAllMocks();
-    vi.resetModules();
-  });
-
-  it('logs the error to stderr when runValidate throws unexpectedly, then returns the clean fallback', async () => {
-    // Intercept the validate module so runValidate throws a TypeError — simulating
-    // a bug in the validation engine (not a benign file-not-found).
-    vi.mock('./validate.js', () => ({
-      runValidate: () => {
-        throw new TypeError('validator internal crash: Cannot read properties of undefined');
-      },
-      isBacklogWarning: () => false,
-      partitionWarnings: (ws: unknown[]) => ({ health: ws, coherence: [] }),
-    }));
-
-    // Pick up the mocked validate dependency.
-    const { runValidateTolerant } = await import('./tolerant-read.js');
-
-    const stderrSpy = vi.spyOn(process.stderr, 'write').mockImplementation(() => true);
-
-    const result = await runValidateTolerant('/some/cwd');
-
-    // The fallback must still be returned — callers must not crash.
-    expect(result.valid).toBe(true);
-    expect(result.drift_verdict).toBe('clean');
-
-    // RED (fails today): the bare catch {} never calls process.stderr.write.
-    // After the fix, at least one stderr.write call must occur containing the error.
-    expect(stderrSpy).toHaveBeenCalled();
-    const written = stderrSpy.mock.calls.map((c) => String(c[0])).join('');
-    expect(written).toContain('runValidateTolerant');
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── readCatalogTolerant — benign fallback (no logging required) ──────────────
-
-describe('readCatalogTolerant — benign fallback', () => {
-  afterEach(() => {
-    vi.resetModules();
-  });
-
-  it('returns an empty-catalog fallback when the catalog file does not exist', async () => {
-    const { readCatalogTolerant } = await import('./tolerant-read.js');
-    const result = await readCatalogTolerant('/tmp/__tend_no_catalog__');
-    expect(result.features).toEqual([]);
-    expect(result.schema_version).toBe('1');
-  });
-});
-
-// ─── readAllFeaturesTolerant — benign fallback (no logging required) ──────────
-
-describe('readAllFeaturesTolerant — benign fallback', () => {
-  afterEach(() => {
-    vi.resetModules();
-  });
-
-  it('returns an empty array when the features dir does not exist', async () => {
-    const { readAllFeaturesTolerant } = await import('./tolerant-read.js');
-    const result = await readAllFeaturesTolerant('/tmp/__tend_no_features__');
-    expect(result).toEqual([]);
-  });
-});

-/**
- * Tests for src/core/ui-html.ts
- *
- * Tests the pure helpers (buildHtml, serializeData) and the async functions
- * (writeUiTendHtml, refreshUiTendHtmlData) using a real temp directory.
- *
- * readBundleAssets is not tested directly because it reads dist/ui/assets/
- * which may not exist in the test environment. Tests that need a full bundle
- * use stub assets injected via buildHtml directly.
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
-import { mkdtemp, mkdir, readFile, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { join } from 'node:path';

-
-// Real Vite bundle location, relative to this source file at runtime.

-
-// ─── Fixtures ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-const STUB_ASSETS: BundleAssets = {

-let tmp: string;

-// ─── Test project scaffold ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-async function makeTendDirs(root: string): Promise<void> {
-  await mkdir(join(root, 'docs', 'tend', 'features'), { recursive: true });
-}
-
-/** Write a minimal garden polyglot so readCatalog succeeds. */
-async function writeTendHtml(root: string, catalog: Catalog): Promise<void> {
-  const { features, ...catalogBlock } = catalog;
-  const data = {
-    id: 'garden',
-    title: 'Test Garden',
-    status: 'planned',
-    catalog: catalogBlock,
-    features_aggregate: features,
-  };
-  const json = JSON.stringify(data, null, 2);
-  const text =
-    '<!doctype html>\n<html><body>\n' +
-    '<script id="oo-meta" type="application/json">\n{"kind":"garden","template_version":"1"}\n</script>\n' +
-    '<script id="oo-data" type="application/json">\n' +
-    json +
-    '\n</script>\n</body></html>\n';
-  await writeFile(join(root, 'docs', 'tend', 'overview.html'), text, 'utf8');
-}
-
-beforeEach(async () => {

-  await makeTendDirs(tmp);
-  await writeTendHtml(tmp, makeCatalog());

-afterEach(async () => {

-// ─── uiTendHtmlPath ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-// ─── serializeData ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-describe('serializeData', () => {

-    const result = serializeData(features, makeCatalog());

-// ─── buildHtml ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('buildHtml', () => {
-  it('produces a self-contained HTML document', () => {

-  it('is openable without errors — no unclosed script tags', () => {

-  it('is self-contained — embeds no external resource URLs (locked principle)', () => {

-// ─── no-server structural assertion (c006, unit half) ─────────────────────────
-//
-// c006 checks: "Static HTML means no port collisions" — `tend ui` must never
-// open a listening socket. This suite asserts that neither the HTML-assembly
-// module (src/core/ui-html.ts) nor the CLI entry-point (src/ui/generate.ts)
-// import or call HTTP/net server APIs — a fast, deterministic structural guard
-// against a server creeping in. It is the UNIT half of c006's evidence; the
-// integration half (real generate path → self-contained, file://-openable
-// artifact) lives in the "self-contained artifact (c006, integration half)"
-// suite below.
-//
-// Why structural (not lsof)?
-//   lsof is fragile in CI (requires root or procfs, races on fast exit). A
-//   structural assertion on the source is honest, specific, and fast at the
-//   unit level; the integration suite proves the positive behavior — the
-//   produced file is complete and reachable from a path with no network.
-
-describe('no-server structural assertion (c006)', () => {
-  it('src/core/ui-html.ts imports no HTTP/net server APIs', async () => {
-    const src = await import('node:fs/promises').then((m) =>
-      m.readFile(
-        new URL('../../src/core/ui-html.ts', import.meta.url),
-        'utf8',
-      ),
-    );
-    // None of these patterns should appear anywhere in the source.
-    const forbidden = [
-      /\bcreateServer\b/,
-      /\.listen\s*\(/,
-      /\bnet\.Server\b/,
-      /\bhttp\.Server\b/,
-      /\bhttps\.Server\b/,
-    ];
-    for (const pattern of forbidden) {
-      expect(src).not.toMatch(pattern);
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('src/ui/generate.ts imports no HTTP/net server APIs', async () => {
-    const src = await import('node:fs/promises').then((m) =>
-      m.readFile(
-        new URL('../../src/ui/generate.ts', import.meta.url),
-        'utf8',
-      ),
-    );
-    const forbidden = [
-      /\bcreateServer\b/,
-      /\.listen\s*\(/,
-      /\bnet\.Server\b/,
-      /\bhttp\.Server\b/,
-      /\bhttps\.Server\b/,
-    ];
-    for (const pattern of forbidden) {
-      expect(src).not.toMatch(pattern);
-    }
-  });
-});

-// ─── self-contained artifact (c006, integration half) ─────────────────────────
-//
-// c006's verification_recipe demands behavioral proof, not just a source grep:
-// "Run `tend ui` in a fixture project ... no listening process ... the generated
-// HTML opens from a `file://` URL with the network disabled." This suite drives
-// the REAL production write path — writeUiTendHtml(), which `tend ui` uses for
-// its default persistent output — against a real fixture project on disk, then
-// inspects the produced artifact:
-//
-//   - the full JS + CSS bundle is INLINED (no <script src>/<link href> that a
-//     browser would need to fetch),
-//   - no external URL and no server reference appear,
-//   - the embedded data block carries the fixture's feature, and
-//   - the file is reachable as a `file://` URL — i.e. it works opened directly
-//     from a path with no server and no network.
-//
-// It reads the real dist/ui/assets/ bundle (the same one shipped in the npm
-// package). If that bundle is absent (corrupt install / CI without a build),
-// the suite skips rather than emit a false failure — the unit half above still
-// guards against a server creeping in.
-describe.skipIf(!HAS_REAL_BUNDLE)('self-contained artifact (c006, integration half)', () => {
-  /** Scaffold a fixture project with a garden + one feature, return its root. */
-  async function scaffoldProject(): Promise<{ root: string; featureId: string }> {
-    const featureId = 'sample-feature';
-    // Garden is already written in beforeEach via writeTendHtml(tmp, makeCatalog()).
-    // Add one feature polyglot so the embedded data is non-trivial.
-    const feature = makeFeature({ id: featureId, title: 'Sample Feature', status: 'verified' });
-    const featurePath = join(tmp, 'docs', 'tend', 'features', `${featureId}.tend.html`);
-    const featureJson = JSON.stringify(feature).replace(/<\/script/g, '<\\/script');
-    const featureHtml =
-      '<!doctype html>\n<html><body>\n' +
-      '<script id="oo-data" type="application/json">\n' +
-      featureJson +
-      '\n</script>\n</body></html>\n';
-    await writeFile(featurePath, featureHtml, 'utf8');
-    return { root: tmp, featureId };
-  }
-
-  it('writeUiTendHtml produces a fully self-contained, file://-openable artifact (no server, no network)', async () => {
-    const { root, featureId } = await scaffoldProject();
-
-    // Drive the REAL production path — reads the real Vite bundle, embeds the
-    // real on-disk data, writes docs/tend/board.html atomically. Same function
-    // `tend ui` calls for its persistent output.
-    const features = await import('./files.js').then((m) => m.readAllFeatures(root));
-    const catalog = await import('./files.js').then((m) => m.readCatalog(root));
-    const writtenPath = await writeUiTendHtml({ cwd: root, features, catalog });
-
-    expect(writtenPath).toBe(uiTendHtmlPath(root));
-
-    const html = await readFile(writtenPath, 'utf8');
-    const assets = readBundleAssets();
-
-    // 1. The real JS + CSS bundle is INLINED — a browser fetches nothing.
-    expect(html).toContain(assets.css);
-    expect(html).toContain(assets.js);
-
-    // 2. No FETCHABLE external sub-resource — this is the offline-rendering
-    //    property, the claim that matters for c006. Inert string URLs inside the
-    //    inlined JS (e.g. React's "https://react.dev/errors/" doc links) are NOT
-    //    fetched and do not break offline use, so a blunt "no https:// substring"
-    //    check would be wrong. We assert the real thing: no <script src>, no
-    //    <link href>, and no CSS @import of an external URL.
-    expect(html).not.toMatch(/<script[^>]*\ssrc\s*=/i);
-    expect(html).not.toMatch(/<link[^>]*\shref\s*=/i);
-    expect(html).not.toMatch(/@import\s+(?:url\()?["']?https?:\/\//i);
-
-    // 3. The embedded data block carries the fixture's feature.
-    const m = /<script id="tend-data" type="application\/json">([\s\S]*?)<\/script>/.exec(html);
-    expect(m).not.toBeNull();
-    const data = JSON.parse(m![1]!) as { features: Feature[] };
-    expect(data.features.some((f) => f.id === featureId)).toBe(true);
-
-    // 4. The artifact opens from a `file://` URL — reachable from a path with no
-    //    network. The file:// URL resolves to the exact bytes we wrote.
-    const fileUrl = pathToFileURL(writtenPath);
-    expect(fileUrl.protocol).toBe('file:');
-    const viaFileUrl = await readFile(fileUrl, 'utf8');
-    expect(viaFileUrl).toBe(html);
-  });
-});

deleted file mode 100644
index 0de207d..0000000
--- a/src/core/write-queue.test.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,89 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * Tests for src/core/write-queue.ts — in-process write serialization.
- *
- * The MCP server is one process; every tend_* write handler does a
- * read-modify-write on the shared garden (features_aggregate + health_snapshot).
- * withFileLock makes each write atomic but does NOT serialize the
- * read→modify→write span, so concurrent handlers lose each other's updates
- * (last-writer-wins). serializeWrite is the in-process mutex that closes that
- * span. These tests reproduce the lost-update and assert the queue prevents it.
- */
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { serializeWrite } from './write-queue.js';
-
-describe('serializeWrite — in-process write serialization', () => {
-  it('runs queued tasks strictly sequentially — never two at once, in FIFO order', async () => {
-    let active = 0;
-    let maxActive = 0;
-    const order: number[] = [];
-    const task = (n: number) =>
-      serializeWrite(async () => {
-        active++;
-        maxActive = Math.max(maxActive, active);
-        await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5));
-        order.push(n);
-        active--;
-      });
-    await Promise.all([task(1), task(2), task(3), task(4)]);
-    expect(maxActive).toBe(1); // never two critical sections overlapping
-    expect(order).toEqual([1, 2, 3, 4]); // FIFO
-  });
-
-  it('prevents lost updates on a concurrent read-modify-write (the garden race)', async () => {
-    // Each writer reads a shared snapshot, awaits (the window where an
-    // unserialized writer would race), then writes snapshot+n. Without
-    // serialization all 8 read [] and the last write wins → 7 lost.
-    const shared = { items: [] as number[] };
-    const readModifyWrite = (n: number) =>
-      serializeWrite(async () => {
-        const snapshot = shared.items.slice();
-        await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2));
-        shared.items = [...snapshot, n];
-      });
-    await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: 8 }, (_, i) => readModifyWrite(i)));
-    expect(shared.items.sort((a, b) => a - b)).toEqual([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]);
-  });
-
-  it('releases the lock when a task throws, so the next task still runs', async () => {
-    const ran: string[] = [];
-    const a = serializeWrite(async () => {
-      throw new Error('boom');
-    }).catch(() => ran.push('a-failed'));
-    const b = serializeWrite(async () => {
-      ran.push('b-ran');
-    });
-    await Promise.all([a, b]);
-    expect(ran).toEqual(['a-failed', 'b-ran']);
-  });
-
-  it('returns the task result to the caller', async () => {
-    const r = await serializeWrite(async () => 42);
-    expect(r).toBe(42);
-  });
-
-  // arch-a F9: no timeout — a hung task blocks the queue forever.
-  // Fix: serializeWrite should reject tasks that don't settle within a reasonable
-  // deadline (30 s in production; a much shorter one in tests) so the queue
-  // never wedges the entire MCP write surface.
-  it('rejects a task that exceeds the timeout and keeps the queue alive (arch-a F9)', async () => {
-    // A promise that never resolves — simulates deadlocked I/O or an infinite loop.
-    const neverResolves = () => new Promise<never>(() => { /* hang forever */ });
-
-    // With a 30 s timeout in production we can't wait that long in a test.
-    // serializeWrite must accept an optional timeout parameter (ms) so callers can
-    // control it; the default is 30 000.
-    // RED: today serializeWrite has no timeout parameter — the call signature only
-    // accepts a task factory. This assertion will fail at compile time (TS) or at
-    // runtime with the current implementation because the hung task never rejects.
-    //
-    // We test with a very short timeout (50 ms) to keep the test fast.
-    const hangPromise = serializeWrite(neverResolves, 50);
-
-    // The hung task must reject within ~50 ms, not hang the test runner.
-    await expect(hangPromise).rejects.toThrow(/timed? ?out/i);
-
-    // The queue must still be usable after the timed-out task:
-    const afterHang = await serializeWrite(async () => 'queue-alive');
-    expect(afterHang).toBe('queue-alive');
-  }, 5_000); // test-level timeout: 5 s to catch an infinite hang
-});
