-# OO:SHELL:START
-# template_version: 3
-#
-# Tend polyglot shell core.
-#
-# Five built-in verbs + custom-verb fallback. Bash drives the polyglot's own
-# runtime — reading itself, building itself, verifying itself. Anything that
-# touches multiple files (validate, aggregate, sync, refresh-refs) lives in
-# the MCP server or CLI, not here.
-#
-# Built-ins:
-#   data    Dump oo-data as JSON for jq piping
-#   status  Quick text overview (id, title, status, kind, progress)
-#   help    List available verbs (including any custom ones)
-#   run     Orchestrate the build: iterate steps[], invoke agent per step, smoke
-#   smoke   Run oo-data.smoke.cmd; exit 0/non-0
-#
-# Extension point:
-#   cmd_<verb>  Custom-verb fallback — define a cmd_<name> function in
-#               OO:CUSTOM and it becomes invocable as `bash file <name>`.
-set -euo pipefail
-
-SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
-case "$SELF" in
-  /*) ;;
-  *) SELF="$(cd "$(dirname "$SELF")" && pwd)/$(basename "$SELF")" ;;
-esac
-SELF_BASE="$(basename "$SELF")"
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# Block extraction
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-# Extract raw JSON between <script id="..." type="application/json"> and the
-# next </script> (markers excluded). Writes to stdout.
-_extract_block() {
-  local file="$1" block_id="$2"
-  awk -v id="$block_id" '
-    $0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*<script id=\"" id "\" type=\"application/json\">$" { in_block=1; next }
-    in_block && /^[[:space:]]*<\/script>$/ { exit }
-    in_block { print }
-  ' "$file"
-}
-
-# Extract a scalar field from a named block via jq.
-_extract_block_field() {
-  local file="$1" block="$2" field="$3"
-  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-    echo "error: jq is required for $field extraction" >&2
-    return 1
-  fi
-  _extract_block "$file" "$block" | jq -r ".${field} // empty"
-}
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# Identity (read live from oo-data and oo-meta)
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-FEATURE_ID="$(_extract_block_field "$SELF" "oo-data" "id" 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
-TITLE="$(_extract_block_field "$SELF" "oo-data" "title" 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
-STATUS="$(_extract_block_field "$SELF" "oo-data" "status" 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
-KIND="$(_extract_block_field "$SELF" "oo-meta" "kind" 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# cmd_data — dump oo-data JSON to stdout
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-cmd_data() {
-  _extract_block "$SELF" "oo-data"
-}
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# cmd_status — one-line identity + progress
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-cmd_status() {
-  local impl_pct verif_pct
-  if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-    impl_pct="$(_extract_block "$SELF" "oo-data" | jq -r '.progress.implementation // 0')"
-    verif_pct="$(_extract_block "$SELF" "oo-data" | jq -r '.progress.verification // 0')"
-  else
-    impl_pct="-"; verif_pct="-"
-  fi
-  printf '%s · %s · %s · %s · impl %s%% · verif %s%%\n' \
-    "${FEATURE_ID:-?}" "${TITLE:-?}" "${STATUS:-?}" "${KIND:-?}" "$impl_pct" "$verif_pct"
-}
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# cmd_help — list verbs (including any custom-verb additions)
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-cmd_help() {
-  cat <<EOF
-tend ${KIND:-artifact}: ${FEATURE_ID:-(unknown)}
-${TITLE:-}
-
-usage: bash $SELF_BASE [VERB]
-
-built-in verbs:
-  data         Dump oo-data as JSON (pipe to jq)
-  status       One-line status to stdout
-  run          Orchestrate the build: iterate steps[], invoke agent per step, run smoke
-  smoke        Run oo-data.smoke.cmd; exit 0/non-0
-  help         Show this
-
-EOF
-
-  # List custom verbs (cmd_* functions besides the built-ins).
-  local custom_verbs
-  custom_verbs="$(declare -F | awk '{print $3}' | grep -E '^cmd_' \
-    | grep -vxE 'cmd_data|cmd_status|cmd_help|cmd_run|cmd_smoke|cmd_default' \
-    | sed 's/^cmd_/  /; s/_/-/g' || true)"
-  if [ -n "$custom_verbs" ]; then
-    cat <<EOF
-custom verbs:
-$custom_verbs
-
-EOF
-  fi
-
-  cat <<EOF
-env:
-  TEND_AGENT_CMD=${TEND_AGENT_CMD:-claude -p}
-
-multi-file ops (validate, aggregate, sync) live in:
-  tend <verb>           CLI
-  tend_<verb>           MCP server
-EOF
-}
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# cmd_default — friendly landing when run with no args
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-cmd_default() {
-  cmd_help
-}
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# cmd_smoke — run oo-data.smoke.cmd; exit 0/non-0
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-cmd_smoke() {
-  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-    echo "error: jq is required for smoke" >&2
-    return 1
-  fi
-  local data smoke_cmd
-  data="$(_extract_block "$SELF" "oo-data")"
-  smoke_cmd="$(printf '%s' "$data" | jq -r '.smoke.cmd // empty')"
-  if [ -z "$smoke_cmd" ]; then
-    echo "smoke: no cmd configured" >&2
-    return 1
-  fi
-  echo "[smoke] $smoke_cmd"
-  eval "$smoke_cmd"
-}
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# cmd_run — orchestrate the build: iterate steps, invoke agent per step, smoke
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-#
-# The polyglot is the orchestrator; the agent CLI is the worker. Steps are
-# read from oo-data.steps[]. Each step's description is piped to the agent
-# command on stdin. Any step that exits non-zero halts the run and the
-# trailing smoke step does NOT execute.
-#
-# Agent command resolution order:
-#   1. oo-data.execute.agent_cmd  (file-level override)
-#   2. TEND_AGENT_CMD             (env override)
-#   3. claude -p                  (default)
-cmd_run() {
-  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-    echo "error: jq is required for run" >&2
-    return 1
-  fi
-  local data agent_cmd step step_id step_desc step_first_line
-  local -a agent_arr
-  data="$(_extract_block "$SELF" "oo-data")"
-
-  agent_cmd="$(printf '%s' "$data" | jq -r '.execute.agent_cmd // empty')"
-  if [ -z "$agent_cmd" ]; then
-    agent_cmd="${TEND_AGENT_CMD:-claude -p}"
-  fi
-  read -ra agent_arr <<< "$agent_cmd"
-
-  while IFS= read -r step; do
-    step_id="$(printf '%s' "$step" | jq -r '.id')"
-    step_desc="$(printf '%s' "$step" | jq -r '.description // .title // ""')"
-    step_first_line="$(printf '%s' "$step_desc" | head -1)"
-    echo "[step ${step_id}] ${step_first_line}"
-    if ! printf '%s' "$step_desc" | "${agent_arr[@]}"; then
-      echo "error: step ${step_id} failed" >&2
-      return 1
-    fi
-  done < <(printf '%s' "$data" | jq -c '.steps[]?')
-
-  cmd_smoke
-}
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# Dispatcher
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-case "${1:-}" in
-  "")             cmd_default ;;
-  data)           shift; cmd_data "$@" ;;
-  status)         shift; cmd_status "$@" ;;
-  help|-h|--help) shift; cmd_help "$@" ;;
-  run)            shift; cmd_run "$@" ;;
-  smoke)          shift; cmd_smoke "$@" ;;
-  *)
-    # Custom-verb fallback — look for a function named cmd_<verb> defined in
-    # OO:CUSTOM or appended by a project-local extension.
-    verb="${1//-/_}"; shift
-    if declare -F "cmd_$verb" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-      "cmd_$verb" "$@"
-    else
-      echo "unknown verb: ${verb//_/-}" >&2
-      cmd_help
-      exit 1
-    fi
-    ;;
-esac
-
-# OO:SHELL:END
diff --git a/tests/bash/run-verb.sh b/tests/bash/run-verb.sh
deleted file mode 100755
index b723ca1..0000000
--- a/tests/bash/run-verb.sh
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,119 +0,0 @@
-#!/usr/bin/env bash
-# Tests for the `run` verb in polyglot tend artifacts.
-# RED: all tests must FAIL before implementation, PASS after.
-set -uo pipefail
-
-FIXTURE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/fixtures" && pwd)/run-fixture.tend.html"
-
-pass=0
-fail=0
-
-_assert() {
-  local desc="$1" ok="$2"
-  if [ "$ok" -eq 0 ]; then
-    echo "PASS: $desc"
-    pass=$((pass + 1))
-  else
-    echo "FAIL: $desc"
-    fail=$((fail + 1))
-  fi
-}
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# Test 1 — happy path: TEND_AGENT_CMD=cat echoes step descriptions + smoke runs
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# `cat` reads stdin and writes it to stdout — so each step's description
-# appears in output. Smoke cmd is `echo smoke-ok`.
-
-rc1=0
-out1="$(TEND_AGENT_CMD=cat bash "$FIXTURE" run 2>&1)" || rc1=$?
-
-_assert "happy path: step 1 description in output" \
-  "$(echo "$out1" | grep -q 'step one work' && echo 0 || echo 1)"
-_assert "happy path: step 2 description in output" \
-  "$(echo "$out1" | grep -q 'step two work' && echo 0 || echo 1)"
-_assert "happy path: smoke ran (smoke-ok in output)" \
-  "$(echo "$out1" | grep -q 'smoke-ok' && echo 0 || echo 1)"
-_assert "happy path: exit 0" \
-  "$([ "$rc1" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# Test 2 — stop on failure: TEND_AGENT_CMD=false → step fails → smoke skipped
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# `false` exits non-zero for every input. First step fails; smoke must NOT run.
-
-rc2=0
-out2="$(TEND_AGENT_CMD=false bash "$FIXTURE" run 2>&1)" || rc2=$?
-
-_assert "stop on failure: smoke did NOT run" \
-  "$(echo "$out2" | grep -q 'smoke-ok' && echo 1 || echo 0)"
-_assert "stop on failure: exit non-zero" \
-  "$([ "$rc2" -ne 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# Test 3 — multi-word agent command: flags in TEND_AGENT_CMD arrive as
-#           separate, correctly-preserved arguments (no glob expansion).
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# The bug: `printf ... | $agent_cmd` — unquoted $agent_cmd is subject to bash
-# word-splitting AND glob expansion.  A command string like
-#   "bash /path/stub.sh --pattern *"
-# has its literal "*" expanded to all files in cwd, corrupting the arg list.
-# The array fix (`read -ra agent_arr; "${agent_arr[@]}"`) prevents glob
-# expansion because "${agent_arr[@]}" is a quoted expansion.
-#
-# Strategy: pass TEND_AGENT_CMD="<stub> --pattern *".  A stub records its
-# argv to a file.  Assert the stub receives exactly "--pattern" and "*"
-# as its two args (not a glob-expanded list of cwd files).
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-STUB_SCRIPT3="$(mktemp /tmp/tend-run-stub3-XXXXXX.sh)"
-STUB_ARGS_FILE3="$(mktemp /tmp/tend-run-args3-XXXXXX.txt)"
-
-cat > "$STUB_SCRIPT3" <<'STUB_EOF'
-#!/usr/bin/env bash
-# Record argv count and first two args; echo stdin so step content appears.
-echo "$#" >> "$STUB_ARGS_FILE3"
-printf '%s\n' "$@" >> "$STUB_ARGS_FILE3"
-cat
-STUB_EOF
-chmod +x "$STUB_SCRIPT3"
-
-rc3=0
-out3="$(STUB_ARGS_FILE3="$STUB_ARGS_FILE3" \
-        TEND_AGENT_CMD="bash $STUB_SCRIPT3 --pattern *" \
-        bash "$FIXTURE" run 2>&1)" || rc3=$?
-
-# The stub is called once per step (2 steps total). Read the args from the
-# first invocation (lines 1-3: argc, arg1, arg2).
-argc3="$(sed -n '1p' "$STUB_ARGS_FILE3" 2>/dev/null)"
-arg1_3="$(sed -n '2p' "$STUB_ARGS_FILE3" 2>/dev/null)"
-arg2_3="$(sed -n '3p' "$STUB_ARGS_FILE3" 2>/dev/null)"
-rm -f "$STUB_SCRIPT3" "$STUB_ARGS_FILE3"
-
-_assert "multi-word agent cmd: run exits 0" \
-  "$([ "$rc3" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
-
-_assert "multi-word agent cmd: --pattern flag preserved as separate arg (arg1)" \
-  "$([ "$arg1_3" = "--pattern" ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
-
-_assert "multi-word agent cmd: '*' literal preserved (not glob-expanded) as arg2" \
-  "$([ "$arg2_3" = "*" ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
-
-_assert "multi-word agent cmd: exactly 2 args passed to stub (not glob-expanded to many)" \
-  "$([ "$argc3" = "2" ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
-
-_assert "multi-word agent cmd: step descriptions reached stdin" \
-  "$(echo "$out3" | grep -q 'step one work' && echo 0 || echo 1)"
-
-_assert "multi-word agent cmd: smoke still ran" \
-  "$(echo "$out3" | grep -q 'smoke-ok' && echo 0 || echo 1)"
-
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# Summary
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-echo ""
-echo "Results: $pass passed, $fail failed"
-if [ "$fail" -gt 0 ]; then
-  exit 1
-fi
-exit 0

diff --git a/tests/e2e/dogfood-render.spec.ts b/tests/e2e/dogfood-render.spec.ts
deleted file mode 100644
index a41f5e6..0000000
--- a/tests/e2e/dogfood-render.spec.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,81 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * E2E render tests for the canonical dogfood polyglots in docs/tend/features/.
- *
- * Each .tend.html file ships in the repo. We verify that:
- *  1. JSDOM can parse the inner HTML.
- *  2. The article populates at least one section (renderers ran).
- *  3. The rail mount has content (rail renderer ran).
- *  4. No console.error from the engine.
- *
- * Strategy: extract the HTML between the OO_HTML bash heredoc markers, load
- * into JSDOM with runScripts: 'dangerously', wait for the master render loop to
- * settle (Promise resolution + a tick), then assert structural facts.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll } from 'vitest';
-import { JSDOM, VirtualConsole } from 'jsdom';
-import { readFileSync, existsSync, readdirSync } from 'fs';
-import { resolve } from 'path';
-
-const REPO_ROOT = resolve(__dirname, '../..');
-const FEATURES_DIR = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'docs/tend/features');
-const GARDEN_PATH = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'docs/tend/overview.html');
-
-function extractInnerHtml(polyglotText: string): string {
-  const m = polyglotText.match(/: << 'OO_HTML'\n([\s\S]+?)\nOO_HTML/);
-  if (!m) throw new Error('not a polyglot: missing OO_HTML markers');
-  return m[1];
-}
-
-async function loadInJsdom(file: string) {
-  const innerHtml = extractInnerHtml(readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
-  const virtualConsole = new VirtualConsole();
-  const errors: string[] = [];
-  virtualConsole.on('jsdomError', (e) => errors.push(String(e?.message ?? e)));
-  virtualConsole.on('error', (...args) => errors.push(args.map(String).join(' ')));
-  const dom = new JSDOM(innerHtml, {
-    runScripts: 'dangerously',
-    resources: 'usable',
-    url: 'http://localhost/',
-    virtualConsole,
-  });
-  // Wait for master loop to run.
-  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 150));
-  return { doc: dom.window.document, errors };
-}
-
-describe('dogfood polyglot rendering', () => {
-  const featurePolyglots = existsSync(FEATURES_DIR)
-    ? readdirSync(FEATURES_DIR).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.tend.html')).map((f) => resolve(FEATURES_DIR, f))
-    : [];
-
-  it('at least one feature polyglot is present', () => {
-    expect(featurePolyglots.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
-  });
-
-  for (const file of featurePolyglots) {
-    const name = file.split('/').pop()!;
-    it(`feature polyglot renders: ${name}`, async () => {
-      const { doc, errors } = await loadInJsdom(file);
-      const sections = doc.querySelectorAll('article#article section');
-      const rail = doc.querySelector('[data-rail-mount]');
-      expect(sections.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
-      expect(rail).toBeTruthy();
-      expect(rail!.innerHTML.trim().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
-      // Engine fatal errors only (not jsdom CSS warnings).
-      const fatal = errors.filter((e) => /TypeError|ReferenceError|SyntaxError/.test(e));
-      expect(fatal).toEqual([]);
-    });
-  }
-
-  if (existsSync(GARDEN_PATH)) {
-    it('garden polyglot renders', async () => {
-      const { doc, errors } = await loadInJsdom(GARDEN_PATH);
-      const sections = doc.querySelectorAll('article#article section');
-      expect(sections.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
-      const fatal = errors.filter((e) => /TypeError|ReferenceError|SyntaxError/.test(e));
-      expect(fatal).toEqual([]);
-    });
-  }
-});
diff --git a/tests/e2e/mcp-stdio.spec.ts b/tests/e2e/mcp-stdio.spec.ts
deleted file mode 100644
index db0f0e4..0000000
--- a/tests/e2e/mcp-stdio.spec.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,271 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * Real stdio MCP integration test.
- *
- * Spawns `node dist/bin/tend.js serve` as an actual child process, speaks the
- * MCP JSON-RPC protocol over stdin/stdout, and asserts integration-level
- * behavior that in-process / mock-server tests cannot reach:
- *
- *   1. The server starts over stdio and produces a valid `initialize` response.
- *   2. `tools/list` returns EXACTLY the 11 canonical tool names — no more,
- *      no less.  Dropping or adding a registerXTools call breaks this.
- *   3. All server output lands on stdout, the banner lands on stderr.  stdout
- *      stays clean (valid JSON-RPC only).
- *   4. `tend_validate` responds over the real transport with a structured
- *      result, proving full request/response round-trips at integration depth.
- *
- * Evidence scope:
- *   cli-serve  c001 — server starts via stdio, responds to initialize + tools/list
- *   cli-serve  c010 / mcp-server c010 — stdout clean, banner on stderr only
- *   mcp-server c001 — 11 tools registered, served over stdio
- *   mcp-server.tool-inventory c001 — exact tool name set matches canonical list
- *   mcp-server.tool-inventory c002 — exhaustiveness: bogus tool not in list
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect, afterEach } from 'vitest';
-import { spawn, type ChildProcess } from 'node:child_process';
-import { mkdtemp, mkdir, writeFile, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';
-
-// ─── Canonical tool inventory ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
-// Source of truth: src/mcp/tools/index.ts.  This list MUST equal the set of
-// tool names registered by registerAllTools().  If any registration call is
-// removed or renamed, the test fails — that is the point.
-
-export const CANONICAL_TOOLS = [
-  'tend_aggregate',
-  'tend_create_feature',
-  'tend_delete_feature',
-  'tend_get_context',
-  'tend_get_gaps',
-  'tend_get_next',
-  'tend_get_unblocked',
-  'tend_output_execution_plan',
-  'tend_update_catalog',
-  'tend_update_feature',
-  'tend_validate',
-] as const;
-
-// ─── Minimal tend project scaffold ───────────────────────────────────────────
-// Enough for the server to start and answer tend_validate without path errors.
-
-async function scaffoldTendProject(root: string): Promise<void> {
-  await mkdir(join(root, 'docs', 'tend', 'features'), { recursive: true });
-  await mkdir(join(root, 'docs', 'tend', 'adapters'), { recursive: true });
-
-  const gardenData = {
-    id: 'garden',
-    title: 'Test Garden',
-    status: 'planned',
-    catalog: {
-      schema_version: '1',
-      project_id: 'test',
-      status: 'draft',
-    },
-    features_aggregate: [],
-  };
-
-  const gardenHtml =
-    '<!doctype html><html><body>\n' +
-    '<script id="oo-meta" type="application/json">\n' +
-    '{"kind":"garden","template_version":"1"}\n' +
-    '</script>\n' +
-    '<script id="oo-data" type="application/json">\n' +
-    JSON.stringify(gardenData, null, 2) +
-    '\n</script>\n</body></html>\n';
-
-  await writeFile(join(root, 'docs', 'tend', 'overview.html'), gardenHtml, 'utf8');
-}
-
-// ─── JSON-RPC framing over child process stdio ────────────────────────────────
-
-interface JsonRpcResponse {
-  jsonrpc: '2.0';
-  id: number | string;
-  result?: unknown;
-  error?: { code: number; message: string };
-}
-
-class McpStdioClient {
-  private proc: ChildProcess;
-  private buf = '';
-  private pending = new Map<number, (r: JsonRpcResponse) => void>();
-  private nextId = 1;
-  readonly stderr: string[] = [];
-
-  constructor(cwd: string) {
-    const tendBin = resolve(__dirname, '../../dist/bin/tend.js');
-    this.proc = spawn('node', [tendBin, 'serve'], {
-      cwd,
-      stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
-    });
-
-    this.proc.stdout!.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => {
-      this.buf += chunk.toString('utf8');
-      let nl: number;
-      while ((nl = this.buf.indexOf('\n')) !== -1) {
-        const line = this.buf.slice(0, nl).trim();
-        this.buf = this.buf.slice(nl + 1);
-        if (!line) continue;
-        let msg: JsonRpcResponse;
-        try {
-          msg = JSON.parse(line) as JsonRpcResponse;
-        } catch {
-          // Non-JSON on stdout is itself a test failure — collected for assertion
-          this.stderr.push(`[STDOUT-NON-JSON] ${line}`);
-          continue;
-        }
-        if (msg.id != null) {
-          const resolve = this.pending.get(msg.id as number);
-          if (resolve) {
-            this.pending.delete(msg.id as number);
-            resolve(msg);
-          }
-        }
-      }
-    });
-
-    this.proc.stderr!.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => {
-      this.stderr.push(chunk.toString('utf8'));
-    });
-  }
-
-  send(method: string, params: unknown = {}, id?: number): Promise<JsonRpcResponse> {
-    const callId = id ?? this.nextId++;
-    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
-      this.pending.set(callId, resolve);
-      const msg = JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: callId, method, params }) + '\n';
-      this.proc.stdin!.write(msg, (err) => { if (err) reject(err); });
-      // Safety timeout so a hanging test doesn't block the suite
-      setTimeout(() => {
-        if (this.pending.has(callId)) {
-          this.pending.delete(callId);
-          reject(new Error(`MCP call "${method}" timed out after 8s`));
-        }
-      }, 8000);
-    });
-  }
-
-  notify(method: string): void {
-    const msg = JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', method }) + '\n';
-    this.proc.stdin!.write(msg);
-  }
-
-  async close(): Promise<void> {
-    this.proc.stdin!.end();
-    await new Promise<void>((res) => {
-      const t = setTimeout(() => { this.proc.kill('SIGTERM'); res(); }, 2000);
-      this.proc.on('exit', () => { clearTimeout(t); res(); });
-    });
-  }
-}
-
-// ─── Fixture lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-let tmp: string;
-let client: McpStdioClient;
-
-afterEach(async () => {
-  await client?.close().catch(() => { /* already dead */ });
-  if (tmp) await rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
-});
-
-// ─── Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('mcp stdio integration', () => {
-  it(
-    'initializes over stdio and lists exactly the 11 canonical tools',
-    { timeout: 20_000 },
-    async () => {
-      // Scaffold a minimal project and point the server at it via cwd.
-      tmp = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'tend-stdio-test-'));
-      await scaffoldTendProject(tmp);
-
-      client = new McpStdioClient(tmp);
-
-      // ── 1. initialize handshake ───────────────────────────────────────────
-      const initResp = await client.send('initialize', {
-        protocolVersion: '2024-11-05',
-        capabilities: {},
-        clientInfo: { name: 'tend-stdio-test', version: '1.0.0' },
-      });
-
-      expect(initResp.error).toBeUndefined();
-      expect(initResp.result).toBeDefined();
-      const serverInfo = (initResp.result as { serverInfo?: { name?: string } }).serverInfo;
-      expect(serverInfo?.name).toBe('tend');
-
-      // ── 2. initialized notification (completes the handshake) ─────────────
-      client.notify('notifications/initialized');
-
-      // ── 3. tools/list — the integration-level claim ───────────────────────
-      const listResp = await client.send('tools/list', {});
-
-      expect(listResp.error).toBeUndefined();
-
-      const tools = (listResp.result as { tools?: Array<{ name: string }> }).tools ?? [];
-      const names = tools.map((t) => t.name).sort();
-
-      // Assert exact set equality: same count AND same names.
-      expect(names).toHaveLength(CANONICAL_TOOLS.length);
-      expect(names).toEqual([...CANONICAL_TOOLS].sort());
-
-      // ── 4. stdout clean — all output is valid JSON-RPC (negctrl companion) ─
-      // If anything non-JSON landed on stdout the client already pushed it to
-      // stderr[] with the [STDOUT-NON-JSON] prefix.  Assert that list is empty.
-      const stdoutCorruption = client.stderr.filter((s) => s.startsWith('[STDOUT-NON-JSON]'));
-      expect(stdoutCorruption).toEqual([]);
-
-      // ── 5. banner on stderr only ──────────────────────────────────────────
-      const stderrText = client.stderr.filter((s) => !s.startsWith('[STDOUT-NON-JSON]')).join('');
-      expect(stderrText).toMatch(/tools registered/);
-    },
-  );
-
-  it(
-    'serves tend_validate over real stdio transport (round-trip proof)',
-    { timeout: 20_000 },
-    async () => {
-      tmp = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'tend-stdio-validate-'));
-      await scaffoldTendProject(tmp);
-
-      client = new McpStdioClient(tmp);
-
-      // Handshake
-      await client.send('initialize', {
-        protocolVersion: '2024-11-05',
-        capabilities: {},
-        clientInfo: { name: 'tend-stdio-test', version: '1.0.0' },
-      });
-      client.notify('notifications/initialized');
-
-      // Call tend_validate through the real transport
-      const resp = await client.send('tools/call', {
-        name: 'tend_validate',
-        arguments: {},
-      });
-
-      expect(resp.error).toBeUndefined();
-      const content = (resp.result as { content?: Array<{ type: string; text: string }> }).content;
-      expect(Array.isArray(content)).toBe(true);

-/**
- * Unit tests for the universal renderer (`templates/_partials/oo-render.js`).
- *
- * Asserts the presence-driven contract:
- *   - Schema field is present in data → section renders.
- *   - Schema field is absent or empty → section is omitted (auto-elide).
- *   - No kind switch: garden / feature / subpage all use the same renderer;
- *     what differs is WHICH optional fields the data populates.
- *
- * The renderer is loaded via Node require (UMD wrapper). No DOM needed.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll } from 'vitest';
-import { resolve } from 'path';
-
-const PARTIALS = resolve(__dirname, '../../templates/_partials');
-
-// The renderer's UMD factory exports renderPage when required from CJS.
-// oo-render.js requires oo-helpers.js relative to itself, which works under
-// vitest because the partials dir is co-located.
-// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-var-requires
-const OoRender = require(resolve(PARTIALS, 'oo-render.js'));
-
-const META_FEATURE = { kind: 'feature', generated_at: '2026-05-15T00:00:00Z' };
-const META_GARDEN = { kind: 'garden', generated_at: '2026-05-15T00:00:00Z' };
-const META_SUBPAGE = { kind: 'subpage', generated_at: '2026-05-15T00:00:00Z' };
-
-function call(data: any, meta: any = META_FEATURE) {
-  return OoRender.renderPage(data, meta);
-}
-

-  it('handles null / undefined data gracefully', () => {

-    const result2 = OoRender.renderPage(undefined, {});

-    expect(result2.main).toBe('');

-});

-// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-// Friction 7 — per-check truth sub-label in the rail.
-//
-// The ONLY degraded-verdict signal recorded IN oo-data at render time is
-// `validates_job_satisfied === false` (the test passes mechanically but does
-// NOT assert the bound persona-job's measurable). Mock-only + staleness are
-// computed server-side at validate time and never persisted onto the verdict —
-// so the renderer honestly cannot surface them (see the code comment in
-// renderChecks). This block pins the honest behavior: the job-unsatisfied
-// sub-label renders; nothing fabricates a mock/stale label.
-// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-
-describe('Rail — per-check truth sub-label (friction 7)', () => {
-  it('adds a muted "job not asserted" sub-label on a check whose verdict has validates_job_satisfied:false', () => {

-        ],
-      },
-    });
-    expect(rail).toMatch(/detail-criterion__sublabel/);
-    expect(rail).toMatch(/job not asserted/);
-  });
-
-  it('does NOT add the sub-label when validates_job_satisfied is true', () => {
-    const { rail } = call({
-      what: 'x',
-      checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'a check', validates: 'what', status: 'satisfied' }],

-        verdicts: [

-        ],
-      },
-    });
-    expect(rail).not.toMatch(/detail-criterion__sublabel/);
-    expect(rail).not.toMatch(/job not asserted/);

-
-  it('does NOT add the sub-label when validates_job_satisfied is null (no job binding) or absent', () => {

-  it('does NOT fabricate a mock-only / stale sub-label (those are validate-time-only, not in oo-data)', () => {

-describe('No kind switch in render output', () => {

-    // (type=feature vs type=garden in the meta strip) but not WHICH
-    // sections render.

-      what: 'x',
-      narrative: '## hi',

-    const asGarden = call(data, META_GARDEN);
-    const asSubpage = call(data, META_SUBPAGE);
-
-    // main is identical across kinds — pure function of data. (The garden ALWAYS
-    // earns a masthead band; that band is a separate return field and does not
-    // change `main` — the dek is absent here, so nothing moves out of main.)
-    expect(asFeature.main).toBe(asGarden.main);
-    expect(asGarden.main).toBe(asSubpage.main);
-
-    // Feature and subpage have no masthead (no dek / no media), so their rails are

-    // differs (no detail-meta), and its meta strip lives in the masthead instead.

-const KLEMENT_JOB =

-  "working on, because every minute spent re-explaining yesterday's decisions is a minute " +
-  "not shipping, we believe opening one polyglot file should hand the next agent the same " +
-  "context the last agent had. We'll know we got it right when `bash docs/tend/features/" +
-  "<id>.tend.html data | jq` returns the current state of thinking in under one second.";

-describe('autoIcon — phase / kind mapping', () => {
-  it('returns an SVG string for every known journey_phase', () => {
-    const phases = ['orient', 'author', 'plan', 'build', 'verify', 'review'];
-    phases.forEach(function (p) {
-      const svg = autoIcon({ journey_phase: p });
-      expect(svg).toMatch(/^<svg viewBox="0 0 120 80"/);
-    });
-  });
-
-  it('returns an SVG for persona kind', () => {
-    expect(autoIcon({ kind: 'persona' })).toMatch(/^<svg viewBox="0 0 120 80"/);
-  });
-
-  it('returns an SVG for opportunity kind', () => {
-    expect(autoIcon({ kind: 'opportunity' })).toMatch(/^<svg viewBox="0 0 120 80"/);
-  });
-
-  it('returns the fallback SVG when neither phase nor kind matches', () => {
-    const svg = autoIcon({ id: 'unknown' });
-    // fallback is a document with folded tab — uses tc-wh tc-frame path + tc-la lines + tc-ac pill
-    expect(svg).toMatch(/^<svg viewBox="0 0 120 80"/);
-    expect(svg).toMatch(/tc-frame/);
-    expect(svg).toMatch(/tc-ac/);
-    const lines = (svg.match(/class="tc-la"/g) || []).length;
-    expect(lines).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
-  });
-
-  it('uses only .tc-* class primitives — no inline fill or stroke attributes', () => {
-    const phases = ['orient', 'author', 'plan', 'build', 'verify', 'review'];
-    phases.forEach(function (p) {
-      const svg = autoIcon({ journey_phase: p });
-      // All icons must use only .tc-* class names — no inline hex fill or stroke.
-      expect(svg).not.toMatch(/fill="#[0-9a-fA-F]/);
-      expect(svg).not.toMatch(/stroke="#[0-9a-fA-F]/);
-    });
-  });
-});

-    verified: { count: 18, at_risk: 4 },

-// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-// M1 — THE MASTHEAD BAND
-//
-// A full-width editorial band ABOVE the three columns. Presence-driven, one
-// component, class-aware by data (no per-kind scaffold). Four variants:
-//   RICH   — feature/subpage with a dek OR media/thumbnail: kicker + h1 + dek
-//            standfirst + persona/solves chips, visual card + status card.
-//   GARDEN — project title + dek-as-tagline + the HEALTH cockpit (moved from the
-//            rail) + catalog chips with VIEW-TIME counts.
-//   PERSONA/OPPORTUNITY — archetype/description lede + portrait/status card +
-//            count chips.
-//   DEGRADED — no dek AND no media: '' (the current compact header is kept).
-//
-// When the masthead renders it ABSORBS (removes, never copies): the rail's top
-// meta strip, the top-chrome status chip (boot-side), and (garden) the rail
-// health cockpit. Degraded pages keep all of those.
-// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-

-// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-// T2 — TOC + rail redesign.
-//
-// Rail groups into three bands (IDENTITY → GRAPH → PROOF), fixed order across
-// every kind. Checks become compact rows (verdict glyph + id + 1-line clamped
-// desc) that expand a per-check <details>. Long link lists collapse to top-5 +
-// a "+N more" expander. The TOC clamps long entries to 2 lines and carries the
-// full text on `title`. Cross-highlight wires probe links + [check:id] stamps
-// to their rail rows. Pure renderer/CSS/boot — no schema, no new data.
-// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-
-describe('T2 — rail three-band grouping', () => {
-  function bandOrder(rail: string): string[] {
-    const order: string[] = [];
-    const re = /data-rail-band="(identity|graph|proof)"/g;
-    let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
-    while ((m = re.exec(rail))) order.push(m[1]);
-    return order;
-  }
-
-  it('a feature rail emits exactly the three bands in fixed order IDENTITY → GRAPH → PROOF', () => {
-    const { rail } = call({
-      what: 'x',
-      status: 'in-progress',
-      journey_phase: 'build',
-      dependencies: ['dep-a'],
-      enables: ['en-b'],
-      checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'a check', validates: 'what', method: 'synthetic-test', status: 'satisfied' }],
-      steps: [{ id: 's1', title: 'do it', status: 'done' }],
-      smoke: { cmd: 'bash t.sh' },
-    });
-    expect(bandOrder(rail)).toEqual(['identity', 'graph', 'proof']);
-  });
-
-  it('places journey in IDENTITY, edges in GRAPH, checks/steps/smoke in PROOF (by position)', () => {
-    const { rail } = call({
-      what: 'x',
-      journey_phase: 'build',
-      dependencies: ['dep-a'],
-      checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'a check', validates: 'what', status: 'satisfied' }],
-    });
-    const idIdx = rail.indexOf('data-rail-band="identity"');
-    const grIdx = rail.indexOf('data-rail-band="graph"');
-    const prIdx = rail.indexOf('data-rail-band="proof"');
-    // journey lives in IDENTITY (before GRAPH); depends-on in GRAPH (before PROOF);
-    // checks in PROOF (after GRAPH).
-    expect(rail.indexOf('journey')).toBeGreaterThan(idIdx);
-    expect(rail.indexOf('journey')).toBeLessThan(grIdx);
-    expect(rail.indexOf('depends on')).toBeGreaterThan(grIdx);
-    expect(rail.indexOf('depends on')).toBeLessThan(prIdx);
-    expect(rail.indexOf('rail-c1')).toBeGreaterThan(prIdx);
-  });
-
-  it('a garden rail keeps the band order — identity then proof (catalog/aggregate land in PROOF, never above identity)', () => {
-    const { rail } = call(
-      {
-        what: 'project',
-        journey_phase: 'orient',
-        catalog: { personas: [{ id: 'p1', label: 'P1' }] },
-        features_aggregate: { feature_count: 1, by_phase: { build: [{ id: 'f1', status: 'verified' }] } },
-      },
-      META_GARDEN,
-    );
-    // Gardens carry no deps/enables/subpages → no GRAPH band (presence-driven).
-    // The bands that DO render keep their fixed relative order.
-    expect(bandOrder(rail)).toEqual(['identity', 'proof']);
-    // catalog (personas) sits in PROOF, below the identity band.
-    const prIdx = rail.indexOf('data-rail-band="proof"');
-    expect(rail.indexOf('personas')).toBeGreaterThan(prIdx);
-  });
-
-  it('a band with no content does not emit its wrapper (presence-driven)', () => {
-    // No journey / personas / parent → IDENTITY band has nothing → no wrapper.
-    const { rail } = call({ what: 'x', checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'd', validates: 'what', status: 'satisfied' }] });
-    expect(rail).not.toMatch(/data-rail-band="identity"/);
-    expect(rail).toMatch(/data-rail-band="proof"/);
-  });
-
-  it('emits small-caps band labels via .rail-band__label', () => {
-    const { rail } = call({
-      what: 'x',
-      journey_phase: 'build',
-      dependencies: ['dep-a'],
-      checks: [{ id: 'c1', description: 'd', validates: 'what', status: 'satisfied' }],
-    });
-    expect(rail).toMatch(/rail-band__label/);
-  });
-});
-

-describe('T2 — +N more expander for long link lists', () => {

deleted file mode 100644
index 04b46b2..0000000
--- a/tests/e2e/traceability.spec.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,125 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * Traceability smoke tests across the dogfood polyglots.
- *
- * Reads docs/tend/ at runtime (no mocks, no stubs) and asserts structural
- * integrity at the unit level:
- *
- *   1. Every coverage_files path actually exists on disk.
- *   2. Every step.traces_to check_id exists in the feature's checks[].
- *   3. Every subpage's parent refers to a known feature.
- *
- * These invariants are also enforced by `tend validate` and `tend coverage`,
- * but this test asserts them at the module level so regressions surface in
- * the vitest run without needing an MCP server or CLI invocation.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll } from 'vitest';
-import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';
-import type { Feature } from '../../src/core/types.js';
-import { scanAllFeaturesStrict } from '../../src/core/files.js';
-
-const REPO_ROOT = resolve(__dirname, '../..');
-const FEATURES_DIR = join(REPO_ROOT, 'docs', 'tend', 'features');
-
-// ─── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-/** Extract the oo-data JSON block from a polyglot file. */
-function extractOoData(filePath: string): Feature {
-  const text = readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8');
-  const match = /<script id="oo-data" type="application\/json">\n([\s\S]*?)\n<\/script>/.exec(text);
-  if (!match || !match[1]) throw new Error(`oo-data not found in ${filePath}`);
-  return JSON.parse(match[1]) as Feature;
-}
-
-// ─── Fixtures ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-let features: Feature[] = [];
-let featureIds: Set<string>;
-
-beforeAll(async () => {
-  if (!existsSync(FEATURES_DIR)) return;
-  const scan = await scanAllFeaturesStrict(REPO_ROOT);
-  // Surface malformed polyglots loudly instead of silently dropping them —
-  // the whole point of this test is dogfood-integrity.
-  const malformed = scan.filter((r) => !r.ok) as Array<{ ok: false; file: string; error: string }>;
-  if (malformed.length > 0) {
-    throw new Error(
-      `malformed polyglots in docs/tend/:\n${malformed.map((m) => `  ${m.file}: ${m.error}`).join('\n')}`,
-    );
-  }
-  features = scan.flatMap((r) => (r.ok && r.file !== 'overview.html' ? [r.feature] : []));
-  featureIds = new Set(features.map((f) => f.id));
-});
-
-// ─── Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-
-describe('traceability: dogfood integrity', () => {
-  it('at least one feature polyglot is present', () => {
-    expect(features.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
-  });
-
-  it('all coverage_files paths exist on disk', () => {
-    const ghosts: string[] = [];
-    for (const f of features) {
-      for (const p of f.coverage_files ?? []) {
-        const abs = join(REPO_ROOT, p);
-        if (!existsSync(abs)) {
-          ghosts.push(`${f.id}: ${p}`);
-        }
-      }
-    }
-    expect(ghosts, `ghost coverage_files:\n${ghosts.join('\n')}`).toEqual([]);
-  });
-
-  it('all step.traces_to check_ids exist in the feature checks[]', () => {
-    const orphans: string[] = [];
-    for (const f of features) {
-      const checkIds = new Set((f.checks ?? []).map((c) => c.id));
-      if (checkIds.size === 0) continue; // no checks — traces_to validation is N/A
-      for (const step of f.steps ?? []) {
-        for (const traced of step.traces_to ?? []) {
-          if (!checkIds.has(traced)) {
-            orphans.push(`${f.id}: step "${step.id}" traces_to unknown check "${traced}"`);
-          }
-        }
-      }
-    }
-    expect(orphans, `orphan traces_to:\n${orphans.join('\n')}`).toEqual([]);
-  });
-
-  it('all subpage parent refs resolve to a known target', () => {
-    // Subpage parents can be feature ids, "garden" (drill-downs of the
-    // project root), persona/opp/component catalog ids — anything in the
-    // garden's catalog or features_aggregate counts as a known target.
-    const broken: string[] = [];
-
-    // Build the set of valid parent targets once. featureIds already
-    // covers feature/subpage polyglots; we additionally accept "garden"
-    // plus everything in catalog.{personas,opportunities,components}.
-    const validParents = new Set<string>(featureIds);
-    validParents.add('garden');
-    try {
-      const gardenPath = join(REPO_ROOT, 'docs', 'tend', 'overview.html');
-      if (existsSync(gardenPath)) {
-        const garden = extractOoData(gardenPath) as unknown as {
-          catalog?: { personas?: Array<{ id: string }>; opportunities?: Array<{ id: string }>; components?: Array<{ id: string }> };
-        };
-        for (const p of garden.catalog?.personas ?? [])      validParents.add(p.id);
-        for (const o of garden.catalog?.opportunities ?? []) validParents.add(o.id);
-        for (const c of garden.catalog?.components ?? [])    validParents.add(c.id);
-      }
-    } catch {
-      // Garden missing/unreadable — fall through with feature-only validity.
-    }
-
-    for (const f of features) {
-      if (!f.parent) continue;
-      if (!validParents.has(f.parent)) {
-        broken.push(`${f.id}: parent "${f.parent}" not found in features, garden, or catalog`);
-      }
-    }
-    expect(broken, `broken parent refs:\n${broken.join('\n')}`).toEqual([]);
-  });
-});

- * share the universal polyglot scaffolder in `scripts/_polyglot_assembler.py`

- * (CLAUDE.md). Kind-specific divergence is limited to bash header, crumb,
- * title, and seed oo-meta + oo-data.
- *
- * Verifies each assembler:
- *   1. Runs without error (exit code 0)
- *   2. Output contains the consolidated client bundle (oo-helpers, oo-render,
- *      oo-boot identifiable fragments) and uses the universal scaffold's
- *      body-flow + data-rail-mount mounts.
- *   3. No references to deleted partials (oo-engine.js, oo-client-core.html,
- *      oo-renderers-{feature,garden,subpage}.js, oo-render-{kind}.html).
- *   4. Polyglot bash layer passes `bash -n`.
- *   5. Output files exist and are non-empty.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll } from 'vitest';
-import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'child_process';
-import { readFileSync, statSync, existsSync } from 'fs';
-import { resolve } from 'path';
-
-const REPO_ROOT = resolve(__dirname, '../..');
-const SCRIPTS = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'scripts');
-
-const SCRIPTS_LIST = [
-  resolve(SCRIPTS, 'assemble-feature-template.py'),
-  resolve(SCRIPTS, 'assemble-garden-bed.py'),
-];
-
-// The assembler outputs only build artifacts during tests. docs/tend/overview.html
-// (the LIVE garden polyglot) is MCP-owned per CLAUDE.md and SP-FIX-9 and is
-// NOT regenerated by the assembler in test runs — re-scaffold by hand with
-// `python3 scripts/assemble-garden-bed.py --canonical`.
-const OUTPUTS: Record<string, string[]> = {
-  'assemble-feature-template.py': [resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'templates/feature.tend.html')],
-  'assemble-garden-bed.py': [
-    resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'templates/overview.html'),
-    resolve(REPO_ROOT, '.context/bed-demo/tend.html'),
-  ],
-};
-
-// Fragments that prove the new client bundle landed.
-const NEW_CLIENT_FRAGMENTS = [
-  'OoRender',         // from oo-render.js return value
-  'OoHelpers',        // from oo-helpers.js return value
-  'renderPage',       // entry point
-  'data-render-mount="body-flow"', // universal scaffold mount
-  'data-rail-mount',  // rail mount
-];
-
-// Fragments from the OLD architecture that must NOT appear in the assembled
-// output. (Comments in oo-boot.js intentionally mention flow_order /
-// defaultPosition / master-loop as a "what we removed" docstring; those are
-// strings inside a comment, not real code references — so we don't list them
-// here.)
-const OLD_FRAGMENTS = [
-  'oo-engine.js',
-  'oo-client-core.html',
-  'oo-renderers-feature.js',
-  'oo-renderers-garden.js',
-  'oo-renderers-subpage.js',
-  '__OO_ENGINE_PLACEHOLDER__',
-  'registerRenderer',
-  'BLOCK_RENDERERS',
-];
-
-function scriptName(scriptPath: string): string {
-  return scriptPath.split('/').pop()!;
-}
-
-function runScript(scriptPath: string): void {
-  execFileSync('python3', [scriptPath], {
-    cwd: REPO_ROOT,
-    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
-    timeout: 30_000,
-  });
-}
-
-describe('Assembler exit code', () => {
-  for (const scriptPath of SCRIPTS_LIST) {
-    const name = scriptName(scriptPath);
-    it(`${name}: exits 0`, () => {
-      expect(() => runScript(scriptPath)).not.toThrow();
-    });
-  }
-});
-
-describe('Assembled output uses consolidated client bundle', () => {
-  for (const scriptPath of SCRIPTS_LIST) {
-    const name = scriptName(scriptPath);
-    const outputs = OUTPUTS[name];
-    for (const fragment of NEW_CLIENT_FRAGMENTS) {
-      it(`${name}: contains "${fragment}"`, () => {
-        for (const outPath of outputs) {
-          const content = readFileSync(outPath, 'utf8');
-          expect(content).toContain(fragment);
-        }
-      });
-    }
-  }
-});
-
-describe('Assembled output has no references to deleted partials', () => {
-  for (const scriptPath of SCRIPTS_LIST) {
-    const name = scriptName(scriptPath);
-    const outputs = OUTPUTS[name];
-    for (const old of OLD_FRAGMENTS) {
-      it(`${name}: does NOT contain "${old}"`, () => {
-        for (const outPath of outputs) {
-          const content = readFileSync(outPath, 'utf8');
-          expect(content).not.toContain(old);
-        }
-      });
-    }
-  }
-});
-
-describe('Polyglot bash layer is syntactically valid', () => {
-  for (const scriptPath of SCRIPTS_LIST) {
-    const name = scriptName(scriptPath);
-    const outputs = OUTPUTS[name];
-    it(`${name}: assembled output passes bash -n`, () => {
-      for (const outPath of outputs) {
-        const result = spawnSync('bash', ['-n', outPath], { encoding: 'utf8' });
-        expect(result.status).toBe(0);
-      }
-    });
-  }
-});
-
-describe('Output files exist and are non-empty', () => {
-  for (const scriptPath of SCRIPTS_LIST) {
-    const name = scriptName(scriptPath);
-    const outputs = OUTPUTS[name];
-    it(`${name}: all output files exist and are non-empty`, () => {
-      for (const outPath of outputs) {
-        expect(existsSync(outPath), `missing: ${outPath}`).toBe(true);
-        const stat = statSync(outPath);
-        expect(stat.size, `empty: ${outPath}`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
-      }
-    });
-  }

-
-// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-// polyglot-scaffold check c001 — "Every assembled polyglot has six OO sections
-// in order: STYLE, RENDER, DATA, CLIENT, CUSTOM (optional), SHELL."
-//
-// The canonical scaffold (scripts/_polyglot_assembler.py) emits the START
-// markers in this fixed order; OO:CUSTOM is the one optional zone and is NOT
-// emitted by the scaffolder (projects hand-add it), so it is excluded from the
-// required ordered set per the check's "(optional)" wording. SHELL is a bash
-// comment (`# OO:SHELL:START`), not an HTML comment, because it lives in the
-// heredoc-trailing shell core.
-//
-// Assertion: each marker is present AND its first index is strictly increasing
-// in the assembled output — this catches a dropped marker (find() === -1) OR a
-// reordered marker (index goes backwards). The prior cited test
-// (NEW_CLIENT_FRAGMENTS + bash -n + file existence) asserted none of this.
-// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-const ORDERED_MARKERS = [
-  '<!-- OO:STYLE:START -->',
-  '<!-- OO:RENDER:START -->',
-  '<!-- OO:DATA:START -->',
-  '<!-- OO:CLIENT:START -->',
-  '# OO:SHELL:START',
-];
-
-// Re-run both assemblers once so these suites assert on freshly-built output,
-// not a stale artifact left on disk.
-beforeAll(() => {
-  for (const scriptPath of SCRIPTS_LIST) {
-    runScript(scriptPath);
-  }
-});
-
-describe('Assembled polyglot has the six OO section markers in canonical order (c001)', () => {
-  for (const scriptPath of SCRIPTS_LIST) {
-    const name = scriptName(scriptPath);
-    const outputs = OUTPUTS[name];
-
-    it(`${name}: all ordered OO markers are present`, () => {
-      for (const outPath of outputs) {
-        const content = readFileSync(outPath, 'utf8');
-        for (const marker of ORDERED_MARKERS) {
-          expect(content.includes(marker), `${outPath} missing marker: ${marker}`).toBe(true);
-        }
-      }
-    });
-
-    it(`${name}: OO marker indices are strictly increasing (no drop, no reorder)`, () => {
-      for (const outPath of outputs) {
-        const content = readFileSync(outPath, 'utf8');
-        const indices = ORDERED_MARKERS.map((m) => content.indexOf(m));
-        for (let i = 1; i < indices.length; i++) {
-          // -1 (missing) is < any real index, so a dropped marker fails here too,
-          // but we assert > -1 explicitly for a clearer message.
-          expect(
-            indices[i],
-            `marker out of order or missing in ${outPath}: ` +
-              `"${ORDERED_MARKERS[i]}" (idx ${indices[i]}) must come after ` +
-              `"${ORDERED_MARKERS[i - 1]}" (idx ${indices[i - 1]})`,
-          ).toBeGreaterThan(indices[i - 1]);
-        }
-      }
-    });
-  }
-});
-
-// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-// polyglot-scaffold check c006 — "An assembled polyglot is fully self-contained
-// — no external CSS, JS, or data URLs; everything is inline so `cat + paste` and
-// offline open both work."
-//
-// We assert the assembled output makes ZERO external resource fetches:
-//   - no <link rel="stylesheet" href="http(s)://...">
-//   - no <script src="http(s)://...">
-//   - no CSS url(http(s)://...) or @import of an http(s) URL
-//   - no dynamic import('http(s)://...')
-//
-// The only legitimate `http(s)://` strings in the scaffold are SVG XML
-// namespace declarations (xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg") — a namespace
-// identifier the browser NEVER fetches, not a resource ref. A naive "no
-// http:// anywhere" assertion would false-fail on the correct assembler, so we
-// (a) target real resource-ref syntax, and (b) as a backstop, assert every
-// bare http(s):// occurrence is a whitelisted XML namespace. `data:` URIs are
-// permitted (the media schema allows inline base64) and are not external.
-// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-const EXTERNAL_RESOURCE_PATTERNS: { label: string; re: RegExp }[] = [
-  { label: 'external stylesheet <link href>', re: /<link\b[^>]*\bhref\s*=\s*["']https?:\/\//i },
-  { label: 'external <script src>', re: /<script\b[^>]*\bsrc\s*=\s*["']https?:\/\//i },
-  { label: 'external <img src>', re: /<img\b[^>]*\bsrc\s*=\s*["']https?:\/\//i },
-  { label: 'CSS @import of external URL', re: /@import\s+(?:url\()?["']?https?:\/\//i },
-  { label: 'CSS url(external)', re: /url\(\s*["']?https?:\/\//i },
-  { label: "dynamic import('http...')", re: /\bimport\s*\(\s*["']https?:\/\//i },
-];
-
-// Whitelisted bare-URL contexts that are NOT external fetches.
-const NAMESPACE_URL = /xmlns(?::\w+)?\s*=\s*["']https?:\/\//i;
-
-describe('Assembled polyglot is fully self-contained — no external resource refs (c006)', () => {
-  for (const scriptPath of SCRIPTS_LIST) {
-    const name = scriptName(scriptPath);
-    const outputs = OUTPUTS[name];
-
-    for (const { label, re } of EXTERNAL_RESOURCE_PATTERNS) {
-      it(`${name}: has no ${label}`, () => {
-        for (const outPath of outputs) {
-          const content = readFileSync(outPath, 'utf8');
-          expect(re.test(content), `${outPath} contains ${label}`).toBe(false);
-        }
-      });
-    }
-
-    it(`${name}: every http(s):// occurrence is a whitelisted XML namespace (no rogue external URL)`, () => {
-      for (const outPath of outputs) {
-        const content = readFileSync(outPath, 'utf8');
-        const lines = content.split('\n');
-        const offenders: string[] = [];
-        lines.forEach((line, i) => {
-          if (!/https?:\/\//i.test(line)) return;
-          if (NAMESPACE_URL.test(line)) return; // SVG xmlns — never fetched
-          offenders.push(`${outPath}:${i + 1}: ${line.trim().slice(0, 120)}`);
-        });
-        expect(offenders, `non-namespace external URL(s) found:\n${offenders.join('\n')}`).toEqual(
-          [],
-        );
-      }
-    });
-  }
-});

@@ -1,100 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * lib-color-tokens.spec.ts — color-token substitution in the preview harness.
- *
- * resvg (the PNG rasterizer behind `tend preview-thumbnail` / `preview-cards`)
- * does NOT resolve CSS custom properties (`var(--token)`) or the `currentColor`
- * keyword — it renders them black (or, for `var(--x, fallback)`, the inline
- * fallback). Every diagram in `oo-data.media` uses the documented inline-`var()`
- * color convention, so without a substitution pass each diagram previews as
- * black-on-black and the skill's visual-verify loop reports false failures.
- *
- * `substituteColorTokens` (exported from `src/core/svg-preview.ts`) rewrites
- * `var(--token)` and `currentColor` to the resolved literal hex for the target
- * theme BEFORE resvg sees the markup. These tests pin that behavior so the
- * visual-verify loop stays faithful.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { resolve } from 'node:path';
-import {
-  substituteColorTokens,
-  wrapSvgWithStyles,
-  resolveTokens,
-} from '../../src/core/svg-preview.js';
-
-const REPO_ROOT = resolve(__dirname, '../..');
-// The preview commands resolve the canonical token source from the package; here
-// we read it directly from the in-repo partial (the same file the package ships).
-const OO_STYLE_CSS = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'templates/_partials/oo-style.css');
-
-const TOKENS = {
-  '--accent': '#D97757',
-  '--bg-2': '#f5f3ee',
-  '--text': '#3a3a3a',
-  '--text-muted': '#8a8a86',
-};
-
-describe('substituteColorTokens', () => {
-  it('replaces a bare var(--token) with the resolved literal hex', () => {
-    const out = substituteColorTokens('<rect fill="var(--accent)"/>', TOKENS);
-    expect(out).toBe('<rect fill="#D97757"/>');
-  });
-
-  it('replaces var(--token, fallback) with the resolved token, not the fallback', () => {
-    const out = substituteColorTokens('<rect fill="var(--bg-2, #1f1d1a)"/>', TOKENS);
-    expect(out).toBe('<rect fill="#f5f3ee"/>');
-  });
-
-  it('keeps the inline fallback when the token is unknown', () => {
-    const out = substituteColorTokens('<text fill="var(--mystery, #8a8a86)"/>', TOKENS);
-    expect(out).toBe('<text fill="#8a8a86"/>');
-  });
-
-  it('maps an unknown token with no fallback to the theme text color (stays visible)', () => {
-    const out = substituteColorTokens('<text fill="var(--mystery)"/>', TOKENS);
-    expect(out).toBe('<text fill="#3a3a3a"/>');
-  });
-
-  it('replaces currentColor (any casing) with the theme text color', () => {
-    const out = substituteColorTokens(
-      '<text fill="currentColor"/><line stroke="currentcolor"/>',
-      TOKENS,
-    );
-    expect(out).toBe('<text fill="#3a3a3a"/><line stroke="#3a3a3a"/>');
-  });
-
-  it('substitutes tokens inside an SVG <style> block, not just attributes', () => {
-    const svg = '<style>.box{fill:var(--bg-2, #1f1d1a)} .lbl{fill:currentColor}</style>';
-    const out = substituteColorTokens(svg, TOKENS);
-    expect(out).toBe('<style>.box{fill:#f5f3ee} .lbl{fill:#3a3a3a}</style>');
-  });
-
-  it('leaves literal hex colors untouched', () => {
-    const out = substituteColorTokens('<rect fill="#abc123"/>', TOKENS);
-    expect(out).toBe('<rect fill="#abc123"/>');
-  });
-});
-
-describe('wrapSvgWithStyles resolves tokens for resvg', () => {
-  // The light + dark token maps come from the real oo-style.css :root blocks.
-  const themes = resolveTokens(OO_STYLE_CSS);
-
-  for (const theme of ['light', 'dark'] as const) {
-    it(`leaves no unresolved var() or currentColor in the ${theme} wrap`, () => {
-      const raw =
-        '<svg viewBox="0 0 100 40" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">' +
-        '<rect fill="var(--bg-2)" stroke="currentColor"/>' +
-        '<text fill="var(--accent)">x</text>' +
-        '</svg>';
-      const wrapped = wrapSvgWithStyles(raw, themes[theme]);
-      // The author-facing SVG body must be fully literalized.
-      expect(wrapped).not.toMatch(/var\(\s*--/);
-      // currentColor in the body is gone (the injected .tc-* block uses literal hex).
-      expect(wrapped.replace(/<defs>.*?<\/defs>/s, '')).not.toMatch(/currentColor/i);
-      // The accent token resolved to the theme's literal accent hex.
-      expect(wrapped).toContain(themes[theme]['--accent']);
-    });
-  }
-});
diff --git a/tests/scripts/narrative-links.spec.ts b/tests/scripts/narrative-links.spec.ts
deleted file mode 100644
index dc9f605..0000000
--- a/tests/scripts/narrative-links.spec.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,80 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * Narrative link-integrity test.
- *
- * Scans every shipped polyglot (garden + features, including drill-downs) and verifies
- * that every internal markdown link in `oo-data.narrative` resolves to a real
- * file on disk. Catches the wrong-prefix bug class where a feature narrative
- * links to `features/X.tend.html` — a path that works from the garden but
- * 404s from a sibling feature because the page is already in `features/`.
- *
- * Why this lives in tests/scripts (not the runtime validator): it's a
- * dogfood-state assertion, not a contract for user projects. User projects
- * may have valid narratives that don't yet have target files; we only assert
- * tend's own narratives don't ship with broken links.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { readFileSync, existsSync } from 'fs';
-import { dirname, resolve } from 'path';
-import { globSync } from 'glob';
-
-const REPO_ROOT = resolve(__dirname, '../..');
-const POLYGLOTS = globSync('docs/tend/{overview.html,features/*.tend.html}', { cwd: REPO_ROOT }).sort();
-
-function extractOoData(source: string): unknown | null {
-  const match = source.match(/<script id="oo-data" type="application\/json">\s*([\s\S]*?)\s*<\/script>/);
-  if (!match) return null;
-  try {
-    return JSON.parse(match[1]);
-  } catch {
-    return null;
-  }
-}
-
-function extractMarkdownLinkHrefs(markdown: string): string[] {
-  // [text](href) — non-greedy on text and href, skip image syntax (preceded by !)
-  const hrefs: string[] = [];
-  const re = /(?<!!)\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)\s]+)(?:\s+"[^"]*")?\)/g;
-  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
-  while ((m = re.exec(markdown)) !== null) hrefs.push(m[1]);
-  return hrefs;
-}
-
-function isInternal(href: string): boolean {
-  if (!href) return false;
-  if (href.startsWith('http://') || href.startsWith('https://')) return false;
-  if (href.startsWith('mailto:')) return false;
-  if (href.startsWith('#')) return false; // same-page anchor
-  return true;
-}
-
-describe('narrative link integrity', () => {
-  it('every internal narrative link resolves to a file on disk', () => {
-    const broken: string[] = [];
-    for (const relPath of POLYGLOTS) {
-      const abs = resolve(REPO_ROOT, relPath);
-      const source = readFileSync(abs, 'utf8');
-      const data = extractOoData(source) as { narrative?: string } | null;
-      const narrative = data?.narrative;
-      if (!narrative || typeof narrative !== 'string') continue;
-
-      const sourceDir = dirname(abs);
-      for (const href of extractMarkdownLinkHrefs(narrative)) {
-        if (!isInternal(href)) continue;
-        const cleanHref = href.split('#')[0];
-        if (!cleanHref) continue;
-        const target = resolve(sourceDir, cleanHref);
-        if (!existsSync(target)) {
-          broken.push(`${relPath}: narrative link [${href}] → ${target} (missing)`);
-        }
-      }
-    }
-    if (broken.length) {
-      throw new Error(
-        `${broken.length} broken narrative link(s):\n` + broken.map(b => '  ' + b).join('\n')
-      );
-    }
-    expect(broken).toEqual([]);
-  });
-});
diff --git a/tests/scripts/oo-style-tokens.spec.ts b/tests/scripts/oo-style-tokens.spec.ts
deleted file mode 100644
index 05fa986..0000000
--- a/tests/scripts/oo-style-tokens.spec.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,301 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * oo-style-tokens.spec.ts — CSS token-hygiene guard.
- *
- * Decision d001 (CLAUDE.md): no raw hex values in component classes — all
- * color via CSS custom properties (tokens). Raw hex is allowed only inside
- * the :root and [data-theme] / @media blocks where the tokens are *defined*.
- *
- * This test reads templates/_partials/oo-style.css, strips every token-
- * definition block (:root { ... }, [data-theme] { ... }, @media block that
- * contains :root), then asserts that zero raw hex sequences (#xxx / #xxxxxx)
- * remain in the component-class portion.
- *
- * It was RED before the chip-tend--strong fix (the only raw hex outside tokens
- * was `#fff` in the var() fallback on that rule). It must stay GREEN after.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { resolve } from 'node:path';
-
-const REPO_ROOT = resolve(__dirname, '../..');
-const CSS_PATH = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'templates/_partials/oo-style.css');
-
-/**
- * Strip all token-definition blocks from the CSS text so only the
- * component-class portion remains for hex scanning.
- *
- * Removes:
- *   - :root { ... }
- *   - [data-theme="..."] { ... }
- *   - @media (...) { :root... { ... } } (the auto-dark prefers-color-scheme block)
- *
- * Uses a balanced-brace approach — finds the opening brace for each block
- * and walks forward counting depth until the matching closing brace.
- */
-function stripTokenBlocks(css: string): string {
-  // Patterns that open a token-definition block.
-  // We also strip inline `rgba(...)` / `var(--shadow, rgba(...))` sequences
-  // since those contain parentheses but never raw hex.
-  const BLOCK_OPEN_RE = /(?::root\s*\{|\[data-theme[^\]]*\]\s*\{|@media\s[^{]+\{)/g;
-
-  let result = css;
-  let offset = 0;
-
-  // Iterate over a fresh copy so indices don't shift under us.
-  const src = css;
-  BLOCK_OPEN_RE.lastIndex = 0;
-  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
-  const removals: Array<[number, number]> = [];
-
-  while ((m = BLOCK_OPEN_RE.exec(src)) !== null) {
-    // Find the opening brace of this block.
-    const braceStart = src.indexOf('{', m.index);
-    if (braceStart === -1) continue;
-
-    let depth = 0;
-    let i = braceStart;
-    while (i < src.length) {
-      if (src[i] === '{') depth++;
-      else if (src[i] === '}') {
-        depth--;
-        if (depth === 0) { i++; break; }
-      }
-      i++;
-    }
-    removals.push([m.index, i]);
-  }
-
-  // Apply removals in reverse order so earlier indices stay valid.
-  for (let r = removals.length - 1; r >= 0; r--) {
-    const [start, end] = removals[r]!;
-    result = result.slice(0, start) + result.slice(end);
-  }
-
-  // Also strip rgba(...) sequences — they aren't hex but contain # if
-  // someone writes hex-less alpha, so exclude them from the scan to avoid
-  // false positives on `rgba(0,0,0,0.08)` etc.
-  // (No action needed — rgba doesn't contain #.)
-
-  return result;
-}
-
-/** Return all raw hex colour sequences found in the text. */
-function findRawHex(css: string): string[] {
-  const HEX_RE = /#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b/g;
-  const hits: string[] = [];
-  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
-  while ((m = HEX_RE.exec(css)) !== null) {
-    hits.push(m[0]);
-  }
-  return hits;
-}
-
-describe('oo-style.css token hygiene', () => {
-  it('component classes contain zero raw hex values (all colour via tokens)', () => {
-    const src = readFileSync(CSS_PATH, 'utf8');
-    const componentCss = stripTokenBlocks(src);
-    const hexHits = findRawHex(componentCss);
-
-    // If this assertion fails, hexHits lists every offending value so the
-    // developer knows exactly what to fix.
-    expect(hexHits).toEqual([]);
-  });
-
-  it('the :root block itself defines hex tokens (sanity: strip did not remove everything)', () => {
-    // After stripping, there should be CSS left — we haven't emptied the file.
-    const src = readFileSync(CSS_PATH, 'utf8');
-    const componentCss = stripTokenBlocks(src);
-    expect(componentCss.trim().length).toBeGreaterThan(100);

-
-/**
- * Return the body of the FIRST top-level block whose opening selector matches
- * `openRe` (a regex anchored to the selector text immediately before `{`).
- * Uses balanced-brace walking so nested `{}` (e.g. an inner `:root` inside an
- * `@media` block) are captured whole.
- *
- * @param css   full stylesheet text
- * @param openRe regex matching the selector + opening brace, e.g. /:root\s*\{/
- * @returns the text between the matched `{` and its balancing `}` (exclusive),
- *          or null when no match.
- */
-function blockBody(css: string, openRe: RegExp): string | null {
-  const m = openRe.exec(css);
-  if (!m) return null;
-  const braceStart = css.indexOf('{', m.index);
-  if (braceStart === -1) return null;
-  let depth = 0;
-  for (let i = braceStart; i < css.length; i++) {
-    if (css[i] === '{') depth++;
-    else if (css[i] === '}') {
-      depth--;
-      if (depth === 0) return css.slice(braceStart + 1, i);
-    }
-  }
-  return null;
-}
-
-/** Names of every custom property assigned a value (`--foo: ...;`) in `body`. */
-function tokenNames(body: string): Set<string> {
-  const RE = /(--[a-z0-9-]+)\s*:/g;
-  const names = new Set<string>();
-  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
-  while ((m = RE.exec(body)) !== null) names.add(m[1]!);
-  return names;
-}
-
-/**
- * Token families that carry COLOUR and therefore must be re-defined in every
- * dark-mode block so the theme swaps consistently (c003 — "colors swap
- * consistently"). Structural tokens (--sp-*, --radius*, fonts, --rail-w, …)
- * are deliberately NOT in this set: they must stay constant across themes so
- * the layout is identical between light and dark.
- */
-function isColourToken(name: string): boolean {
-  if (name.startsWith('--glyph-')) return true;
-  if (name.startsWith('--sev-')) return true;
-  return [
-    '--bg', '--bg-2',
-    '--text', '--text-2', '--text-muted', '--muted',
-    '--border', '--border-strong',
-    '--accent', '--accent-d', '--accent-weak',
-    '--heading', '--surface', '--surface-hover', '--shadow',
-  ].includes(name);
-}
-
-describe('oo-style.css dark/light theme parity (c003)', () => {
-  const css = readFileSync(CSS_PATH, 'utf8');
-
-  // The three token-defining blocks. The two dark blocks live AFTER the base
-  // :root; slicing from the @media block onward keeps the base-:root match from
-  // shadowing the nested dark :root.
-  const baseRoot = blockBody(css, /:root\s*\{/);
-  const autoDark = blockBody(css, /@media\s*\(prefers-color-scheme:\s*dark\)\s*\{\s*:root[^{]*\{/);
-  const explicitDark = blockBody(css, /:root\[data-theme="dark"\]\s*\{/);
-
-  it('all three token-defining blocks are present', () => {
-    expect(baseRoot).not.toBeNull();
-    expect(autoDark).not.toBeNull();
-    expect(explicitDark).not.toBeNull();
-  });
-
-  it('every colour token defined in :root is overridden in the prefers-color-scheme dark block', () => {
-    const base = tokenNames(baseRoot!);
-    const dark = tokenNames(autoDark!);
-    const missing = [...base].filter((n) => isColourToken(n) && !dark.has(n)).sort();
-    // A non-empty list = colour tokens that keep their light value in auto-dark,
-    // i.e. the theme would NOT swap consistently for those surfaces.
-    expect(missing).toEqual([]);
-  });
-
-  it('every colour token defined in :root is overridden in the [data-theme="dark"] block', () => {
-    const base = tokenNames(baseRoot!);
-    const dark = tokenNames(explicitDark!);
-    const missing = [...base].filter((n) => isColourToken(n) && !dark.has(n)).sort();
-    expect(missing).toEqual([]);
-  });
-
-  it('the two dark blocks override the identical token set (auto-dark === manual-dark)', () => {
-    const a = [...tokenNames(autoDark!)].sort();
-    const b = [...tokenNames(explicitDark!)].sort();
-    expect(a).toEqual(b);
-  });
-
-  it('spacing tokens are NOT redefined in either dark block (layout identical across themes)', () => {
-    const autoSp = [...tokenNames(autoDark!)].filter((n) => n.startsWith('--sp-'));
-    const darkSp = [...tokenNames(explicitDark!)].filter((n) => n.startsWith('--sp-'));
-    expect(autoSp).toEqual([]);
-    expect(darkSp).toEqual([]);
-  });
-});
-
-describe('oo-style.css single token source — per-kind rhythm identity (c005)', () => {
-  const css = readFileSync(CSS_PATH, 'utf8');
-  // Strip /* ... */ comments so prose mentioning `.feature-card` etc. can't be
-  // misread as a real selector (regex below would otherwise cross into the next
-  // rule via the comment body).
-  const cssNoComments = css.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '');
-
-  it('no kind/role selector redefines a palette or spacing token (all kinds resolve identical values)', () => {
-    // feature / garden / subpage share one stylesheet with one token source.
-    // A selector like `.kind-garden { --accent: ... }` or `[data-kind="feature"]
-    // { --sp-4: ... }` would fork the rhythm per kind — forbidden. `[^{}]*`
-    // cannot cross a `{` or `}`, so this only matches a token ASSIGNMENT inside
-    // the body of a kind-scoped rule, never a component that merely uses var().
-    const KIND_TOKEN_RE =
-      /(?:\.kind-[a-z]+|\.(?:feature|garden|subpage)\b|\[data-kind[^\]]*\])[^{}]*\{[^{}]*--(?:sp-|text|bg|accent|glyph|sev|border|surface|heading)[a-z0-9-]*\s*:/g;
-    const hits = cssNoComments.match(KIND_TOKEN_RE) ?? [];
-    expect(hits).toEqual([]);
-  });
-
-  it('each spacing token is defined exactly once in the whole file (single edit point)', () => {
-    // c004/c005 core: doubling the base rhythm is a one-line edit because each
-    // --sp-N has exactly one definition site. (Dark blocks must not redefine
-    // spacing — guarded above — so the count here stays 1 per token.)
-    for (const tok of ['--sp-1', '--sp-2', '--sp-3', '--sp-4', '--sp-6', '--sp-8']) {
-      const count = (css.match(new RegExp(`${tok}\\s*:`, 'g')) ?? []).length;
-      expect(count, `${tok} should be defined exactly once`).toBe(1);
-    }
-  });
-});
-
-/**
- * On-scale spacing step values, in px. These are exactly the values the `--sp-*`
- * scale defines (d003 — manual 4px grid with deliberate gaps: no --sp-5 / --sp-7).
- * A component rule that writes one of these as a raw px in a coarse-spacing
- * property (padding / margin / gap) instead of `var(--sp-*)` defeats the
- * single-edit-point promise the WHY slot makes (c004): doubling the rhythm would
- * miss that rule. Sub-grid px (1 / 2 / 3 / 6 / 11 / 18 / 20 / 22 / 360 …) sit
- * BETWEEN the gapped scale and are deliberately raw per d003 — they are permitted.
- */
-const ON_SCALE_SPACING_PX = new Set([4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32]);
-
-/**
- * Coarse-spacing declarations whose values must resolve through `var(--sp-*)`
- * rather than an on-scale raw px. Border / radius / font-size / width / height
- * are NOT coarse spacing (they carry their own fixed-px semantics) and are out
- * of scope. `calc(...)` expressions are stripped before scanning: the two in
- * oo-style.css couple to a fixed icon / marker width (16px icon, 12px ▸ marker)
- * for geometric alignment, not to the rhythm — tokenising them would drift them
- * from the dimension they align to (same spirit as the d003 sub-grid exception).
- */
-function onScaleRawSpacing(componentCss: string): string[] {
-  // Strip calc(...) expressions — px inside them is alignment geometry, not rhythm.
-  const noCalc = componentCss.replace(/calc\([^)]*\)/g, 'calc()');
-  // Match a coarse-spacing property and capture its value up to the `;` or `}`.
-  const DECL_RE = /(?:padding|margin|gap|row-gap|column-gap)[a-z-]*\s*:\s*([^;{}]+)/g;
-  const PX_RE = /(\d+)px/g;
-  const offenders: string[] = [];
-  let decl: RegExpExecArray | null;
-  while ((decl = DECL_RE.exec(noCalc)) !== null) {
-    const value = decl[1]!;
-    let px: RegExpExecArray | null;
-    PX_RE.lastIndex = 0;
-    while ((px = PX_RE.exec(value)) !== null) {
-      if (ON_SCALE_SPACING_PX.has(Number(px[1]))) {
-        offenders.push(decl[0].trim());
-        break; // one entry per declaration, even if it has several on-scale values
-      }
-    }
-  }
-  return offenders;
-}
-
-describe('oo-style.css on-scale spacing through tokens (c004)', () => {
-  it('no component rule hardcodes an on-scale spacing px in padding/margin/gap (all coarse spacing via var(--sp-*))', () => {
-    const src = readFileSync(CSS_PATH, 'utf8');
-    // Reuse the c002 boundary: strip the token-DEFINITION blocks (:root, the two
-    // dark blocks, @media-with-:root) where `--sp-1: 4px` etc. legitimately live;
-    // what remains is the component portion. Then strip comments so prose px in a
-    // /* ... */ note can't be misread as a declaration value.
-    const componentCss = stripTokenBlocks(src).replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '');
-    const offenders = onScaleRawSpacing(componentCss);
-    // If this fails, `offenders` lists each declaration that still hardcodes an
-    // on-scale step (e.g. `padding: 8px 12px`) so the fix is `var(--sp-2) var(--sp-3)`.
-    expect(offenders).toEqual([]);
-  });
-});

-/**
- * Structural tests for the canonical oo-shell-core.sh partial (c005, c008).
- *
- * c005 — The 5 built-in verbs are canonical case entries:
- *   Tests prove verbs are wired as explicit `case` branches, not just fallback-
- *   routed via cmd_* functions. Removing a case entry from the canonical partial
- *   must fail these tests even if the cmd_* function still exists.
- *
- * c008 — Canonical partial has all 5 cmd_ functions AND the builtins-fixture
- *   shell section is byte-identical to the canonical partial (drift-channel
- *   closure). Breaking the canonical partial is caught by builtins.sh because
- *   the fixture embeds exactly that content.
- *
- * @vitest-environment node
- */
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { resolve } from 'node:path';
-
-const REPO_ROOT = resolve(__dirname, '../..');
-const CANONICAL = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'templates/_partials/oo-shell-core.sh');
-const FIXTURE = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'tests/bash/fixtures/builtins-fixture.tend.html');
-
-const canonicalContent = readFileSync(CANONICAL, 'utf8');
-
-// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-// c008 — Canonical partial: all 5 cmd_ function definitions present
-// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-describe('c008: canonical oo-shell-core.sh contains all 5 cmd_ function definitions', () => {
-  const VERBS = ['cmd_data', 'cmd_status', 'cmd_help', 'cmd_run', 'cmd_smoke'] as const;
-
-  for (const fn of VERBS) {
-    it(`${fn}() is defined in templates/_partials/oo-shell-core.sh`, () => {
-      // Match `cmd_data() {` or `cmd_data ()` at the start of a function def line.
-      const fnPattern = new RegExp(`^${fn}\\s*\\(\\s*\\)`, 'm');
-      expect(canonicalContent).toMatch(fnPattern);
-    });
-  }
-});
-
-// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-// c005 — Dispatcher: all 5 verbs are explicit case entries (not fallback-only)
-// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-describe('c005: dispatcher has explicit case entries for all 5 built-in verbs', () => {
-  // Extract the case block from the dispatcher section.
-  // We look for `case "${1:-}" in` ... `esac` and check each verb appears as
-  // a case pattern. This distinguishes explicit case wiring from cmd_* fallback.
-  const caseBlockMatch = canonicalContent.match(/case "\$\{1:-\}" in([\s\S]*?)esac/);
-  it('dispatcher contains a case block', () => {
-    expect(caseBlockMatch).not.toBeNull();
-  });
-
-  const caseBlock = caseBlockMatch ? caseBlockMatch[1] : '';
-
-  // Use multiline flag so ^ matches start of each line in the case block.
-  const CASE_ENTRIES = [
-    { verb: 'data',   pattern: /^\s+data\)/m },
-    { verb: 'status', pattern: /^\s+status\)/m },
-    // help may appear with aliases: `help|-h|--help)`
-    { verb: 'help',   pattern: /^\s+help(\|-h\|--help)?\)/m },
-    { verb: 'run',    pattern: /^\s+run\)/m },
-    { verb: 'smoke',  pattern: /^\s+smoke\)/m },
-  ] as const;
-
-  for (const { verb, pattern } of CASE_ENTRIES) {
-    it(`"${verb}" is an explicit case entry in the dispatcher`, () => {
-      expect(caseBlock).toMatch(pattern);
-    });
-  }
-});
-
-// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-// c008 — Drift-channel closure: builtins-fixture shell section is byte-identical
-//         to the canonical partial
-// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-describe('c008: builtins-fixture shell section matches canonical partial exactly', () => {
-  it('builtins-fixture.tend.html OO:SHELL section is identical to oo-shell-core.sh', () => {
-    const fixtureContent = readFileSync(FIXTURE, 'utf8');
-
-    // Extract the shell section from the fixture (# OO:SHELL:START ... # OO:SHELL:END inclusive).
-    const fixtureShellMatch = fixtureContent.match(/(# OO:SHELL:START[\s\S]*?# OO:SHELL:END)/);
-    expect(
-      fixtureShellMatch,
-      'builtins-fixture.tend.html must contain an OO:SHELL section',
-    ).not.toBeNull();
-
-    const fixtureShell = fixtureShellMatch![1];
-    const canonicalShell = canonicalContent.match(/(# OO:SHELL:START[\s\S]*?# OO:SHELL:END)/)?.[1];
-    expect(
-      canonicalShell,
-      'templates/_partials/oo-shell-core.sh must contain OO:SHELL:START/END markers',
-    ).not.toBeNull();
-
-    expect(
-      fixtureShell,
-      'builtins-fixture shell section has drifted from templates/_partials/oo-shell-core.sh.\n' +
-        'Run: head -52 tests/bash/fixtures/builtins-fixture.tend.html > /tmp/head.txt && ' +
-        'cat templates/_partials/oo-shell-core.sh >> /tmp/head.txt && ' +
-        'cp /tmp/head.txt tests/bash/fixtures/builtins-fixture.tend.html',
-    ).toBe(canonicalShell);
-  });
-});
