-/**
- * Episode segmentation (L0.5, docs/loop-hole-episodes-design.md) — the unit
- * the trace-mining layer clusters next. An episode is anchored at a user
- * turn and carries everything that happened before the next ask (or the
- * session's end): the ordered tool trace with outcomes, how long it took,
- * what it cost, and a resolution signal read off structure alone (no text
- * matching — that stays the reader tier's job).
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { ClaudeCodeAdapter } from '../src/claude-adapter.js';
-import { runExtract } from '../src/extract.js';
-import { StateStore } from '../src/store.js';
-import { segmentEpisodes, type Episode } from '../src/episodes.js';
-import { makeCorpus, toolCallRecord, toolResult, userTurn } from './helpers.js';
-
-const CWD = '/Users/me/repo';
-
-function actionFor(episode: Episode, needle: string) {
-  const action = episode.actions.find((a) => a.template.includes(needle));
-  if (action === undefined) throw new Error(`no action matching "${needle}" in episode at ${episode.ts}`);
-  return action;
-}
-
-describe('episode segmentation', () => {
-  it('a seeded session with three asks yields three episodes, each carrying its ordered action trace with outcomes, duration, token cost, and resolution signal', async () => {
-    const root = makeCorpus([
-      {
-        dir: '-Users-me-repo',
-        sessionId: 'sess-episodes',
-        records: [
-          userTurn('run the release checklist', '2026-06-25T09:00:00.000Z', CWD),
-          toolCallRecord('msg-1', 'tool-1', 'Bash', { command: 'npm test' }, '2026-06-25T09:00:01.000Z', { input_tokens: 10, output_tokens: 5 }, CWD),
-          toolResult('tool-1', false, '2026-06-25T09:00:02.000Z', 'tests passed', CWD),
-          toolCallRecord('msg-2', 'tool-2', 'Bash', { command: 'npm publish' }, '2026-06-25T09:00:05.000Z', { input_tokens: 8, output_tokens: 4 }, CWD),
-          toolResult('tool-2', true, '2026-06-25T09:00:06.000Z', 'permission denied', CWD),
-
-          userTurn('check the deploy status', '2026-06-25T09:05:00.000Z', CWD),
-          toolCallRecord('msg-3', 'tool-3', 'Bash', { command: 'curl https://status.example/health' }, '2026-06-25T09:05:02.000Z', { input_tokens: 6, output_tokens: 2 }, CWD),
-          toolResult('tool-3', false, '2026-06-25T09:05:03.000Z', 'ok', CWD),
-
-          userTurn('write the release notes', '2026-06-25T09:10:00.000Z', CWD),
-          toolCallRecord('msg-4', 'tool-4', 'Bash', { command: 'git log -5' }, '2026-06-25T09:10:07.000Z', { input_tokens: 4, output_tokens: 1 }, CWD),
-          toolResult('tool-4', false, '2026-06-25T09:10:08.000Z', 'log output', CWD),
-          // session ends here — the third ask never gets a follow-up.
-        ],
-      },
-    ]);
-
-    const store = StateStore.empty();
-    await runExtract(new ClaudeCodeAdapter(root), store);
-
-    const episodes = segmentEpisodes(store);
-    expect(episodes).toHaveLength(3);
-    const [first, second, third] = episodes;
-    if (first === undefined || second === undefined || third === undefined) throw new Error('expected three episodes');
-
-    // Episode 1: two-step trace, ordered, outcomes resolved, an error inside it.
-    expect(first.session).toBe('sess-episodes');
-    expect(first.ts).toBe('2026-06-25T09:00:00.000Z');
-    expect(first.actions.map((a) => a.outcome)).toEqual([
-      actionFor(first, 'npm test').outcome,
-      actionFor(first, 'npm publish').outcome,
-    ]);
-    expect(actionFor(first, 'npm test').outcome).toBe('ok');
-    expect(actionFor(first, 'npm publish').outcome).toBe('error');
-    // Order preserved: npm test ran before npm publish.
-    expect(first.actions[0]?.template).toContain('npm test');
-    expect(first.actions[1]?.template).toContain('npm publish');
-    expect(first.durationMs).toBe(Date.parse('2026-06-25T09:00:05.000Z') - Date.parse('2026-06-25T09:00:00.000Z'));
-    expect(first.tokens).toEqual({ input: 10 + 8, output: 5 + 4 });
-    // A follow-up ask arrived, and this episode's trace contains an error —
-    // presumed a fix-forward rather than an unrelated new request.
-    expect(first.resolution).toBe('unresolved');
-
-    // Episode 2: single-step, clean trace, followed by another ask.
-    expect(second.actions).toHaveLength(1);
-    expect(actionFor(second, 'curl').outcome).toBe('ok');
-    expect(second.durationMs).toBe(Date.parse('2026-06-25T09:05:02.000Z') - Date.parse('2026-06-25T09:05:00.000Z'));
-    expect(second.tokens).toEqual({ input: 6, output: 2 });
-    expect(second.resolution).toBe('resolved');

-    // Episode 3: last ask in the session — nothing followed it.

-    expect(actionFor(third, 'git log').outcome).toBe('ok');
-    expect(third.durationMs).toBe(Date.parse('2026-06-25T09:10:07.000Z') - Date.parse('2026-06-25T09:10:00.000Z'));
-    expect(third.tokens).toEqual({ input: 4, output: 1 });
-    expect(third.resolution).toBe('abandoned');
-  });
-});
-
-describe('episode segmentation: negative controls', () => {
-  it('an ask with no follow-up tool calls is still one episode, not zero — an empty trace is a real episode', async () => {

-
-  it('two sessions sharing the exact same ask text never merge into one episode', async () => {

-        dir: '-Users-me-repoA',

-        records: [

-          toolCallRecord('msg-x', 'tool-x', 'Bash', { command: 'systemctl restart worker' }, '2026-06-27T09:00:01.000Z', { input_tokens: 3, output_tokens: 1 }, '/Users/me/repoA'),
-          toolResult('tool-x', false, '2026-06-27T09:00:02.000Z', 'restarted', '/Users/me/repoA'),

-      {
-        dir: '-Users-me-repoB',
-        sessionId: 'sess-y',
-        records: [userTurn('restart the worker', '2026-06-27T10:00:00.000Z', '/Users/me/repoB')],
-      },
-    ]);
-
-    const store = StateStore.empty();
-    await runExtract(new ClaudeCodeAdapter(root), store);
-    const episodes = segmentEpisodes(store);
-
-    expect(episodes).toHaveLength(2);
-    const bySession = new Map(episodes.map((e) => [e.session, e]));

-/**

- * from the assistant usage records between it and the next turn — deduped by
- * assistant message id, since one completion repeats its usage across every

--- a/spikes/loop-hole/tests/facet-checkpoint.spec.ts

@@ -1,124 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * Backfill checkpointing (SNAG-18, root cause 2): the run-end-only cache save
- * meant a backfill killed mid-pass lost every reader call it had already paid
- * for. The facet cache must hit disk after EVERY completed session read, not
- * only once the whole pass finishes — so an interruption anywhere in a long
- * backfill loses zero paid reads, and the next pass resumes from exactly
- * where it stopped instead of re-reading sessions already answered.
- */
-
-import { existsSync, mkdtempSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { join } from 'node:path';
-import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
-import { runPipeline } from '../src/run.js';
-import { FacetStore } from '../src/facet-store.js';
-import type { FacetReader } from '../src/facets.js';
-import { makeCorpus, userTurn } from './helpers.js';
-
-function outDir(): string {
-  return mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'loophole-facet-checkpoint-'));
-}
-
-function threeSessionCorpus(): string {
-  return makeCorpus([
-    {
-      dir: '-Users-me-repoA',
-      sessionId: 'sess-1',
-      records: [
-        userTurn('first real ask', '2026-06-01T10:00:00.000Z'),
-        userTurn('first follow-up', '2026-06-01T10:05:00.000Z'),
-      ],
-    },
-    {
-      dir: '-Users-me-repoB',
-      sessionId: 'sess-2',
-      records: [
-        userTurn('second real ask', '2026-06-02T10:00:00.000Z'),
-        userTurn('second follow-up', '2026-06-02T10:05:00.000Z'),
-      ],
-    },
-    {
-      dir: '-Users-me-repoC',
-      sessionId: 'sess-3',
-      records: [
-        userTurn('third real ask', '2026-06-03T10:00:00.000Z'),
-        userTurn('third follow-up', '2026-06-03T10:05:00.000Z'),
-      ],
-    },
-  ]);
-}
-
-describe('backfill checkpointing', () => {
-  it('persists the facet cache to disk after EVERY completed session read, not only at the end of the pass', async () => {
-    const corpus = threeSessionCorpus();
-    const out = outDir();
-    const facetStorePath = join(out, 'loop-hole.facets.json');
-
-    // Records how many sessions were already ON DISK the instant each reader
-    // call fires — the old (buggy) behavior only ever writes once, at the
-    // very end of the pass, so every call would see 0 no matter how many
-    // prior sessions had already finished reading.
-    const onDiskBeforeEachCall: number[] = [];
-    let calls = 0;
-    const reader: FacetReader = () => {
-      onDiskBeforeEachCall.push(existsSync(facetStorePath) ? FacetStore.load(facetStorePath).size : 0);
-      calls += 1;
-      const quote = calls === 1 ? 'first real ask' : calls === 2 ? 'second real ask' : 'third real ask';
-      return JSON.stringify([{ category: 'instruction', summary: `finding ${calls}`, quotes: [quote] }]);
-    };
-
-    await runPipeline({ corpusDir: corpus, outDir: out, facetReader: reader, minUserTurns: 2 });
-
-    expect(calls).toBe(3);
-    expect(onDiskBeforeEachCall).toEqual([0, 1, 2]);
-
-    const finalStore = FacetStore.load(facetStorePath);
-    expect(finalStore.size).toBe(3);
-  });
-
-  it('an interrupted backfill loses zero paid reads — the next pass resumes exactly where it stopped', async () => {
-    const corpus = threeSessionCorpus();
-    const out = outDir();
-    const facetStorePath = join(out, 'loop-hole.facets.json');
-
-    // Sessions sort sess-1 < sess-2 < sess-3; the third call stands in for
-    // the process dying mid-backfill (a network drop, an OOM kill, ctrl-c) —
-    // the pipeline call itself still returns (a refused session is handled),
-    // but the two sessions that DID finish reading before it must already be
-    // safely checkpointed, not lost because the pass never reached the end.
-    let callCount = 0;
-    const crashingReader: FacetReader = () => {
-      callCount += 1;
-      if (callCount === 3) throw new Error('simulated process interruption');
-      const quote = callCount === 1 ? 'first real ask' : 'second real ask';
-      return JSON.stringify([{ category: 'instruction', summary: `finding ${callCount}`, quotes: [quote] }]);
-    };
-
-    const first = await runPipeline({ corpusDir: corpus, outDir: out, facetReader: crashingReader, minUserTurns: 2 });
-    expect(first.facets.refusedSessions).toBe(1);
-
-    const afterCrash = FacetStore.load(facetStorePath);
-    expect(afterCrash.get('sess-1')).toBeDefined();
-    expect(afterCrash.get('sess-2')).toBeDefined();
-    expect(afterCrash.get('sess-3')).toBeUndefined();
-
-    // Resume with a healthy reader — it must be invoked exactly once, for
-    // sess-3 only; sess-1 and sess-2 are not re-read (zero reads lost).
-    const resumeCalls: string[] = [];
-    const resumeReader: FacetReader = (prompt) => {
-      resumeCalls.push(prompt);
-      return JSON.stringify([{ category: 'instruction', summary: 'finding 3', quotes: ['third real ask'] }]);
-    };
-    const second = await runPipeline({ corpusDir: corpus, outDir: out, facetReader: resumeReader, minUserTurns: 2 });
-
-    expect(resumeCalls).toHaveLength(1);
-    expect(second.facets.readerCalls).toBe(1);
-
-    const finalStore = FacetStore.load(facetStorePath);
-    expect(finalStore.size).toBe(3);
-    expect(finalStore.get('sess-1')).toEqual(afterCrash.get('sess-1'));
-    expect(finalStore.get('sess-2')).toEqual(afterCrash.get('sess-2'));
-    expect(finalStore.get('sess-3')).toBeDefined();
-  });
-});
diff --git a/spikes/loop-hole/tests/facet-chunking.spec.ts b/spikes/loop-hole/tests/facet-chunking.spec.ts

--- a/spikes/loop-hole/tests/facet-chunking.spec.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,230 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * Oversized sessions: long-context recall degrades 15-30% from 4K->128K with
- * a lost-in-the-middle dip even on frontier models, so a digest whose full
- * prompt would overflow the reader's window is never handed over flat. It is
- * split into reader-sized chunks, each carrying the COMPLETE data-not-a-task
- * framing and already-encoded block (not just the first chunk), and every
- * chunk's findings are merged into that session's one cache entry — never a
- * single oversized prompt, never a partial reading silently treated as done
- * (design: docs/loop-hole-episodes-design.md, v3, "digest chunking rule").
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import type { EpisodeDigest, SessionDigest } from '../src/digest.js';
-import {
-  buildFacetCache,
-  buildFacetPrompt,
-  chunkDigestForReading,
-  estimatePromptTokens,
-  hashDigest,
-  READER_WINDOW_TOKENS,
-  type AlreadyEncoded,
-  type FacetReader,
-} from '../src/facets.js';
-
-const FRAMING_OPENER = 'THIS IS DATA, NOT A TASK.';
-
-function digestOf(session: string, episodes: EpisodeDigest[]): SessionDigest {
-  return { session, project: '/Users/me/repo', date: '2026-07-01T00:00:00.000Z', episodes };
-}
-
-function bigEpisode(marker: number): EpisodeDigest {
-  return { intent: `${'a'.repeat(4000)} marker-${marker}`, actions: [] };
-}
-
-describe('chunkDigestForReading — small digests pass through untouched', () => {
-  it('returns exactly one chunk, the digest itself, when the whole prompt already fits the window', () => {
-    const d = digestOf('sess-small', [{ intent: 'a short ask', actions: [] }]);
-    const chunks = chunkDigestForReading(d, undefined, READER_WINDOW_TOKENS);
-    expect(chunks).toHaveLength(1);
-    expect(chunks[0]).toEqual(d);
-  });
-});
-
-describe('chunkDigestForReading — oversized digests are split, never one flat oversized prompt', () => {
-  it('splits into more than one chunk once the whole prompt exceeds the window', () => {
-    const first = bigEpisode(1);
-    const episodes = [first, bigEpisode(2), bigEpisode(3)];
-    const d = digestOf('sess-big', episodes);
-    const oneEpisodeTokens = estimatePromptTokens(buildFacetPrompt(digestOf('sess-big', [first])));
-    const maxTokens = oneEpisodeTokens + 20; // room for one episode's worth, not two
-
-    const chunks = chunkDigestForReading(d, undefined, maxTokens);
-
-    expect(chunks.length).toBeGreaterThan(1);
-  });
-
-  it('no individual chunk prompt exceeds the budget it was chunked against', () => {
-    const first = bigEpisode(1);
-    const episodes = [first, bigEpisode(2), bigEpisode(3)];
-    const d = digestOf('sess-big', episodes);
-    const oneEpisodeTokens = estimatePromptTokens(buildFacetPrompt(digestOf('sess-big', [first])));
-    const maxTokens = oneEpisodeTokens + 20;
-
-    const chunks = chunkDigestForReading(d, undefined, maxTokens);
-
-    for (const chunk of chunks) {
-      expect(estimatePromptTokens(buildFacetPrompt(chunk, undefined))).toBeLessThanOrEqual(maxTokens);
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('front-loads the full data-not-a-task framing and already-encoded block into EVERY chunk, not only the first', () => {
-    const first = bigEpisode(1);
-    const episodes = [first, bigEpisode(2), bigEpisode(3)];
-    const d = digestOf('sess-big', episodes);
-    const encoded: AlreadyEncoded = { instructions: ['never fix symptoms, fix root causes'], skills: [], loops: [] };
-    const oneEpisodeTokens = estimatePromptTokens(buildFacetPrompt(digestOf('sess-big', [first]), encoded));
-    const maxTokens = oneEpisodeTokens + 20;
-
-    const chunks = chunkDigestForReading(d, encoded, maxTokens);
-
-    expect(chunks.length).toBeGreaterThan(1);
-    for (const chunk of chunks) {
-      const prompt = buildFacetPrompt(chunk, encoded);
-      expect(prompt.startsWith(FRAMING_OPENER)).toBe(true);
-      expect(prompt).toContain('never fix symptoms, fix root causes');
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('never drops or duplicates episodes — concatenating every chunk reconstructs the original order exactly', () => {
-    const first = bigEpisode(1);
-    const episodes = [first, bigEpisode(2), bigEpisode(3), bigEpisode(4)];
-    const d = digestOf('sess-big', episodes);
-    const oneEpisodeTokens = estimatePromptTokens(buildFacetPrompt(digestOf('sess-big', [first])));
-
-    const chunks = chunkDigestForReading(d, undefined, oneEpisodeTokens + 20);
-
-    expect(chunks.flatMap((chunk) => chunk.episodes)).toEqual(episodes);
-  });
-
-  it('keeps session, project, and date identical across every chunk — only episodes are sliced', () => {
-    const first = bigEpisode(1);
-    const episodes = [first, bigEpisode(2), bigEpisode(3)];
-    const d = digestOf('sess-big', episodes);
-    const oneEpisodeTokens = estimatePromptTokens(buildFacetPrompt(digestOf('sess-big', [first])));
-
-    const chunks = chunkDigestForReading(d, undefined, oneEpisodeTokens + 20);
-
-    expect(chunks.length).toBeGreaterThan(1);
-    for (const chunk of chunks) {
-      expect(chunk.session).toBe(d.session);
-      expect(chunk.project).toBe(d.project);
-      expect(chunk.date).toBe(d.date);
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('a single episode that alone exceeds the budget still gets its own chunk rather than being dropped or split mid-episode', () => {
-    const huge: EpisodeDigest = { intent: 'z'.repeat(20000), actions: [] };
-    const d = digestOf('sess-huge', [huge]);
-
-    const chunks = chunkDigestForReading(d, undefined, 10); // an absurdly small budget
-
-    expect(chunks).toHaveLength(1);
-    expect(chunks[0]?.episodes).toEqual([huge]);
-  });
-});
-
-describe('buildFacetCache — chunks an oversized session and merges findings across all its chunks', () => {
-  it('calls the reader once per chunk, merges every chunk\'s findings under one entry keyed by the whole-digest hash', () => {
-    const episodes = Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, i) => ({ intent: `${'p'.repeat(4000)} ep-${i}`, actions: [] }));
-    const digest: SessionDigest = {
-      session: 'sess-oversized',
-      project: '/Users/me/repo',
-      date: '2026-07-01T00:00:00.000Z',
-      episodes,
-    };
-    expect(estimatePromptTokens(buildFacetPrompt(digest))).toBeGreaterThan(READER_WINDOW_TOKENS);
-
-    const prompts: string[] = [];
-    let call = 0;
-    const reader: FacetReader = (prompt) => {
-      prompts.push(prompt);
-      call += 1;
-      return JSON.stringify([{ category: 'friction', summary: `finding from chunk ${call}`, quotes: [] }]);
-    };
-
-    const result = buildFacetCache([digest], {}, reader);
-
-    // Never one flat oversized prompt: more than one call, and every call individually fits the window.
-    expect(result.readerCalls).toBeGreaterThan(1);
-    expect(prompts).toHaveLength(result.readerCalls);
-    for (const prompt of prompts) {
-      expect(prompt.startsWith(FRAMING_OPENER)).toBe(true);
-      expect(estimatePromptTokens(prompt)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(READER_WINDOW_TOKENS);
-    }
-
-    const entry = result.cache['sess-oversized'];
-    expect(entry).toBeDefined();
-    expect(entry?.digestHash).toBe(hashDigest(digest)); // hashed whole, unchunked — independent of the slicing
-    expect(entry?.findings).toHaveLength(result.readerCalls); // one finding per chunk, all merged in
-  });
-
-  // SYN-N4 (synN3-finding.md): the old all-or-nothing chunk merge made
-  // refusal probability COMPOUND with chunk count (one bad chunk among nine
-  // refused the whole mega-session, even though every OTHER chunk read
-  // cleanly). Per-chunk salvage replaces "one bad chunk drops everything"
-  // with "one bad chunk is dropped and counted; its siblings still cache".
-  it('a chunk that stays unreadable after its one SYN-N2 repair re-ask is dropped and counted — its siblings still cache', () => {
-    const episodes = Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, i) => ({ intent: `${'q'.repeat(4000)} ep-${i}`, actions: [] }));
-    const digest: SessionDigest = {
-      session: 'sess-partial-fail',
-      project: '/Users/me/repo',
-      date: '2026-07-01T00:00:00.000Z',
-      episodes,
-    };
-
-    // The 2nd chunk's failure AND its one SYN-N2 repair re-ask (call 3) both
-    // fail, so the session's repair budget is genuinely exhausted rather
-    // than the transient blip recovering — every OTHER chunk reads cleanly.
-    let call = 0;
-    const reader: FacetReader = () => {
-      call += 1;
-      if (call === 2 || call === 3) return 'not json at all';
-      return JSON.stringify([{ category: 'friction', summary: 'ok finding', quotes: [] }]);
-    };
-
-    const result = buildFacetCache([digest], {}, reader);
-
-    expect(call).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3); // more than one chunk was attempted, plus the repair re-ask
-    const entry = result.cache['sess-partial-fail'];
-    expect(entry).toBeDefined(); // salvaged, not dropped whole
-    expect(entry?.droppedChunks).toBe(1);
-    expect(entry?.findings.length).toBeGreaterThan(0); // the surviving chunks' findings still cache
-    expect(result.partialSessions).toBe(1);
-    expect(result.droppedChunks).toBe(1);
-    expect(result.refusedSessions).toBe(0);
-  });
-
-  it('when EVERY chunk fails, the session still refuses outright — nothing survives it to cache', () => {
-    const episodes = Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, i) => ({ intent: `${'w'.repeat(4000)} ep-${i}`, actions: [] }));
-    const digest: SessionDigest = {
-      session: 'sess-total-fail',
-      project: '/Users/me/repo',
-      date: '2026-07-01T00:00:00.000Z',
-      episodes,
-    };
-
-    const reader: FacetReader = () => 'not json at all, ever';
-
-    const result = buildFacetCache([digest], {}, reader);
-
-    expect(result.cache['sess-total-fail']).toBeUndefined();
-    expect(result.refusedSessions).toBe(1);
-    expect(result.partialSessions).toBe(0);
-  });
-
-  it('a digest that fits the window in one piece is unaffected — still exactly one reader call', () => {
-    const digest = digestOf('sess-small', [{ intent: 'a short ask', actions: [] }]);
-    let calls = 0;
-    const reader: FacetReader = () => {
-      calls += 1;
-      return '[]';
-    };
-
-    const result = buildFacetCache([digest], {}, reader);
-
-    expect(calls).toBe(1);
-    expect(result.readerCalls).toBe(1);
-    expect(result.cache['sess-small']).toBeDefined();
-  });
-});
diff --git a/spikes/loop-hole/tests/facet-negctrl.spec.ts b/spikes/loop-hole/tests/facet-negctrl.spec.ts
deleted file mode 100644

--- a/spikes/loop-hole/tests/facet-negctrl.spec.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,127 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * The negative control for the comprehension tier: a corpus of one-off,
- * preference-free sessions — every ask distinct, nothing stated twice, no
- * "always"/"never"/quality-bar language anywhere — must yield zero
- * recurring-instruction findings. This is the facets analogue of
- * tests/negctrl.spec.ts's guard against the whole product's failure mode: a
- * reader that "finds" standing instructions in ordinary one-off chatter
- * manufactures busywork instead of surfacing real signal.
- *
- * Unlike the cluster negative control, the facets tier has no deterministic
- * algorithm to interrogate — the reader is a model seam (`FacetReader`,
- * per facets.ts). So the zero has to be proven at the layer that IS
- * deterministic: the quote-honesty gate (`enforceQuoteHonesty`). A well-
- * behaved reader answering `[]` is not proof of anything — it is the second
- * test here that does the real work, feeding an over-eager reader that tries
- * to invent a recurring-instruction finding on this exact one-off corpus,
- * and showing the gate silences it because no such text ever appears
- * verbatim in any session. The third test proves that silence is the gate
- * doing its job, not blanket suppression: the identical reader, grounding
- * its finding in a real quote from the corpus, survives.
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { ClaudeCodeAdapter } from '../src/claude-adapter.js';
-import { runExtract } from '../src/extract.js';
-import { StateStore } from '../src/store.js';
-import { buildSessionDigests } from '../src/digest.js';
-import { buildFacetCache, enforceQuoteHonesty, type FacetReader } from '../src/facets.js';
-import { makeCorpus, userTurn } from './helpers.js';
-
-/** Five sessions, five unrelated one-off asks — nothing recurs, nothing
- * reads as a standing preference or quality bar. */
-const ONE_OFF_SESSIONS = [
-  { dir: '-Users-me-repoA', sessionId: 'sess-status', intent: 'check the deploy status', ts: '2026-06-10T09:00:00.000Z' },
-  { dir: '-Users-me-repoB', sessionId: 'sess-prs', intent: 'list open pull requests', ts: '2026-06-11T09:00:00.000Z' },
-  { dir: '-Users-me-repoC', sessionId: 'sess-parser', intent: 'explain how the parser handles block comments', ts: '2026-06-12T09:00:00.000Z' },
-  { dir: '-Users-me-repoD', sessionId: 'sess-rebase', intent: 'rebase this branch onto main', ts: '2026-06-13T09:00:00.000Z' },
-  { dir: '-Users-me-repoE', sessionId: 'sess-async', intent: 'convert this callback into an async function', ts: '2026-06-14T09:00:00.000Z' },
-] as const;
-
-async function buildOneOffDigests() {
-  const root = makeCorpus(
-    ONE_OFF_SESSIONS.map((s) => ({
-      dir: s.dir,
-      sessionId: s.sessionId,
-      records: [userTurn(s.intent, s.ts, `/Users/me/${s.dir.slice(1)}`)],
-    })),
-  );
-  const store = StateStore.empty();
-  await runExtract(new ClaudeCodeAdapter(root), store);
-  return buildSessionDigests(store);
-}
-
-describe('facet negative control', () => {
-  it('a corpus of one-off, preference-free sessions yields zero findings from a compliant reader', async () => {
-    const digests = await buildOneOffDigests();
-    expect(digests).toHaveLength(ONE_OFF_SESSIONS.length);
-
-    const reader: FacetReader = () => '[]';
-    const { cache, readerCalls } = buildFacetCache(digests, {}, reader);
-
-    expect(readerCalls).toBe(ONE_OFF_SESSIONS.length);
-    expect(Object.keys(cache)).toHaveLength(ONE_OFF_SESSIONS.length);
-    const totalFindings = Object.values(cache).reduce((n, s) => n + s.findings.length, 0);
-    expect(totalFindings).toBe(0);
-  });
-
-  it('quote honesty silences an over-eager reader that invents a recurring-instruction finding on the same corpus', async () => {
-    const digests = await buildOneOffDigests();
-
-    // A reader that claims the same "standing instruction" on every session,
-    // regardless of what that session actually contains — the failure mode
-    // this check guards against, since the words never appear verbatim in
-    // any of these one-off asks.
-    const reader: FacetReader = () =>
-      JSON.stringify([
-        {
-          category: 'instruction',
-          summary: 'always run the release checklist before shipping',
-          quotes: ['always run the release checklist before shipping'],
-        },
-      ]);
-
-    const { cache } = buildFacetCache(digests, {}, reader);
-
-    let totalFindings = 0;
-    let totalDropped = 0;
-    for (const digest of digests) {
-      const session = cache[digest.session];
-      expect(session).toBeDefined();
-      const honest = enforceQuoteHonesty(session!.findings, digest);
-      totalFindings += honest.findings.length;
-      totalDropped += honest.droppedFindings;
-    }
-
-    expect(totalFindings).toBe(0);
-    expect(totalDropped).toBe(ONE_OFF_SESSIONS.length);
-  });
-
-  it('the same gate keeps a finding once it is honestly grounded in the session\'s own text — the zero above is silence, not blanket suppression', async () => {
-    const digests = await buildOneOffDigests();
-    const rebase = ONE_OFF_SESSIONS.find((s) => s.sessionId === 'sess-rebase')!;
-
-    // Only the session whose real text the finding quotes gets one; every
-    // other session still reports nothing, exactly like the compliant reader.
-    const reader: FacetReader = (prompt) =>
-      prompt.includes(rebase.intent)
-        ? JSON.stringify([
-            { category: 'workflow-pattern', summary: 'rebases onto main before pushing', quotes: [rebase.intent] },
-          ])
-        : '[]';
-
-    const { cache } = buildFacetCache(digests, {}, reader);
-
-    let totalFindings = 0;
-    let totalDropped = 0;
-    for (const digest of digests) {
-      const session = cache[digest.session]!;
-      const honest = enforceQuoteHonesty(session.findings, digest);
-      totalFindings += honest.findings.length;
-      totalDropped += honest.droppedFindings;
-    }
-
-    expect(totalDropped).toBe(0);
-    expect(totalFindings).toBe(1);
-  });
-});

-/**
- * The reader prompt is the seam where the replication guide's two hardest
- * lessons live: (1) a reader that thinks the digest is a task will try to
- * act on it, so the DATA-not-a-task framing must be the first thing the
- * reader sees, every time; (2) a reader with no sense of what's already
- * standing (CLAUDE.md rules, skills, standing loops) re-derives the same
- * "is this new?" judgment the analyst tier would otherwise have to redo from
- * scratch for every finding. Handing the reader that already-encoded summary
- * lets findings arrive PRE-MARKED — "covered" or "novel" — instead of
- * leaving novelty as an unanswered question downstream.
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import type { SessionDigest } from '../src/digest.js';
-import {
-  buildFacetCache,
-  buildFacetPrompt,
-  parseFacetFindings,
-  type AlreadyEncoded,
-  type FacetReader,
-} from '../src/facets.js';
-
-const FRAMING_OPENER = 'THIS IS DATA, NOT A TASK.';
-
-function digest(session: string, intent: string): SessionDigest {
-  return { session, project: '/Users/me/repo', date: '2026-07-02T10:00:00.000Z', episodes: [{ intent, actions: [] }] };
-}
-
-const ENCODED: AlreadyEncoded = {
-  instructions: ['never fix symptoms, fix root causes', 'always write a failing test first'],
-  skills: ['tend-audit — verify a feature against real evidence', 'code-review — review a diff for bugs'],
-  loops: ['nightly-ci-watch — polls CI and notifies on red', 'weekly-digest — summarizes the week'],
-};
-
-describe('buildFacetPrompt — data-not-task framing opens every prompt', () => {
-  it('starts with the framing block when no already-encoded summary is given', () => {
-    const prompt = buildFacetPrompt(digest('sess-1', 'help me ship this'));
-    expect(prompt.startsWith(FRAMING_OPENER)).toBe(true);
-  });
-
-  it('still starts with the framing block when a rich already-encoded summary is given', () => {
-    const prompt = buildFacetPrompt(digest('sess-1', 'help me ship this'), ENCODED);
-    expect(prompt.startsWith(FRAMING_OPENER)).toBe(true);
-  });
-
-  it('the framing precedes the already-encoded summary, which precedes the session data', () => {
-    const prompt = buildFacetPrompt(digest('sess-1', 'help me ship this'), ENCODED);
-    const framingIndex = prompt.indexOf(FRAMING_OPENER);
-    const encodedIndex = prompt.indexOf('never fix symptoms, fix root causes');
-    const sessionIndex = prompt.indexOf('SESSION sess-1');
-    expect(framingIndex).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
-    expect(encodedIndex).toBeGreaterThan(framingIndex);
-    expect(sessionIndex).toBeGreaterThan(encodedIndex);
-  });
-});
-
-describe('buildFacetPrompt — carries the already-encoded summary', () => {
-  it('carries every standing instruction, skill, and loop verbatim', () => {
-    const prompt = buildFacetPrompt(digest('sess-1', 'an intent'), ENCODED);
-    for (const instruction of ENCODED.instructions) expect(prompt).toContain(instruction);
-    for (const skill of ENCODED.skills) expect(prompt).toContain(skill);
-    for (const loop of ENCODED.loops) expect(prompt).toContain(loop);
-  });
-
-  it('carries a partial summary (only skills known, no instructions or loops) without crashing', () => {
-    const partial: AlreadyEncoded = { instructions: [], skills: ['tend-audit — verify with evidence'], loops: [] };
-    const prompt = buildFacetPrompt(digest('sess-1', 'an intent'), partial);
-    expect(prompt).toContain('tend-audit — verify with evidence');
-  });
-
-  it('states plainly that everything is novel when the encoded summary is entirely empty', () => {
-    const empty: AlreadyEncoded = { instructions: [], skills: [], loops: [] };
-    const prompt = buildFacetPrompt(digest('sess-1', 'an intent'), empty);
-    expect(prompt.toLowerCase()).toContain('novel');
-  });
-
-  it('instructs the reader to mark each finding covered or novel against the summary', () => {
-    const prompt = buildFacetPrompt(digest('sess-1', 'an intent'), ENCODED);
-    expect(prompt).toContain('novelty');
-    expect(prompt).toContain('"covered"');
-    expect(prompt).toContain('"novel"');
-  });
-});
-
-describe('parseFacetFindings — novelty is an optional, validated field', () => {
-  it('accepts and preserves a "covered" finding', () => {
-    const raw = JSON.stringify([{ category: 'instruction', summary: 'reiterates a rule', quotes: ['x'], novelty: 'covered' }]);
-    const findings = parseFacetFindings(raw);
-    expect(findings?.[0]?.novelty).toBe('covered');
-  });
-
-  it('accepts and preserves a "novel" finding', () => {
-    const raw = JSON.stringify([{ category: 'friction', summary: 'a new pain point', quotes: ['x'], novelty: 'novel' }]);
-    const findings = parseFacetFindings(raw);
-    expect(findings?.[0]?.novelty).toBe('novel');
-  });
-
-  it('still accepts a finding that omits novelty entirely (older prompt, no encoded set) with the field absent', () => {

-    const findings = parseFacetFindings(raw);
-    expect(findings).toHaveLength(1);
-    expect(findings?.[0]?.novelty).toBeUndefined();
-  });
-
-  it('refuses the whole reading when novelty is present but not one of the two declared values', () => {
-    const raw = JSON.stringify([{ category: 'friction', summary: 'x', quotes: ['x'], novelty: 'maybe' }]);
-    expect(parseFacetFindings(raw)).toBeNull();
-  });
-});
-
-describe('buildFacetCache — wires the already-encoded summary into every reader call', () => {
-  it('every prompt the reader receives carries the encoded summary handed to buildFacetCache', () => {
-    const digests = [digest('sess-a', 'first session'), digest('sess-b', 'second session')];
-    const seenPrompts: string[] = [];
-    const reader: FacetReader = (prompt) => {
-      seenPrompts.push(prompt);
-      return '[]';
-    };
-
-    buildFacetCache(digests, {}, reader, ENCODED);
-
-    expect(seenPrompts).toHaveLength(2);
-    for (const prompt of seenPrompts) {
-      expect(prompt.startsWith(FRAMING_OPENER)).toBe(true);
-      expect(prompt).toContain('never fix symptoms, fix root causes');
-    }
-  });
-
-  it('a cache hit (unchanged digest) makes no reader call at all, so the encoded summary is irrelevant to it', () => {
-    const digests = [digest('sess-a', 'first session')];
-    const reader: FacetReader = () => '[]';
-    const first = buildFacetCache(digests, {}, reader, ENCODED);
-    let calls = 0;
-    const countingReader: FacetReader = (prompt) => {
-      calls += 1;
-      return reader(prompt);
-    };
-
-    buildFacetCache(digests, first.cache, countingReader, ENCODED);
-
-    expect(calls).toBe(0);
-  });
-});

-/**
- * Quote honesty — the application-layer gate the facets.ts doc comment defers
- * to explicitly ("quote honesty is a later tier's job"): a reader is never
- * trusted to police its own evidence, so every finding's quotes are checked
- * against its own session's digest before the finding is allowed to survive.
- * A finding that fails is dropped, fail-closed, and the drop is counted so a
- * caller can surface it rather than silently losing findings.
- */
-

- * already classifies WHY a session was refused (thrown reader vs. a schema
- * violation vs. unrepairable JSON) but only ever rolled that up into a bare
- * count. A run whose facets line reads "4 session(s) cached" out of 8 gives
- * no way to tell which 4 refused or why without re-running the reader by
- * hand. `onRefusal` surfaces one sanitized reason per refused session, and
- * run.ts's CLI summary renders one "<session-8chars>: <reason>" line per
- * refusal after the counts line — see facets.loop.html's Tried log,
- * 2026-07-24, and refusal-hygiene.spec.ts for the sibling tiers' convention
- * this follows (judge-error.ts's `sanitizeReason`, one line, capped).

-/**
- * Schema discipline — the reader is a raw-text seam, so its output is
- * adversarial input from the application's point of view. `parseFacetFindings`
- * must accept only entries that fully satisfy the finding schema (a known
- * category, a non-empty summary, a quotes array of strings); an individual
- * entry that fails is dropped and counted (SYN-N4 per-entry salvage,
- * synN3-finding.md) while its valid siblings survive — a top-level
- * structural failure (no array found, unparseable JSON, not an array at
- * all) still refuses the WHOLE reading, and so does an array where EVERY
- * entry fails (nothing left to salvage). `buildFacetCache` must carry a
- * genuine whole-reading refusal through without poisoning the cache: the
- * refused session gets no entry (so the next pass retries it), and —
- * critically — a malformed reading for one session in a batch must never
- * affect any sibling session's entry.
- */

-/**

- * analogue of fixtures.ts's turn-paraphrase groups: facet-proposals.spec.ts
- * (recall + negative control) and fixture-leak.spec.ts (the anti-Goodhart
- * lint, extended to scan this file too) both draw from this one home.
- *
- * Groups are synonym/paraphrase-anchored on purpose, same discipline as
- * fixtures.ts's own groups: no synonym table anywhere in src, semantics come
- * from the static distilled model (embed/static.ts). Measured against
- * potion-base-8M (2026-07-05, `.loop-scratch/probe-theme-fixtures.mjs`):
- * every within-group pair sits at 0.794-0.955, well clear of the 0.70
- * calibrated threshold (themes.ts's `THEME_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD`); the
- * adversarial cross-topic pair sits at 0.181.
- */
-
-/**
- * Same standing instruction, three independent phrasings, of three DIFFERENT
- * lengths (49 / 42 / 39 chars) — the 3-session repeated-instruction case a
- * theme is built to catch, AND the retitle fixture: a 2-session theme over
- * just the first two picks the 42-char phrase as its shortest-summary
- * `label` (themes.ts's `buildTheme`); adding the third session's shorter
- * (39-char) phrasing genuinely retitles the theme (a new, different
- * `themeKey`) while its quotes stay mostly the same — exactly the drift a
- * fingerprint-based suppression (memory.ts's `fingerprintTheme`) must survive.
- */
-export const INSTRUCTION_THEME_SUMMARIES = [
-  'always write a failing test before fixing any bug',
-  'write a failing test before fixing the bug',
-  'a failing test must precede any bug fix',
-] as const;
-
-/** Same standing correction, three independent phrasings — proves
- * `formForTheme('correction')` (themes.ts) licenses `standing-instruction`
- * once the SAME correction recurs across sessions, unlike typology.ts's
- * single-finding matrix (which prices, never justifies, a lone correction). */
-export const CORRECTION_THEME_SUMMARIES = [
-  'never use rm to delete files, use trash instead',
-  'never use rm for deletion, use trash instead',
-  'use trash instead of rm when deleting files',
-] as const;
-
-/** Same recurring pain, three independent phrasings, but `friction` — proves
- * a category with no legal form never themes no matter how many sessions or
- * how tightly the phrasings cluster (themes.ts's `formForTheme`). */
-export const FRICTION_REPEATED_SUMMARIES = [

-  'that integration test times out the ci pipeline once more',
-] as const;
-
-/** One real finding, present in exactly one session — never a theme
- * regardless of how clearly it names a recurring-sounding instruction. */
-export const SINGLE_SESSION_FINDING_SUMMARY = 'always squash commits before merging a pull request' as const;
-
-/** Two dissimilar, one-off asks — the negative-control corpus: nothing here
- * should ever connect into a theme (measured cross-pair similarity: 0.181). */
-export const ADVERSARIAL_UNRELATED_SUMMARIES = [
-  'explain how the parser tokenizes block comments',
-  'rebase this feature branch onto main',
-] as const;
-
-export const ALL_FACET_THEME_FIXTURE_SUMMARIES = [

-  ...ADVERSARIAL_UNRELATED_SUMMARIES,
-] as const;

--- a/spikes/loop-hole/tests/fixture-leak.spec.ts

@@ -1,66 +0,0 @@
-/**
- * The anti-Goodhart lint — mechanized, not cultural. A membership/similarity
- * check can always be "passed" by hardcoding the test's example inputs into
- * source (a synonym table, a phrase regex, a concept list); that is exactly
- * how this spike's first paraphrase check was gamed (docs/overfit-postmortem.md).
- * This spec makes that cheat structurally impossible for the current fixtures:
- * no fixture phrase — and no fragment of one longer than a single common word —
- * may appear anywhere in src/.
- *
- * The scan algorithm (function-word set, 2+-content-word windows) is
- * generalized in loop/src/core/fixture-leak.ts and shared with the first-party
- * `loop lint --fixtures` CLI, so the two can never drift apart
- * (docs/tend2-build-contract.md, "one source of truth per rule") — this spec
- * is a consumer of that module, not its own implementation.
- *
- * Rotating the fixtures (new phrasings, same behavior) keeps the defense
- * honest over time; each kind of fixture has its own single home (turns in
- * fixtures.ts, facet-theme summaries in facet-theme-fixtures.ts, synthesis
- * dossier prose in synthesis-fixtures.ts) — this spec unions every one of
- * them so a rotation, or a brand-new fixture file, still exercises the whole
- * defense at once. A new fixture file must be added to `FIXTURE_SOURCES`
- * below or this lint silently stops covering it.
- */
-
-import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { join, relative } from 'node:path';
-import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
-import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
-import { scanFixtureLeaks } from '../../../loop/src/core/fixture-leak.js';
-import { ALL_FIXTURE_TURNS } from './fixtures.js';
-import { ALL_FACET_THEME_FIXTURE_SUMMARIES } from './facet-theme-fixtures.js';
-import { ALL_SYNTHESIS_FIXTURE_STRINGS } from './synthesis-fixtures.js';
-
-/** Every fixture source this lint scans — one entry per fixture file. */
-const FIXTURE_SOURCES: readonly string[] = [
-  ...ALL_FIXTURE_TURNS,
-  ...ALL_FACET_THEME_FIXTURE_SUMMARIES,
-  ...ALL_SYNTHESIS_FIXTURE_STRINGS,
-];
-
-const SRC_DIR = join(fileURLToPath(new URL('.', import.meta.url)), '..', 'src');
-
-function sourceFiles(dir: string): string[] {
-  const out: string[] = [];
-  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir)) {
-    const path = join(dir, entry);
-    if (statSync(path).isDirectory()) out.push(...sourceFiles(path));
-    else if (path.endsWith('.ts')) out.push(path);
-  }
-  return out;
-}
-
-describe('fixture phrases must not leak into src/ (anti-Goodhart lint)', () => {
-  it('no fixture phrase or multi-word fragment appears in any source file', () => {
-    const files = sourceFiles(SRC_DIR);
-    expect(files.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
-    const leaks = scanFixtureLeaks(
-      FIXTURE_SOURCES,
-      files.map((path) => ({ path: relative(SRC_DIR, path), content: readFileSync(path, 'utf8') })),
-    );
-    expect(
-      leaks,
-      leaks.map((l) => `src leak: "${l.fragment}" (from fixture "${l.fixture}") found in ${l.file}`).join('\n'),
-    ).toEqual([]);
-  });
-});

-/**
- * Shared paraphrase fixtures — one home, three consumers: paraphrase.spec
- * (recall), concept-precision.spec (adversarial precision), and
- * fixture-leak.spec (the anti-Goodhart lint proving none of these strings
- * leaked into src/ as a hand-listed answer key).
- *
- * Groups are synonym-anchored on purpose: restart/reboot, clear/wipe,
- * deploy/ship/roll-out. That is what the deterministic semantic tier can
- * honestly join (measured 2026-07-02: within-group best edges ≥0.762 on
- * potion-base-8M). Zero-lexical-overlap asks and speech-act distinctions are
- * deliberately NOT here — they are the LLM merge tier's job.
- */
-
-/** Same ask, synonym verbs, no synonym table anywhere in src. */
-export const RESTART_TURNS = [
-  'restart the ingest worker',

-export const CLEANUP_TURNS = [

-
-/**
- * Same topic, different intent — lexically close to a group but NOT the ask.
- * Each pairs with the group it shadows; none may join that group's cluster.
- * (Measured similarities 0.166–0.635, all under the 0.70 threshold.)
- */
-export const ADVERSARIAL_TURNS = [
-  'document the restart flag in the readme',
-  'update the status field in the schema',
-  'the build cache design doc needs a diagram',
-  'write docs for the staging api',
-] as const;
-
-/**
- * A same-intent "checking on it" burst, phrased with zero lexical overlap
- * between asks — the polling.spec.ts contrast fixture proving cluster.ts's
- * embedding-threshold intent grouping fragments a real polling burst into
- * near-singletons (its documented blind spot), which is exactly the gap
- * polling.ts's timing-only detector closes.
- *
- * Note (episodes.loop.html c9, polling-sameness.spec.ts): these six phrases
- * also measure BELOW the real calibrated threshold pairwise on potion-base-8M
- * (0.12-0.44, max "done yet"<>"making progress" 0.440 vs the 0.70 floor) —
- * static.ts's own documented "Honest limits" for zero-lexical-overlap
- * pragmatic asks. They stay scoped to demonstrating cluster.ts's lexical
- * blind spot only; polling.ts's same-ask gate never asserts these six as a
- * "should cohere" case (its own fixtures are separate, synonym-anchored
- * paraphrases that do clear the threshold).
- */
-export const POLLING_BURST_TURNS = [
-  'any update',
-  'still running',
-  'status check',
-  'done yet',
-  'hows it going',
-  'making progress',
-] as const;
-
-/**
- * novelty.spec.ts's already-encoded set (a standing instruction, an
- * invocable skill, a standing loop) paired with a finding that only restates
- * each one — and one finding that restates none of them. Measured against
- * potion-base-8M (2026-07-02): each paired finding sits at 0.790-0.816
- * against its own entry (above cluster.ts's 0.70 calibrated threshold), and
- * the unrelated finding tops out at 0.407 against the closest entry —
- * comfortable margin on both sides of the threshold, same tier and same
- * calibration the paraphrase groups above already prove.
- */
-export const NOVELTY_ALREADY_ENCODED = {
-  instructions: ['never merge a pull request without a passing test suite'],
-  skills: ['runs a security review skill that checks pull requests for common vulnerabilities before merge'],
-  loops: ['a nightly watcher that checks deploy status and pings when a deploy fails'],

-export const NOVELTY_COVERED_FINDINGS = [

-  'the agent keeps manually checking pull requests for vulnerabilities instead of using the security review skill',
-  'the agent keeps checking whether the deploy status failed because nothing watches deploy status automatically',

-
-export const NOVELTY_NOVEL_FINDING =

-
-/**
- * polling.ts's same-ask gate fixtures (episodes.loop.html c9,
- * polling-sameness.spec.ts) — real ask text, unlike `POLLING_BURST_TURNS`
- * above (timing-only, no text ever reaches the detector). Measured on
- * potion-base-8M: `POLLING_OFFTOPIC_TURNS` never exceeds 0.292 pairwise (six
- * genuinely different technical questions, one connected component each);
- * `POLLING_CHECKIN_TURNS` forms exactly one connected component of all six
- * at the 0.70 threshold (pairwise range 0.50-0.88) — a real "is it done"
- * check-in, six distinct phrasings.

-export const POLLING_OFFTOPIC_TURNS = [

-export const ALL_FIXTURE_TURNS = [

-/**
- * form-decision.ts (design: propose.loop.html check c10, "classification
- * honesty") — two things must be true:
- *
- *  1. Per-form criteria are structural and total: `decideChainForm`,
- *     `decidePollingForm`, `decideCandidateForm`, and `decideThemeForm` each
- *     read only the SHAPE of their own evidence (trace outcome, timing,

- *     reason — `standing-loop` is reached only via `decideCandidateForm`'s
- *     own criterion, never as a shared fallthrough default.

- *     multi-form — proven END TO END through `runPipeline` (the one-command
- *     pipeline entry, never module calls in isolation), because that is
- *     exactly where the real defect lived: chains.ts and polling.ts were
- *     stamped-green at the module level but never wired into propose.ts or
- *     run.ts, so a real corpus containing a workaround chain or a polling
- *     burst could never emit anything but `standing-loop`. The at-a-glance
- *     counts a reader sees are asserted to match the SAME classified set the

-const BASE = Date.parse('2026-06-01T09:00:00.000Z');

-function action(template: string, outcome: EpisodeAction['outcome'], day: number, offsetMs: number): EpisodeAction {

-    project,

-    ts: new Date(askEpoch).toISOString(),

-describe('form-decision — structural per-form criteria (unit)', () => {

-describe('form-decision — mixed-shape corpus through the one-command pipeline', () => {
-  const outDirs: string[] = [];
-  afterEach(() => {
-    for (const dir of outDirs.splice(0)) rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
-  });
-
-  function outDir(): string {
-    const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'loop-hole-form-decision-'));
-    outDirs.push(dir);
-    return dir;
-  }
-
-  const MIN = 60_000;
-  function ts(day: number, offsetMin = 0): string {
-    return new Date(BASE + day * DAY + offsetMin * MIN).toISOString();
-  }
-
-  const INSTRUCTION_SUMMARY = 'always double check the release notes before shipping';
-  const FACET_SESSIONS = new Set(['facet-0', 'facet-1']);
-
-  /** Returns the same instruction finding for the two facet-theme sessions,
-   * and an honest empty read for every other session in the corpus — a
-   * FacetReader stub, never a mocked unit under test (facets.ts's own
-   * parse/quote-honesty gates still run for real on this reply). */
-  function instructionReader(): FacetReader {
-    return (prompt) => {
-      const match = /^SESSION (\S+) /m.exec(prompt);
-      const session = match?.[1];
-      if (session === undefined || !FACET_SESSIONS.has(session)) return '[]';
-      return JSON.stringify([{ category: 'instruction', summary: INSTRUCTION_SUMMARY, quotes: [INSTRUCTION_SUMMARY] }]);
-    };
-  }
-
-  /** One corpus carrying, deliberately, all five evidence shapes named in
-   * propose.loop.html's c10: a plain recurring request (intent-recurrence),
-   * a convergent multi-step procedure (procedure-chain), a workaround chain
-   * substituting for an absent command (workaround-chain), a polling burst
-   * (polling), and a repeated-instruction facet finding (theme). */
-  function mixedShapeCorpus(): string {
-    const dir = '-Users-me-repo';
-    const sessions = [];
-
-    // Shape: plain recurring request -> intent-recurrence -> standing-loop.
-    for (let d = 0; d < 4; d += 1) {
-      sessions.push({
-        dir,
-        sessionId: `intent-${d}`,
-        records: [userTurn('is the nightly ingest job still green?', ts(d, 0))],
-      });
-    }
-
-    // Shape: convergent multi-step procedure -> procedure-chain -> distilled-skill.
-    for (let d = 10; d < 13; d += 1) {
-      sessions.push({
-        dir,
-        sessionId: `skill-${d}`,
-        records: [
-          userTurn(`please run the release pipeline for build ${d}`, ts(d, 0)),
-          toolCallRecord(`m-skill-${d}-1`, `t-skill-${d}-1`, 'Bash', { command: 'npm run build' }, ts(d, 1), {}),
-          toolResult(`t-skill-${d}-1`, false, ts(d, 1), 'build ok'),
-          toolCallRecord(`m-skill-${d}-2`, `t-skill-${d}-2`, 'Bash', { command: 'npm test' }, ts(d, 2), {}),
-          toolResult(`t-skill-${d}-2`, false, ts(d, 2), 'tests ok'),
-        ],
-      });
-    }
-
-    // Shape: workaround chain substituting for an absent status API ->
-    // workaround-chain -> missing-tool. The status endpoint fails; the
-    // agent falls back to reading the raw deploy log by hand every time.
-    for (let d = 20; d < 23; d += 1) {
-      sessions.push({
-        dir,
-        sessionId: `workaround-${d}`,
-        records: [
-          userTurn(`did deploy ${d} finish`, ts(d, 0)),
-          toolCallRecord(`m-wa-${d}-1`, `t-wa-${d}-1`, 'Bash', { command: 'curl https://deploy-status.example.com/health' }, ts(d, 1), {}),
-          toolResult(`t-wa-${d}-1`, true, ts(d, 1), 'connection refused'),
-          toolCallRecord(`m-wa-${d}-2`, `t-wa-${d}-2`, 'Bash', { command: 'cat /var/log/deploy.log' }, ts(d, 2), {}),
-          toolResult(`t-wa-${d}-2`, false, ts(d, 2), 'deploy finished'),
-        ],
-      });
-    }
-
-    // Shape: polling burst -> polling -> push-loop. Six "is the migration
-    // done" phrasings (POLLING_CHECKIN_TURNS — same-ask under the real
-    // calibrated embedder, episodes.loop.html c9), 5 minutes apart, trivial
-    // (tool-free) traces.
-    sessions.push({
-      dir,
-      sessionId: 'polling-burst',
-      records: POLLING_CHECKIN_TURNS.map((text, i) => userTurn(text, ts(30, 10 + i * 5))),

-
-    // Shape: repeated-instruction facet finding -> instruction (themed
-    // across 2 sessions) -> standing-instruction. Only 2 occurrences —
-    // under cluster.ts's own intent-recurrence floor (3), so this can only
-    // ever surface through the facet-theme path, never double-counted as
-    // its own intent-recurrence candidate.
-    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) {
-      sessions.push({
-        dir,
-        sessionId: `facet-${i}`,
-        records: [userTurn(INSTRUCTION_SUMMARY, ts(40 + i, 0))],
-      });
-    }
-
-    return makeCorpus(sessions);
-  }
-
-  it('emits proposals spanning all five forms — an all-one-form result on this input is the failing test this check exists to catch', async () => {
-    const corpus = mixedShapeCorpus();
-    const out = outDir();
-
-    const result = await runPipeline({ corpusDir: corpus, outDir: out, facetReader: instructionReader() });
-
-    const forms = new Set(result.propose.proposals.map((p) => p.form));
-    expect(result.chains, 'chain detection must have run and surfaced both chains').toBe(2);
-    expect(result.pollingFamilies, 'polling detection must have run and surfaced the burst').toBe(1);
-    expect(
-      forms.size,
-      `expected >=4 distinct forms, got: ${[...forms].sort().join(', ')} (proposals: ${result.propose.proposals.map((p) => `${p.form}:${p.intent}`).join(' | ')})`,
-    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4);
-
-    // Every one of the five evidence shapes this corpus carries is
-    // represented by its own decided form — not merely "at least four
-    // distinct", but the five this fixture was built to prove.
-    expect(forms.has('standing-loop')).toBe(true);
-    expect(forms.has('distilled-skill')).toBe(true);
-    expect(forms.has('missing-tool')).toBe(true);
-    expect(forms.has('push-loop')).toBe(true);
-    expect(forms.has('standing-instruction')).toBe(true);

-
-  it('the briefing\'s at-a-glance counts match the SAME classified set the form-sections render — on real, not hand-built, proposals', async () => {
-    const corpus = mixedShapeCorpus();

-

-    // Independent recount straight from the pipeline's own emitted

-    const glanceHeadingIndex = payload.indexOf('## At a glance');
-    expect(glanceHeadingIndex).toBeGreaterThan(-1);

-
-    const SECTION_HEADINGS: readonly [ProposalForm, string][] = [
-      ['standing-instruction', '## Standing instructions'],
-      ['push-loop', '## Push loops'],
-      ['distilled-skill', '## Skills'],
-      ['standing-loop', '## Standing loops'],
-      ['missing-tool', '## Missing tools'],
-    ];
-
-    for (const [form, heading] of SECTION_HEADINGS) {
-      const count = recount.get(form) ?? 0;
-      // The glance line states this form's count as the exact

-      const expectedFragment = `${count} ${formSectionLabel(form, count)}`;
-      expect(glanceBlock, `at-a-glance must report "${expectedFragment}" for ${form}`).toContain(expectedFragment);
-
-      // And the section itself renders exactly `count` cards — counted by

-    }
-  });
-});

-/** Test helpers: build throwaway JSONL corpora on a temp dir, shaped exactly
- * like a real `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<sessionId>.jsonl` tree. */
-
-import { mkdtempSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync, appendFileSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { join } from 'node:path';
-import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-
-export interface SessionSpec {
-  /** Encoded project directory name, e.g. `-Users-me-repo`. */
-  dir: string;
-  sessionId: string;
-  /** One object per JSONL line, written verbatim. */
-  records: unknown[];
-}
-
-/** Create a fresh temp corpus root and write the given sessions into it. */
-export function makeCorpus(sessions: SessionSpec[]): string {
-  const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'loophole-corpus-'));
-  for (const session of sessions) {
-    const dir = join(root, session.dir);
-    mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
-    const body = session.records.map((r) => JSON.stringify(r)).join('\n') + '\n';
-    writeFileSync(join(dir, `${session.sessionId}.jsonl`), body);
-  }
-  return root;
-}
-
-/** Append one record to an existing session file, changing its byte length. */
-export function appendRecord(root: string, dir: string, sessionId: string, record: unknown): void {
-  appendFileSync(join(root, dir, `${sessionId}.jsonl`), JSON.stringify(record) + '\n');
-}
-
-/** A well-formed user prompt record. */
-export function userTurn(text: string, timestamp: string, cwd = '/Users/me/repo'): unknown {
-  return { type: 'user', timestamp, cwd, message: { role: 'user', content: text } };
-}
-
-/** An assistant record carrying one tool call (plus optional extra blocks). */
-export function toolCall(
-  name: string,
-  input: unknown,
-  timestamp: string,
-  extraBlocks: unknown[] = [],
-  cwd = '/Users/me/repo',
-): unknown {
-  return {
-    type: 'assistant',
-    timestamp,
-    cwd,
-    message: { role: 'assistant', content: [...extraBlocks, { type: 'tool_use', name, input }] },
-  };
-}
-
-/** The token-cost fields a real `usage` record carries (v2 fixtures). */
-export interface UsageInput {
-  input_tokens?: number;
-  output_tokens?: number;
-  cache_creation_input_tokens?: number;
-  cache_read_input_tokens?: number;
-}
-
-/** An assistant record carrying one tool call with a stable id (for a later
- * `toolResult` to resolve) and the completion's usage (v2 fixtures). */
-export function toolCallRecord(
-  messageId: string,
-  toolUseId: string,
-  name: string,
-  input: unknown,
-  timestamp: string,
-  usage: UsageInput,
-  cwd = '/Users/me/repo',
-): unknown {
-  return {
-    type: 'assistant',
-    timestamp,
-    cwd,
-    message: { role: 'assistant', id: messageId, content: [{ type: 'tool_use', id: toolUseId, name, input }], usage },
-  };
-}
-
-/** An assistant text-only record (no tool call) carrying usage (v2 fixtures) —
- * the shape a completion's text block takes when it shares a message id with
- * a sibling `toolCallRecord` line. */
-export function assistantText(
-  messageId: string,
-  text: string,
-  timestamp: string,
-  usage: UsageInput,
-  cwd = '/Users/me/repo',
-): unknown {
-  return {
-    type: 'assistant',
-    timestamp,
-    cwd,
-    message: { role: 'assistant', id: messageId, content: [{ type: 'text', text }], usage },
-  };
-}
-
-/** A user record carrying one tool_result block resolving the given tool_use
- * id (v2 fixtures). */
-export function toolResult(toolUseId: string, isError: boolean, timestamp: string, content: string, cwd = '/Users/me/repo'): unknown {
-  return {
-    type: 'user',
-    timestamp,
-    cwd,
-    message: { role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'tool_result', tool_use_id: toolUseId, is_error: isError, content }] },
-  };
-}
-
-/** A harness-injected task-notification record, shaped exactly like the
- * literal `<task-notification>...</task-notification>` block Claude Code
- * folds into a session as a "user" turn when a background task reports in —
- * no human typed this; it carries no genuine intent. */
-export function taskNotificationTurn(
-  taskId: string,
-  summary: string,
-  event: string,
-  timestamp: string,
-  cwd = '/Users/me/repo',
-): unknown {
-  const content = `<task-notification> <task-id>${taskId}</task-id> <summary>${summary}</summary> <event>${event}</event> </task-notification>`;
-  return { type: 'user', timestamp, cwd, message: { role: 'user', content } };
-}
-
-/** A Conductor queue-operation bookkeeping record — no `message` field at
- * all; the real shape carries the prompt text directly on `content`. */
-export function queueOperationTurn(content: string, timestamp: string, sessionId = 'sess'): unknown {
-  return { type: 'queue-operation', operation: 'enqueue', timestamp, sessionId, content };
-}
-
-/** A Conductor last-prompt snapshot record — no `message` field; carries the
- * prompt on `lastPrompt` and has no `timestamp` in the real shape either. */
-export function lastPromptTurn(lastPrompt: string, leafUuid: string, sessionId = 'sess'): unknown {
-  return { type: 'last-prompt', lastPrompt, leafUuid, sessionId };
-}
-
-/** A harness attachment record (e.g. a budget check-in) — no `message`
- * field; carries structured data on `attachment`. */
-export function attachmentTurn(timestamp: string, cwd = '/Users/me/repo', sessionId = 'sess'): unknown {
-  return {
-    type: 'attachment',
-    attachment: { type: 'budget_usd', used: 0, total: 1.5, remaining: 1.5 },
-    uuid: `uuid-att-${timestamp}`,
-    timestamp,
-    userType: 'external',
-    cwd,
-    sessionId,
-  };
-}

-/**
- * The negative control: a corpus of one-off, non-recurring activity must yield
- * ZERO proposals. This is the guard against the whole product's failure mode —
- * a detector that "finds" rituals in noise manufactures busywork instead of
- * surfacing real recurrence. A genuinely quiet corpus must stay silent.
- *
- * The corpus is deliberately not merely unique: it also contains templates that
- * repeat *twice* — just under the recurrence bar — so the test proves the
- * threshold does the work, not that nothing was seeded at all.
- */
-
-import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
-import { detectRecurrenceCandidates } from '../src/cluster.js';
-import { runPropose, LocalProposer } from '../src/propose.js';
-import { normalizeToolCall } from '../src/normalize.js';
-import type { ActionEvent, StoredState } from '../src/types.js';
-
-const DAY = 86_400_000;
-const START = Date.parse('2026-06-01T09:00:00Z');
-const NOW = Date.parse('2026-06-20T09:00:00Z');
-
-/**
- * A corpus that looks busy but recurs at nothing. Every tool template is either
- * a one-off or appears exactly twice (below the min-occurrence bar of 3); every
- * user turn is a distinct, unrelated request that no cluster of three can form.
- */
-function oneOffState(): StoredState {
-  const oneOffCommands = [
-    'lsof -i :8471',
-    'git status',
-    'ls -la src',
-    'cat README.md',
-    'echo hello',
-    'git log --oneline -5',
-    'wc -l package.json',
-    'head -20 CHANGELOG.md',
-  ];
-  // Two templates that recur exactly twice — just under the threshold of 3.
-  const twiceCommands = ['npm test', 'docker ps'];
-
-  const turns = [
-    'Rename the login button to Sign in',
-    'Explain how the parser handles block comments',
-    'Add a dark mode toggle to the settings page',
-    'Draft a changelog entry for the 2.1 release',
-    'Convert this callback into an async function',
-  ];
-
-  const events: ActionEvent[] = [];
-  let seq = 0;
-
-  oneOffCommands.forEach((command, i) => {
-    events.push(toolEvent('Bash', { command }, i, seq++));
-  });
-
-  // Each "twice" command fires on two different days — recurring, but not enough.
-  twiceCommands.forEach((command, i) => {
-    events.push(toolEvent('Bash', { command }, i, seq++));
-    events.push(toolEvent('Bash', { command }, i + 3, seq++));
-  });
-
-  // A single WebFetch and a single MCP call — distinct one-offs, not rituals.
-  events.push(toolEvent('WebFetch', { url: 'https://news.example.com/today' }, 1, seq++));
-  events.push(toolEvent('mcp__tilth__tilth_search', { query: 'parseComment' }, 2, seq++));
-
-  // Each user turn is asked exactly once, on its own day — no repeated intent.
-  turns.forEach((_text, i) => {
-    events.push(userEvent(i, i, seq++));
-  });
-
-  return { version: 1, watermark: {}, turns, events };
-}
-
-function toolEvent(tool: string, input: unknown, day: number, sequence: number): ActionEvent {
-  const epoch = START + day * DAY + sequence * 1000;
-  return {
-    kind: 'tool',
-    ts: new Date(epoch).toISOString(),
-    epoch,
-    project: '/Users/me/repo',
-    session: `session-${day}`,
-    tool,
-    template: normalizeToolCall(tool, input),
-  };
-}
-
-function userEvent(turn: number, day: number, sequence: number): ActionEvent {
-  const epoch = START + day * DAY + sequence * 1000;
-  return {
-    kind: 'user',
-    ts: new Date(epoch).toISOString(),
-    epoch,
-    project: '/Users/me/repo',
-    session: `session-${day}`,
-    turn,
-  };
-}
-
-describe('negative control', () => {
-  it('a corpus of one-off, non-recurring activity yields no candidates', async () => {

-/**
- * Corpus origin hygiene: a "user" record in a Claude Code transcript is not
- * automatically a genuine human ask. Two structural markers say otherwise —
- * `isSidechain: true` (the line belongs to a sub-agent's own transcript,
- * spawned by the Task tool, not the operator) and `userType` set to anything
- * other than `"external"` (the transcript's own label for a synthetic/
- * injected turn). Both are read off fields the real JSONL already carries;
- * neither is inferred from the turn's text.
- */
-
-import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
-import { ClaudeCodeAdapter } from '../src/claude-adapter.js';
-import { runExtract } from '../src/extract.js';
-import { StateStore } from '../src/store.js';
-import type { ActionEvent } from '../src/types.js';
-import { makeCorpus } from './helpers.js';
-
-const CWD = '/Users/me/repo';
-
-function userEvents(store: StateStore) {
-  return store.events.filter((e): e is Extract<ActionEvent, { kind: 'user' }> => e.kind === 'user');
-}
-
-/** A record shaped exactly like a real `~/.claude/projects/.../*.jsonl` line,
- * with the origin-marking fields real transcripts carry alongside `type`. */
-function rawUserRecord(text: string, timestamp: string, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}): unknown {
-  return {
-    parentUuid: null,
-    isSidechain: false,
-    userType: 'external',
-    cwd: CWD,
-    sessionId: 'sess-origin',
-    version: '2.1.0',
-    type: 'user',
-    message: { role: 'user', content: text },
-    uuid: 'uuid-' + timestamp,
-    timestamp,
-    ...extra,
-  };
-}
-
-describe('corpus origin hygiene', () => {
-  it('interns a genuine external, non-sidechain turn as intent', async () => {
-    const root = makeCorpus([
-      {
-        dir: '-Users-me-repo',

-        records: [rawUserRecord('please clean up the stale branches', '2026-07-01T09:00:00.000Z')],
-      },

-    const store = StateStore.empty();
-    await runExtract(new ClaudeCodeAdapter(root), store);
-
-    expect(userEvents(store)).toHaveLength(1);

-
-  it('never interns a sidechain record as an intent turn', async () => {
-    const root = makeCorpus([

-        dir: '-Users-me-repo',
-        sessionId: 'sess-origin',
-        records: [
-          rawUserRecord('genuine kickoff ask', '2026-07-01T09:00:00.000Z'),
-          // A sub-agent's own transcript line, folded into the parent session

-
-  it('never interns a non-external userType as an intent turn', async () => {
-    const root = makeCorpus([
-      {
-        dir: '-Users-me-repo',
-        sessionId: 'sess-origin',
-        records: [
-          rawUserRecord('genuine kickoff ask', '2026-07-01T09:00:00.000Z'),

-

-/**
- * Paraphrase recall at the semantic tier — differently-worded same-intent
- * instructions must cohere WITHOUT any hand-listed language in src (no
- * synonym tables, no phrase regexes, no concept lists; fixture-leak.spec
- * enforces that ban mechanically). The signal comes from the static distilled
- * embedding model, so the same behavior holds for phrasings and domains this
- * file never names — that is the difference between a product and an answer
- * key (docs/overfit-postmortem.md).
- *
- * Scope honesty: these groups are synonym-anchored (restart/reboot,
- * clear/wipe, deploy/ship/roll-out). Zero-lexical-overlap asks ("status?" vs
- * "how are things looking", measured 0.04–0.45) are beyond ANY cheap
- * embedding and belong to the LLM merge tier — pinning them here would only
- * invite the next lookup table.
- */
-
-import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
-import { detectRecurrenceCandidates } from '../src/cluster.js';
-import { StaticEmbeddingProvider, defaultModelDir } from '../src/embed/static.js';
-import { PARAPHRASE_GROUPS } from './fixtures.js';
-import type { ActionEvent, StoredState } from '../src/types.js';
-
-const DAY = 86_400_000;
-const START = Date.parse('2026-06-01T09:00:00Z');
-const NOW = Date.parse('2026-06-08T09:00:00Z');
-
-const ALL_TURNS = PARAPHRASE_GROUPS.flat();
-
-/** Six events per group across six days, cycling each group's phrasings. */
-function paraphraseState(): StoredState {
-  const events: ActionEvent[] = [];
-  let seq = 0;
-  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i += 1) {
-    let offset = 0;
-    for (const group of PARAPHRASE_GROUPS) {
-      events.push(userEvent(offset + (i % group.length), i, seq++));
-      offset += group.length;
-    }
-  }
-  return { version: 1, watermark: {}, turns: [...ALL_TURNS], events };
-}
-
-function userEvent(turn: number, day: number, sequence: number): ActionEvent {
-  const epoch = START + day * DAY + sequence * 1000;
-  return {
-    kind: 'user',
-    ts: new Date(epoch).toISOString(),
-    epoch,
-    project: '/Users/me/repo',
-    session: `session-${day}`,
-    turn,
-  };
-}
-
-describe('paraphrase recall (semantic tier)', () => {
-  it('collapses each synonym-anchored group into exactly one cluster', async () => {
-    const embedder = StaticEmbeddingProvider.load(defaultModelDir());
-    const candidates = await detectRecurrenceCandidates(paraphraseState(), { now: NOW, embedder });
-    const intents = candidates.filter((candidate) => candidate.kind === 'intent');
-
-    // Exactly one cluster per group: none fragmented, none merged with a neighbor.
-    expect(intents).toHaveLength(PARAPHRASE_GROUPS.length);
-
-    for (const group of PARAPHRASE_GROUPS) {
-      const cluster = intents.find((candidate) =>
-        group.some((turn) => candidate.provenance.some((line) => line.includes(turn))),
-      );
-      expect(cluster, `no cluster found for group "${group[0]}"`).toBeDefined();
-      // Every phrasing of the group landed in this same cluster's provenance.
-      for (const turn of group) {
-        expect(
-          cluster!.provenance.some((line) => line.includes(turn)),
-          `"${turn}" missing from its group's cluster`,
-        ).toBe(true);
-      }
-      // All six events for the group are accounted for by this one cluster.
-      expect(cluster!.eventCount).toBe(6);
-    }
-  });
-});

-/**
- * The whole-pipeline check: one command runs extract → cluster → propose →
- * report over a corpus dir and writes the briefing + draft pages to an out dir.
- *
- * Two lenses, both driving the real modules with no mock of the unit under test:
- *  - the *command form* — spawn `bun src/run.ts <corpus> <out>` exactly as the
- *    loop file advertises, and prove the files it leaves behind are real loop
- *    pages (parse + lint clean, every check open) and a briefing that links them;
- *  - the *pipeline contract* — call `runPipeline` in-process to assert the
- *    honesty invariants that must survive end-to-end: every emitted citation
- *    exists verbatim in the corpus, and a second pass over an unchanged corpus
- *    is a no-op (the incremental watermark the design promises).
- */
-
-import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
-import { existsSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
-import { homedir, tmpdir } from 'node:os';
-import { join } from 'node:path';
-import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
-import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
-import { extractPayload } from '../../../loop/src/core/extract.js';
-import { lint } from '../../../loop/src/core/lint.js';
-import { parse } from '../../../loop/src/core/parse.js';
-import { ClaudeCodeAdapter } from '../src/claude-adapter.js';
-import { corpusStrings } from '../src/propose.js';
-import { StateStore } from '../src/store.js';
-import { runExtract } from '../src/extract.js';
-import { runPipeline } from '../src/run.js';
-import { makeCorpus, toolCall, userTurn } from './helpers.js';
-
-const RUN_TS = fileURLToPath(new URL('../src/run.ts', import.meta.url));
-const DAY = 86_400_000;
-const START = Date.parse('2026-06-01T09:00:00Z');
-
-/** A corpus with two clearly recurring rituals plus a repeated user request. */
-function ritualCorpus(): string {
-  const sessions = [];
-  for (let day = 0; day < 5; day += 1) {
-    const at = (offset: number) => new Date(START + day * DAY + offset * 60_000).toISOString();
-    sessions.push({
-      dir: '-Users-me-repo',
-      sessionId: `session-${day}`,
-      records: [
-        userTurn('What changed in competitor pricing this week?', at(0)),
-        toolCall('Bash', { command: `lsof -i :${8471 + day}` }, at(1)),
-        toolCall('WebFetch', { url: `https://rival.example.com/pricing?d=${day}` }, at(2)),
-        toolCall('Bash', { command: `git status` }, at(3)),
-      ],
-    });
-  }
-  return makeCorpus(sessions);
-}
-
-function outDir(): string {
-  return mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'loophole-pipeline-out-'));
-}
-
-/** Locate the bun runtime the loop file's command relies on. */
-function resolveBun(): string {
-  const candidates = [
-    process.env.BUN_PATH,

-/**

- * unrelated follow-up questions) fired inside one short-interval, trivial-
- * trace burst was indistinguishable from a real "checking on it" burst —
- * both cleared `runsWithinSession`'s timing gate identically.
- *
- * The fix reuses cluster.ts's own embedding seam (never a second embedding
- * stance, never a phrase list): within a timing-qualified run, member asks
- * must also cohere as one connected component at the SAME calibrated
- * threshold `detectRecurrenceCandidates` already uses. Timing narrows to
- * candidate runs; sameness decides real membership within them.
- *
- * These fixtures are calibrated against the real bundled model
- * (potion-base-8M, measured in `.loop-scratch/calibrate-sameness.mjs`, not
- * committed) — own paraphrases, not `POLLING_BURST_TURNS` (see the note on
- * that fixture in fixtures.ts: those six phrases are pragmatically terse
- * enough to sit BELOW this same threshold too, 0.12-0.44, so they stay
- * scoped to demonstrating cluster.ts's lexical blind spot, never asserted
- * here as a "should cohere" case).
- */

-/**
- * Polling collapse — a same-intent, short-interval "checking on it" burst
- * fired while background work is still running must surface as ONE polling
- * shape (a push-loop candidate), never as N separate intent clusters. The
- * contrast case below proves the risk is real: cluster.ts's embedding-based
- * intent grouping is a documented blind spot for zero-lexical-overlap
- * phrasings (embed/static.ts's "Honest limits"), so a real burst phrased a
- * different way each time fragments into near-singletons and never clears
- * the recurrence floor. polling.ts closes that gap by joining on timing and
- * trace shape alone, never on what the ask says.
- */
-
-import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
-import { detectPollingFamilies } from '../src/polling.js';
-import type { Episode, EpisodeAction } from '../src/episodes.js';
-import { detectRecurrenceCandidates } from '../src/cluster.js';
-import type { ActionEvent, StoredState } from '../src/types.js';
-import { POLLING_BURST_TURNS } from './fixtures.js';
-
-const BASE = Date.parse('2026-06-01T09:00:00.000Z');
-const MIN = 60_000;
-
-function action(template: string, day: number, offsetMs: number): EpisodeAction {
-  const epoch = BASE + day * 86_400_000 + offsetMs;
-  return { tool: template.split('(')[0] ?? template, template, outcome: 'ok', ts: new Date(epoch).toISOString(), epoch };
-}
-
-/** A quick "checking on it" ask: no substantive trace, resolves instantly. */
-function quickAsk(session: string, project: string, turn: number, offsetMs: number): Episode {
-  const epoch = BASE + offsetMs;
-  return {
-    session,
-    project,
-    turn,
-    ts: new Date(epoch).toISOString(),
-    epoch,
-    actions: [],
-    durationMs: 0,
-    tokens: { input: 0, output: 0 },
-    resolution: 'resolved',
-  };
-}
-
-/** A substantive ask: real work, real duration — never mistaken for a poll. */
-function substantiveAsk(session: string, project: string, turn: number, offsetMs: number, actions: EpisodeAction[]): Episode {
-  const epoch = BASE + offsetMs;
-  const last = actions[actions.length - 1];
-  return {
-    session,
-    project,
-    turn,
-    ts: new Date(epoch).toISOString(),
-    epoch,
-    actions,
-    durationMs: last === undefined ? 0 : last.epoch - epoch,
-    tokens: { input: 0, output: 0 },
-    resolution: 'resolved',
-  };
-}
-
-describe('polling recall', () => {

-
-    // The burst: six "checking on it" asks, 5 minutes apart, 25 minutes total —
-    // trivial traces, phrased however you like (this module reads none of it).

-      quickAsk(session, project, i + 1, 10 * MIN + i * 5 * MIN),
-    );
-
-    // The state transition that ends the polling: real work again (a

-

-      quickAsk('sess-other', '/Users/me/repoB', 9, 3 * 86_400_000 + 3 * 3_600_000),

-describe('polling precision: distinct bursts stay distinct', () => {
-  it('two separate polling bursts in one session, split by real work, yield two families — not one merged run', async () => {
-    const session = 'sess-two-jobs';
-    const project = '/Users/me/repoG';

deleted file mode 100644
